You can make a reservation online through Epic Mountain Rentals or directly through participating resort rental pages. Booking online is the easiest way to browse available gear options, select your preferred package, and secure your reservation in advance. Booking online in advance helps ensure availability, faster pickup, and access to any applicable discounts. How far in advance do I need to book my reservation? You can book your reservation at any time before your arrival, but we recommend reserving at least a few days in advance to ensure the best selection and availability. If you make a reservation less than 2 calendar days in advance of your arrival, gear will only be available for pick up at a store location and delivery will not be available. Gear selection is subject to gear availability at time of booking. We recommend booking gear for a minimum of 48 hours in advance to ensure the best overall experience and selection. What is your refund policy? Full refunds are available if canceled at least 24 hours in advance by calling us at 970-754-0033 or toll free at 1-800-200-9990. For cancellations inside of 24 hours that have not yet been fulfilled, refunds are available minus a restocking fee by calling us at 970-754-0033. Restocking fees are applicable to each package on the reservation. No shows are non-refundable. What if I return my skis early? You'll be refunded for unused full days minus a restocking fee. Returns after 9 AM are charged for that day. Who can I contact for help with a reservation? We can be contacted at 970-754-0033 or toll free at 1-800-200-9990. What if I need to cancel or change my reservation? Reservations may be canceled up to 24 hours before 8:00 am local time on the first day of your reservation for a full refund, and can be done online. For cancellations inside of 24 hours that have not yet been fulfilled, refunds are available minus a restocking fee. Restocking fees are applicable to each package on the reservation. No shows are non-refundable. Please call 970-754-0033 (or toll free at 1-800-200-9990) so we can assist you. We cannot cancel reservations by email or in person. Rescheduled reservations will be subject to inventory available of their new date, which may be different from your original reservation. How do I determine my skier type? Your skier type reflects your ability level and is typically classified as Type I (Beginner), Type II (Intermediate), or Type III (Advanced). It helps rental shops and technicians set your equipment correctly for safety and performance. Bike Rentals FAQ What is your refund policy? You can cancel up to 24 hours before your reservation for a full refund. Call us to make a change at 970-754-0033 for U.S. reservations or 800-766-0449 for Canadian reservations. If you can, have your confirmation number handy. Can I change my rental dates after I book? Yes. We understand plans change. We're happy to modify your reservation up to 24 hours in advance. Call us to make a change at 970-754-0033 for U.S. reservations or 800-766-0449 for Canadian reservations. If you can, have your confirmation number handy. Do you rent helmets? Absolutely. For your safety, all rentals include a helmet. We have adult and kids sizes available for every bike rental. What should I wear? We recommend wearing layers you can remove as needed and packing rain gear or wind protection. Consider bringing a backpack to store any extra items and a water bottle if you're cruising around town. Do you rent kids' bikes? Most locations have kids bikes available; sizes may be limited. What time can I pick up my half-day morning rental? Generally, half-day morning rentals are 10 AM 2 PM. This can vary by location, so confirm the exact times with your rental shop. What time can I pick up my half-day afternoon rental? Generally, half-day afternoon rentals are 2 PM 6 PM. This can vary by location, so confirm the exact times with your rental shop. Do you rent protective gear aside from helmets? Yes, for certain bike park and downhill bike rentals. These options include knee and elbow pads and body armor and can be selected in Step 3. Are there mountain bike trails for beginners? Most locations have mountain bike trails for beginners. Ask a team member for their trail recommendations based on your experience and comfort level. What happens if I get a flat tire? Safety first. Dismount and move your bike to a safe place. Then, call the rental shop. We'll help fix your flat and get you back out there. We recommend bringing a cell phone and adding the shop's number before you begin your ride. What times of the year do you rent bikes? Typically, May through August, but this can vary by weather conditions and resort. For your safety, some trails may be closed early in the season. Can we bike on the ski resort property? At most resorts, yes. Check current conditions and for any trail restrictions before your visit. Several resorts also have chairlifts that carry you and your bike up the mountain so you can ride down single-track trails or ski runs. Resorts like Whistler Blackcomb, Keystone, Northstar and more have bike parks. My child is coming with a group, but I will not accompany him or her. Is there a liability waiver I need to sign? We require a parent or legal guardian to sign a release of liability on behalf of an unaccompanied person younger than 18 years old. Download, complete and print this waiver and send it with your child. They will not be able to participate if the release is not signed. No exceptions. Are there weight limits on your bikes? Yes, each manufacturer will set a maximum rider weight to ensure the safety of riders please contact your preferred rental store directly to confirm the maximum rider weight for the bike you're interested in renting. Ski & Snowboard FAQ RESERVATIONS & CANCELLATIONS Where do I make a reservation? You can make a reservation online through Epic Mountain Rentals or directly through participating resort rental pages. Booking online is the easiest way to browse available gear options, select your preferred package, and secure your reservation in advance. Booking online in advance helps ensure availability, faster pickup, and access to any applicable discounts. How far in advance do I need to book my reservation? You can book your reservation at any time before your arrival, but we recommend reserving at least a few days in advance to ensure the best selection and availability. If you make a reservation less than 2 calendar days in advance of your arrival, gear will only be available for pick up at a store location and delivery will not be available. Gear selection is subject to gear availability at time of booking. We recommend booking gear for a minimum of 48 hours in advance to ensure the best overall experience and selection. What is your refund policy? Full refunds are available if canceled at least 24 hours in advance by calling us at 970-754-0033 or toll free at 1-800-200-9990. For cancellations inside of 24 hours that have not yet been fulfilled, refunds are available minus a restocking fee by calling us at 970-754-0033. Restocking fees are applicable to each package on the reservation. No shows are non-refundable. What if I return my skis early? You'll be refunded for unused full days minus a restocking fee. Returns after 9 AM are charged for that day. Who can I contact for help with a reservation? We can be contacted at 970-754-0033 or toll free at 1-800-200-9990. What if I need to cancel or change my reservation? For cancellations inside of 24 hours that have not yet been fulfilled, refunds are available minus a restocking fee. Restocking fees are applicable to each package on the reservation. pages.text: Kayak Tahoe - kayak and stand up paddleboard rentals at Lake Tahoe Hit enter to search or ESC to close Rentals Locations Links Weather permitting Kayak Tahoe is open daily. Operating hours are 10am - 5pm with the last rentals leaving at 4pm and returning by 5pm. Please be to the location of your choosing no later than 3:45pm for last rentals. Kayak and Standup Paddleboard Rentals Rental Rate Locations Restrictions There is no better way to experience the incredible beauty of Lake Tahoe than from the lake itself. We provide a range of open-deck (sit-on-top) kayaks and paddleboards that are enjoyed by beginners and experts alike. Rental Rates Single Kayak $40.00 1 hour $50.00 2 hours $110.00 Full Day Double Kayak $55.00 1 hour $85.00 2 hours $130.00 Full Day Paddleboard $40.00 1 hour $50.00 2 hours $110.00 Full Day Our Locations Rental Information General Information All rentals for all locations are first-come, first-served and no reservations are available over the phone or on-line. Parking can be an issue so please try and arrive early. Open-deck kayak rentals include life vests, paddles, backrests, and basic instruction. Paddleboard rentals include paddle, leash, life vest and basic instruction. Dry bags are also available at an extra charge. Consumption of alcohol is not permitted at anytime while renting from or interacting with Kayak Tahoe. Cash and Credit Cards only accepted at all locations. Due to high use, reception can be poor. Cash will expedite the rental process. Please bring an ID with you when you come to rent come to rent. Minors MINIMUM age for participants is 4 years old and the participant must weigh over 30 lbs. Minors ages 13 to 17 MUST be watched at all times by a parent/guardian 18 years of age or older. The parent/guardian MUST always stay within earshot of the minor(s). Minors 12 and under MUST be accompanied on the water by a parent/guardian 18 years of age or older. This can be on single kayaks, paddleboards or double kayaks. The minor and parent/guardian can be on a Paddleboard together if the minor is under 90 lbs. Two participants on the same Paddleboard will NOT be allowed to paddle to Fannette Island (Emerald Bay). Participant MUST be over the age of 15 to take their own vessel (kayak or Paddleboard) to Fannette Island (Emerald Bay). Attention Group Leaders Print out a copy of our Liability Form and Rental Contract . Print one copy of the Rental Contract (this is usually filled out by the credit card holder), and then as many Liability Releases as you need for your group (One per person unless you are family). Staple them together for us and you will be on the water faster! Please note this is not a ticket to the front of the waiting line, you will still need to wait in before we can complete the rental process. Have Fun! Additional Things to Remember You will get wet so please wear suitable clothing. Preferably have footwear that can get wet. Please come prepared to rent before you sign up at our table. i.e. Make sure everyone in the group has gone to the bathroom, applied sunscreen, have their food and water and are ready to receive instruction. Children older than 4 years old and under 50lbs can be a third person on a double kayak. Remember to have FUN! Cold Water Consideration Families with small children and anyone affected by cold water should be cautious and realistic about their swimming ability and experience level. We have provided some links below for two of the most common cold water emergencies. Thank you and we hope to see you on the water soon. Cold Water Information Links: Cold Water Shock – National Center for Cold Water Safety Cold Water Shock – National Weather Service Cold Water Shock – SouthTahoeNow.com news article Hypothermia About us 30 years in operation and counting, we love to paddle, and we love to get people on the water. Customer safety and fun are our priorities, come on down and experience it for yourself. Normally the waves only get half this size on the Lake… Phone: 530-544-2011 Email: contactus@kayaktahoe.com 2026 Kayak Tahoe. Rentals Locations Links

What We Offer Nevada Adventure Rentals is the company to trust if you are planning to go rock climbing in Joshua Tree National Park or go backpacking in the Sierra Nevada mountains. You can choose from one of our custom adventure tours or design your own a la carte adventure with help from our team. No matter how prepared you are for your excursion, you can rely on us to provide you with the equipment and guidance you require to have a safe and exciting trip. Learn More Our Story For more than 30 years, Barry Durbin spent his time doing what he loves—camping, backpacking, climbing, skiing, and motorcycle touring. He then decided to start Nevada Adventure Rentals to support others who want to pursue adventure and live each day like it’s their last. During his many adventures, Barry realized that riding to his outdoor activities was so much more fun than driving to his destination. He believes that driving a car is like watching a movie through the windshield, but riding a motorcycle is like being in the movie, where you can experience all the good and bad encounters that come with the trip. Our team has adopted this belief, which is why we strive to provide our clients with services that allow them to experience “backpacking on a motorcycle.” Connect With Our Team Reach out to us today to learn more about our motorcycle and outdoor equipment rentals. We will be more than happy to address any of your questions or concerns. Our team looks forward to hearing from you! Call for details 530-562-7827 Book Now Browse Our Boats Please review our policies If You Are Visiting From Out Of Town this is important You must be 21 or older to rent. Our rentals operate as bareboat charters on a federally regulated, USCG-patrolled lake. This means: We offer trip protection ($49-$99) that will ensure you can receive a refund if we make a weather-related safety cancellation on the day-of. Trip protection also allows you to receive a monetary refund if you cancel your rental for any reason up to 48 hours from the date of departure. If you do not purchase trip protection we do not offer refunds within 14 days of the reservation date, no exceptions. The non-refundable 6% booking fee is not included in any refunds, full or partial. Without trip protection, rescheduling/holding a credit makes you ineligible for a monetary refund. Lake Tahoe’s weather is difficult to forecast and can be severe in its sudden changes. Because strong winds and thunderstorms are common, we strongly recommend renters keep a day open in their trip so they can accommodate any changes to their plans. We will do our best to give you as much of a heads up as possible if we see weather in the forecast that could affect your reservation day or time. We want to ensure you get the best experience possible out on the lake and appreciate your flexibility in planning that allows us to do so! Bareboat Charter: You rent and are responsible for the boat. Captain/crew, insurance, and fuel are not included. You must provide a valid driver’s license with a name matching that of the card on file at check-in. You may hire a captain through or outside of NLTBR, or drive yourself. Captains are not responsible for the vessel. Preview Our Boats We offer complimentary coolers and ice upon request as well as tubes on select rentals to enhance your experience. Max Capacity: 2 Starting at $179 Book Now Click “ Book Now ” or call 530-562-7827 to book today! Pricing At North Lake Tahoe Boat Rental, we believe everyone should be able to enjoy the spectacular beauty of Lake Tahoe. Our affordable pricing ensures you get a reliable, high-quality Lake Tahoe boat rental experience with no hidden fees. We have only the newest boats, ensuring a safe and reliable adventure—you won’t find yourself stranded on an outdated 2001 Sea Ray. We offer complimentary coolers and ice upon request as well as tubes on select rentals to enhance your experience. Just check the box when booking and we will have it ready for you upon your arrival! Please keep in mind that there is a nonrefundable 6% booking fee for all reservations. Fuel Costs on Lake Tahoe Our boat rentals operate as bareboat charters, meaning fuel and captains are not included. We fill up each boat before and after your rental so that you only pay for what you use. Fuel will be charged to the card on file after your rental generally within 24 hours, but this is subject to weather conditions and gas dock hours. Fuel is currently $10.59/gal at North Tahoe Marina. Half-day rentals average 10-15 gallons while full days average 15-30 gallons. THIS IS NOT A QUOTE, only an estimate for your budgeting. Fuel consumption varies based on activities, speed, engine off time and other variables. Adding a Captain If you’d prefer a captain to handle the driving, you can hire one through or outside of NLTBR. Our captain’s fee is $50/hour. For half-day rentals (3 ½ hours) this equates to $175 and for full-day rentals (7 hours) it is $350. Typical tip is $100 for a half day and $200 for a full day. With a captain, your rental can dock, anchor, go to an on-shore restaurant, and will have a designated driver. If you would like to add one to your reservation, please call or email us . Book your Lake Tahoe Boat Rentals and make the most of your Tahoe adventure at a price that fits your budget! We rent the highest quality sit-on-top kayaks on the market. Our rental kayaks are extremely stable, well-maintained, and great for both beginner and experienced kayakers. Lakefront kayak rentals are available in Kings Beach, California at Secline Beach. Perception Tribe Sit-On-Top Kayaks Available in 9.5 and 11.5-foot single kayaks and a 13.5-foot double kayak. Super versatile, ultra-stable, yet quick and playful. Excellent for any kayaking ability level. Adjustable seatback - for superior support and infinite recline positions. Comfortable padded seat keeps you on the water longer. Molded footrests accommodate paddlers of multiple sizes. Large open storage areas in front and rear with bungee lashing to secure your gear. Scupper holes provide drainage while still allowing your boat to remain buoyant. Rigid side carry handles for easy transport and lockable storage. Front and rear toggle handles. Added jump seat on the 13.5’ double kayak provides the perfect perch for a child. KAYAKING FAQs HOW MUCH DOES IT COST TO RENT A KAYAK? Please visit our Rates page for all kayak rental pricing information. ARE KAYAKS SAFE? Kayaking on Lake Tahoe is safe for people of all skill levels, including beginners. We rent high-quality, stable equipment that’s well maintained, and well-equipped for kayaking on Lake Tahoe. For more information regarding safety, rules, and guidelines, visit our Rules and Guidelines Page. DO YOU OFFER CLEAR KAYAK RENTALS? We do not offer clear kayak rentals. We strongly believe that clear kayaks are not safe for variable water conditions such as Lake Tahoe due to stability issues, less durable materials, and poor handling in choppy conditions. They can also be less visible to other boaters, increasing the risk of collisions. Furthermore, clear kayaks have limited buoyancy, significantly raising the risk of capsizing. Sit-on-top kayaks (what we rent), in contrast, offer better stability, buoyancy, and maneuverability, making them more suitable for beginners and safer for navigating rough waters. Additionally, our sit-on-top kayaks have reinforced structures and higher weight capacities, ensuring a safer experience in challenging conditions. DO I NEED TO WEAR A LIFE JACKET WHILE KAYAKING ON LAKE TAHOE? Anyone under 13 years old will be required to wear a lifejacket, and it’s highly recommended for everyone else. But don’t worry, we have life jackets in all sizes that are free to use with your rental. CAN KIDS AND DOGS RIDE IN YOUR KAYAK RENTALS? Kids are absolutely welcome in our kayak rentals. Unfortunately, because our lakefront kayak rentals are located at a beach that is not dog friendly, we no longer allow dogs to accompany you on your kayak. DO I NEED TO MAKE A RESERVATION TO RENT A KAYAK? Yes, kayak rental reservations are required! We tend to sell out fast, especially on the weekends. We offer lakefront kayak rentals in Kings Beach, California and delivery almost anywhere in North Lake Tahoe for multi-day reservations. To book a kayak rental reservation now, click here. WHAT IS THE BEST TIME OF DAY TO GO KAYAKING ON LAKE TAHOE? Although it varies day-to-day, typically the best time of day to go kayaking on Lake Tahoe is sometime in the morning as there is usually very little wind, and fewer boats on the lake than mid-day or in the afternoon. WHAT SHOULD I BRING WHILE KAYAKING ON LAKE TAHOE? At North Tahoe Paddle we provide lifejackets and paddles, but there are a few additional things we recommend taking with you while kayaking on Lake Tahoe. Sunscreen, water, and a hat to shade your face and eyes from the sun are all highly recommended. We offer a wide selection of both inflatable and hard stand up paddle boards that are great for all ages, sizes, and skill levels. Stand up paddle board rentals are available at our lakefront rental location in Kings Beach, California at Secline Beach. Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Boards Available in 10’6” size, with weight capacities of up to 400 lbs. Perform great in all water conditions. Great for all ages, sizes, and skill levels. Lightweight - weighing less than 30 lbs. Super-portable - when deflated, the boards (along with all the accessories) fit inside a backpack-style carrying bag and will easily fit in the trunk of a small car. Our inflatable paddle boards are virtually indestructible, so you’ll never have to worry about dings, dents, or scratches. Oversized deck pads and high weight capacity are great for bringing a small dog or child paddling. We recommend these boards for families with kids, multiple riders of different weights, and larger riders. SIC/Tahe Hard Stand Up Paddle Boards Available in 10’, and 11’ sizes with weight capacities of up to 275 lbs. Perform great in all water conditions. Great for all ages, sizes, and skill levels. Unique hybrid design featuring a keeled nose for excellent tracking. Super durable Tough-Tec construction makes these boards some of the most durable hard stand up paddle boards on the market. Full rail-to-rail volume for enhanced stability and maximum use of the entire deck. Great for touring and extended paddle boarding sessions. Extra rigid construction makes these boards stiffer than our inflatable paddle boards. We recommend these boards for anyone interested in extended paddles, touring, and customers staying on or very near the lake as they are slightly heavier and less portable than our inflatables. STAND UP PADDLE BOARDING FAQs HOW MUCH DOES IT COST TO RENT A STAND UP PADDLE BOARD? Please visit our Rates page for all stand up paddle board rental pricing information. WHAT’S THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN INFLATABLE PADDLE BOARDS AND HARD PADDLE BOARDS? Essentially, not very much. Both inflatable paddle boards and hard paddle boards are stable, durable, great for all skill levels, and tons of fun. Inflatable paddle boards tend to be lighter, extremely durable, and have a higher weight capacity. Hard stand up paddle boards tend to be a bit heavier, more rigid, glide through the water easier due to having a lower volume, and less affected by wind, as they sit lower in the water. Usually, we tell people that if they are asking this question, they won’t be able to tell the difference! WHAT’S SUP? SUP is simply short for stand up paddle board. It’s a bit easier to say, right? IS PADDLE BOARDING ON LAKE TAHOE DIFFICULT FOR BEGINNERS? Paddle boarding is much easier than it looks, and if you want, you can sit down or kneel rather than standing up on the board. The great thing about paddle boarding on Lake Tahoe is that if you stick close to the shore, you can avoid boat wakes, and the water stays quite shallow (and the shoreline is beautiful too). CAN KIDS RENT A STAND UP PADDLE BOARD ON LAKE TAHOE? Yes, we have paddle board rentals that are suitable for kids as young as eight years old. However, if a child is under 16 years old they must be accompanied by a parent or guardian when they’re out on Lake Tahoe. DO I NEED TO WEAR A LIFE JACKET WHILE PADDLE BOARDING ON LAKE TAHOE? California law states that anyone under 13 years old must wear a life jacket while out on Lake Tahoe although we encourage all paddlers to wear their life jackets to be safe. All others must have a life jacket with them on their paddle boards but aren’t required to wear the life jacket. You can bring your own life jacket with you or use one of ours at no extra charge. WHAT SHOULD I BRING WHILE PADDLE BOARDING ON LAKE TAHOE? At North Tahoe Paddle we provide lifejackets and paddles, but there are a few additional things we recommend taking with you while paddle boarding on Lake Tahoe. Sunscreen, water, and a hat to shade your face and eyes from the sun are all highly recommended. Outside of those items, we do not recommend taking too much more with you due to the design of the paddle board. Paddle Boarding on Lake Tahoe provides plenty of opportunities for amazing photos, and if you need them, we have dry bags and waterproof cell phone cases to keep your cameras and smartphones protected. WILL I FALL OFF OF MY PADDLE BOARD? You might, but most paddle boarders do not. Don’t expect to fall in the water, but be prepared to fall in just in case. Leave behind anything you don’t want to get wet. If you fall off your board, do not linger in the water. It is very easy to get back on the SUP boards from the water. Wearing the coiled ankle leash is required so that if you do fall off of your paddle board, the board won’t drift away from you. CAN BOTH MY CHILD AND I BE ON ONE STAND UP PADDLE BOARD? You can bring your child on your SUP as long as they are under 50 lbs. They should not paddle, but they can enjoy the ride. WHAT IS THE BEST WAY TO TAKE MY PADDLE BOARD OUT OF THE WATER? When taking your paddle board out of the water, the most important part is to avoid damaging the board and the fin in the rear of the board. When paddling into shore slow down to a stop as the water becomes approximately knee-deep. Carefully step off the side of the paddle board and grab the handle with your dominant hand. Carry the paddle board between your side and the arm of your dominant hand. Once on shore, place the paddle board on the sand with the fin pointing up in the air, and never sit or stand on the paddle board once it’s resting on the beach. The Lake Tahoe Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS) Program helps protect the clarity and ecosystem of Lake Tahoe by preventing the introduction and spread of invasive species. Mandatory inspections, decontamination procedures, and boater education all play a critical role in preserving the lake for future generations. Located at Obexer's Marina on Lake Tahoe's West Shore. Obexer's Water Sports (OWS) features jet ski rentals, water ski and wake board lessons, wake skating, wake surfing, tubing and boat charters. Jet Ski Rentals OWS offers a fleet of Sea-Doo GTS 130 personal watercraft available for rent. Jet skis can accommodate up to two passengers depending on the size and weight of the riders. While all ages are welcome to ride, guests must be 18 years of age or older in order to operate a jet ski and carry passengers. All jet ski rentals include fuel, life jacket, and a wetsuit if you chose to wear one. Water Sport Lessons OWS provides lessons in water skiing, wake boarding, wake surfing, and wake skating to all ages and abilities. Our United States Coast Guard Licensed Captains and American Water Ski Association Certified Instructors have the knowledge, skill and experience to give you all the help you need to feel confident and be successful, whether you are a seasoned pro or a first time beginner! All lessons include boat, captain/instructor, fuel, life jackets, wetsuits and equipment. We can also provide lessons on your own boat with water sport instruction as well as safe and effective boat operating/driving techniques. Boat Charters There is nothing like experiencing Lake Tahoe by boat! You can sit back, relax and leave the driving to OWS, one of our certified captains will be happy to get you and your group out on the lake for some spectacular views and fresh mountain air! Lesson and boat charter times book up quickly, to reserve your water sports adventure click on the book now button to reserve your time. Reservation must be made via the online reservation system. We look forward to getting you out on the water! Skip the Traffic. Arrive by Boat. Heading to a Lake Tahoe event this summer? Avoid the congestion, parking hassles, and long drive times by arriving in style aboard an Obexer’s Boat Company charter with Obexer's Water Sports. Our captained charters can transport your group directly across the lake, allowing you to enjoy the scenery while avoiding some of Tahoe’s busiest traffic days. Surf Across the Lake – July 22, 2026 A unique Lake Tahoe paddling and water sports event that brings participants together for a memorable crossing of the lake. American Century Championship Celebrity Golf Tournament – July 8–12, 2026 Watch sports and entertainment celebrities compete at Edgewood Tahoe Golf Course while avoiding the heavy traffic that accompanies one of Tahoe’s largest annual events. Tahoe City Farmers Market – Thursdays Throughout the Summer Enjoy local produce, artisan goods, food vendors, and live entertainment in the heart of Tahoe City. Concerts at Commons Beach – Sundays, June 14 – September 6, 2026 (No Concert July 5) Take in free lakeside concerts at Commons Beach and let us handle the transportation. SMOOTHER IS FASTER: We engineered a flex stay rear end for class-leading suspension performance, while eliminating the extra weight and maintenance associated with pivots required in a traditional design. HYDROFORMED ALLOY: Chisel shaves extra material and weight with a one-piece hydroformed seat tube that integrates the seat tube pivot, main pivot, and BB shell. Start your ride in The Village at Palisades Tahoe and cruise the scenic Truckee River Bike Trail toward Tahoe City and the sparkling blue waters of Lake Tahoe. Safely separated from Route 89, the bike path offers a relaxing way to explore the Tahoe area at your own pace. Riders under 18 must be accompanied by an adult who assumes responsibility for the rental. Bike rentals are available Friday through Sunday out of The Village Demo Center. Rentals will be available daily starting June 19. Bike Rentals E-Bike Rentals Our Rental Fleet Specialized Roll 2.0 The Specialized Roll 2.0 is a comfortable cruiser bike built for relaxed rides, sightseeing, and exploring the Truckee River Bike Trail. Specialized Turbo Como 4.0 The Specialized Turbo Como 4.0 is an electric comfort cruiser with pedal assist, making longer rides feel easier while you take in the scenery. Bike Rental Rates Full Day Half Day Adults $64 $48 Kids (12 and Under) $52 $36 E-Bikes (Ages 16+) $110 $75 *All-day rental is from open to close. Bike Rental Returns Bicycle rentals are due back on the date/time agreed upon by Palisades Tahoe and the renter. Delays will be subject to additional charges. Biking On Mountain Palisades Tahoe does allow biking on the mountain within designated areas. Biking on mountain roads is strictly prohibited. Biking on-mountain is not lift accessed. ADA Accessibility and Services Disabled guests are always welcome and can enjoy full access to the Palisades Tahoe facilities and seasonal access to the mountain. Notify us in advance of special accommodations: Please call 1-800-403-0206 or 1-800-735-2929 (TTY) rich-text, responsive-table Parking rich-text, responsive-table There are several accessible ADA Parking areas for resort guests with Handicap Parking permits for access to our facilities. North Side of The Village East Side of The Village South Side of The Village SnoVentures Far East Olympic Village Events Center rich-text, responsive-table RESTROOMS rich-text, responsive-table There are several wheelchair accessible restrooms in the base area. The Village - two public accessible restrooms are located in the Village. Street signs will direct you to the restrooms. Tram - located on the main level of the Tram building, accessible via the ramp on the South side of the building. Restroom is located on the south side of the building on the lobby level. O House - three of the four levels of the O House have accessible bathrooms. Only the KT Kitchen/Bar One level does NOT have an ADA bathroom on that level. A permanently mount stair climber is located next to the KT Kitchen (food court) for access to the Pocket Bar level accessible restrooms. Or go out the door onto the KT Deck and in the doors to Pocket Bar Plaza Bar - restrooms are located on the other side of the bar. Wildflour Level - restrooms are in the back South side corner. Pocket Bar/Dave’s Deli - restrooms are up the ramp and to the right. Far East Center - East side of Building SnoVentures - North side of Building High Camp - accessible restrooms are available at High Camp Gold Coast - accessible restrooms are available at Gold Coast rich-text, responsive-table VILLAGE AND BASE AREA ENTRANCES rich-text, responsive-table There are three zero entry guest entrances to the Palisades base area. Guest pathways in the base area are comprised of block pavers, asphalt and concrete. All access points are very close to the heart of the base area. North side of The Village access is closest to the Tram, Ticket Sales, O House. East side of The Village access is closest to Village Check In, Conference Rooms and The Village stores. South side of The Village access is closest to the Tahoe Truckee Medical Group, Members Looker Room, Funitel and on snow access. rich-text, responsive-table Palisades ADA Maps rich-text, responsive-table The Village ADA Map & Directory Alpine ADA Maps rich-text, responsive-table Alpine ADA Map & Directory Alpine Lodge ADA Map Level 1 Alpine Lodge ADA Map Level 2 Alpine Lodge ADA Map Ground Level Alpine Base Area ADA Map Adaptive Ski Equipment Palisades Tahoe allows the use of adaptive devices or other “manually-powered mobility aids” designed for use on the ski slopes. Adaptive devices are any specialized equipment that has been designed and manufactured primarily for use by individuals who have disabilities, including: ski bikes, mono-skis, bi skis, outriggers, and sit-skis. The Disabled Sports America Center provides instruction and will arrange the use of such mobility devices when requested in advance to ensure qualified instructors are available. For those that have disabilities and choose to use ski bikes outside of an instructional setting, we ask that you contact Dispatch (Palisades: 530-452-7145 or Alpine: 530 581-8223) prior to your visit to schedule a time for Ski Patrol to inspect your equipment. The use of ski bikes, snow skates, sled dogs, etc. by those without adaptive needs is prohibited. On-Mountain Locations Ticket Windows Wheelchair Accessible Ticket Window and the Season Pass Office is located across from the Funitel and inside the Tram Building. All guests interested in accessing the mountain are required to have a lift ticket or season pass. O House O House facilities Wildflour Level, KT Kitchen/Bar One Level and Pocket Bar Level are accessible from the walkways. Plaza bar is accessible via the elevator adjacent to the loading dock. A Resort Host can help direct guest to the elevator Tram and High Camp Tram lobby is accessible via a ramp on the South side. High Camp facilities are accessible via several small elevators including access to all F&B outlets. Accessible restrooms are available. Funitel and Gold Coast Funitel is accessible entrance is located on the North side of the building off of the pavers. The elevator to access the Funitel loading level is located immediately to the left as you enter the building. A Resort Host can assist you in loading the Funitel. Gold Coast Complex is accessible at all three levels via an elevator located next to the entrance to Starbucks. OVEC - Corporate Office/Grand Ballroom The main conference space (Grand Room) located on the second level is accessible via a ramp on the North West corner of the building. Power Driven Mobility Devices Winter Policy Palisades Tahoe has determined that the use of any power-driven devices or vehicles by the public on the mountain (including other power-driven mobility devices used by individuals with mobility disabilities), creates an unsafe environment for both the user and the public based on the experiences of other ski resorts and Palisades Tahoe’s experience with motorized equipment on the ski slopes generally and with particular attention to various types of power-driven personal mobility devices. Injuries resulting from the use of such devices on the slopes can be more serious than other types of risks and expose the user and other skiers/snowboarders to a greater risk than non-power driven adaptive devices, particularly in the case of collisions with other skiers and snowboarders. These safety concerns are compounded by our facility’s volume of skiers and snowboarders. These safety requirements are based on actual risks and are not intended to be discriminatory in any way; such devices cannot be used by non-disabled persons as well. Use of most power-driven mobility devices are authorized in the base village area. Start your ride in The Village at Palisades Tahoe and cruise the scenic Truckee River Bike Trail toward Tahoe City and the sparkling blue waters of Lake Tahoe. Safely separated from Route 89, the bike path offers a relaxing way to explore the Tahoe area at your own pace. Riders under 18 must be accompanied by an adult who assumes responsibility for the rental. Bike rentals are available Friday through Sunday out of The Village Demo Center. Rentals will be available daily starting June 19. Bike Rentals E-Bike Rentals Our Rental Fleet Specialized Roll 2.0 The Specialized Roll 2.0 is a comfortable cruiser bike built for relaxed rides, sightseeing, and exploring the Truckee River Bike Trail. Specialized Turbo Como 4.0 The Specialized Turbo Como 4.0 is an electric comfort cruiser with pedal assist, making longer rides feel easier while you take in the scenery. Bike Rental Rates Full Day Half Day Adults $64 $48 Kids (12 and Under) $52 $36 E-Bikes (Ages 16+) $110 $75 *All-day rental is from open to close. Bike Rental Returns Bicycle rentals are due back on the date/time agreed upon by Palisades Tahoe and the renter. Delays will be subject to additional charges. Biking On Mountain Palisades Tahoe does allow biking on the mountain within designated areas. Biking on mountain roads is strictly prohibited. Biking on-mountain is not lift accessed. Adaptive devices are any specialized equipment that has been designed and manufactured primarily for use by individuals who have disabilities, including: ski bikes, mono-skis, bi skis, outriggers, and sit-skis. The Disabled Sports America Center provides instruction and will arrange the use of such mobility devices when requested in advance to ensure qualified instructors are available. For those that have disabilities and choose to use ski bikes outside of an instructional setting, we ask that you contact Dispatch (Palisades: 530-452-7145 or Alpine: 530 581-8223) prior to your visit to schedule a time for Ski Patrol to inspect your equipment. The use of ski bikes, snow skates, sled dogs, etc. by those without adaptive needs is prohibited. High Camp facilities are accessible via several small elevators including access to all F&B outlets. Accessible restrooms are available. Funitel and Gold Coast Funitel is accessible entrance is located on the North side of the building off of the pavers. The elevator to access the Funitel loading level is located immediately to the left as you enter the building. A Resort Host can assist you in loading the Funitel. Gold Coast Complex is accessible at all three levels via an elevator located next to the entrance to Starbucks. OVEC - Corporate Office/Grand Ballroom The main conference space (Grand Room) located on the second level is accessible via a ramp on the North West corner of the building. Power Driven Mobility Devices Winter Policy Palisades Tahoe has determined that the use of any power-driven devices or vehicles by the public on the mountain (including other power-driven mobility devices used by individuals with mobility disabilities), creates an unsafe environment for both the user and the public based on the experiences of other ski resorts and Palisades Tahoe’s experience with motorized equipment on the ski slopes generally and with particular attention to various types of power-driven personal mobility devices. Injuries resulting from the use of such devices on the slopes can be more serious than other types of risks and expose the user and other skiers/snowboarders to a greater risk than non-power driven adaptive devices, particularly in the case of collisions with other skiers and snowboarders. These safety concerns are compounded by our facility’s volume of skiers and snowboarders. These safety requirements are based on actual risks and are not intended to be discriminatory in any way; such devices cannot be used by non-disabled persons as well. Use of most power-driven mobility devices are authorized in the base village area. It's typical for the battery capacity range of your Pedego eBike to vary, as with all electric bikes. Several factors can influence your range, such as the pedal assist and/or throttle usage, terrain inclines, weather conditions, the weight of the load, frequent or abrupt starts and stops, and rapid acceleration. To maximize the range of your Pedego eBike, consider adjusting your riding habits and optimizing various factors. Start by using the pedal assist and/or throttle judiciously, particularly on flat terrain, to conserve battery power. When encountering inclines, try to maintain a steady pace and utilize lower assist levels if available to minimize power consumption. Assisting the motor by pedaling up inclines with more effort will lighten the load on the motor and draw less power. Keep an eye on weather forecasts and plan rides during favorable conditions to reduce wind resistance and extreme temperature energy loss. Additionally, minimize the weight of your cargo or belongings carried on the bike to lessen the strain on the battery. Practice smoother acceleration and braking techniques to minimize energy wastage from sudden speed changes and stops. Ensure your bike tires are inflated to the recommended pressure levels as specified in the following the recommended air pressure table. Explore more ways to optimize your battery usage for an enhanced riding experience. By being mindful of these factors and implementing efficient riding strategies, you can extend the range of your Pedego eBike and enjoy longer rides with confidence. You bet! These skis have been designed to help you progress and perfect a carving turn versus a sliding turn. When a skier begins to feel a carving turn their level of confidence improves and the control and sensation that goes along with this technique is exhilarating. Beginners to experts enjoy shaped skis. Do you carry snowboards? Yes, our snowboard fleet consists of premium equipment from Burton, Rossignol, Lib Tech, Jones, Head, YES, Volkl, Blizzard, Dynastar, and more. We carry both step-in and strap-in bindings. Does it take very long to rent equipment? Usually not, especially if you pre-purchase your equipment using our online reservations system. Customers who reserve their equipment online also receive the added benefit of a 20% discount! I don’t know how many days I’m going to ski/board. How do you charge for your rentals? Powder House knows there are a lot of variables that influence how many days a person skis. Make your reservation online or in-store, if you decide to return the equipment early or keep it longer, we will settle the payment differnce upon you returning your equipment. In addition, every 4th consecutive rental day is FREE! I’ll be arriving in the afternoon, can I get my rentals the night before? Certainly, Powder House’s main shop, located at 4045 Lake Tahoe Blvd, is open until 10pm every day. All other locations are open until 10pm during peak season. There is no additional charge for renting the night before (between 3pm – 8pm). Do you sell equipment that was used for past years’ rentals? At the end of each season we do sell selected items from our rental fleet. However, no sales are made during the season. Do you rent Ski Clothing? We rent Jackets, Pants and Helmets for Additional Fees. Gloves, Hats and Goggles are Available for Purchase only. Group members will receive a 10% discount on non-sale items. I don’t know what ski length or type of ski will work best for me. Will the staff at the stores be able to suggest what will work best based on my specific measurements and ability? Yes, worry no more. Powder House’s ski tech’s passion for the sport reaches far beyond the walls of our shops and onto the mountain. They will be able to give you suggestions based on their knowledge of, and personal experience with the equipment. We desire to provide you with the most comfortable and exhilarating experience at every ability level! What are your prices for rental equipment? Because of the variety of packages and individual items we offer, we can best answer this question by referring you to the RATES section of this website. Please double click the rates tab at the top of our home page for more information. Rates listed here do not already include the 20% online booking discount. Our intent was to produce a highly sophisticated small batch (seriously there's not alot of them!) aluminum production for core riders who are dedicated to the mountain lifestyle. So we designed the NIGHTTRAIN in partnership with Dave Weagle using his Orion Dynamics platform and dual idler layout. The NIGHTTRAIN is a full Alloy, no compromise enduro bike that is made for the roughest of terrain to the biggest of jumps, while also being extremely efficient climbing uphill. The bike is designed to pedal very efficiently all while encouraging you to pump, jump and play around on the trail. The NIGHTTRAIN takes from our ski design philosophy at RMU of creating some of the most fun, playful, and versatile skis on the market and brings that to the Bike world. The RMU NIGHTTRAIN is built for riders who want a true freeride/enduro crossover machine capable of handling everything from bike park laps to aggressive backcountry descents. Its unique dual idler drivetrain and two-chain drivetrain system help reduce pedal feedback while improving suspension performance through rough terrain. Built from durable aluminum, the NIGHTTRAIN stands apart from traditional alloy mountain bikes by blending playful freeride mountain bike characteristics with the efficiency and capability expected from a modern enduro mountain bike. pages.text: Reno Brew Bike | Reno's Favorite Pedal Trolley and Pub Crawler Skip to content GIFT CERTIFICATES 775-771-0164 info@renobrewbike.com Reno Brew Bike Reno's Favorite Pedal Trolley and Pub Crawler HOME ABOUT US BIKE STOPS FAQ NEWS & MEDIA OTHER LOCATIONS TOURS TOUR PRICING INDIVIDUAL SEATS PRIVATE TOURS GIFT CERTIFICATES CONTACT BOOK NOW HOME ABOUT US BIKE STOPS FAQ NEWS & MEDIA OTHER LOCATIONS TOURS TOUR PRICING INDIVIDUAL SEATS PRIVATE TOURS GIFT CERTIFICATES CONTACT An adventure your whole group will enjoy! Seating for 15 guests to experience the best of Downtown Reno. Choose the ultimate bachelorette party icebreaker to unite your crew and celebrate the bride-to-be! Make your milestone truly memorable, whether it's a birthday, bachelor party, or team building event! Reserve a private or all-inclusive tour to sample Reno's best locally crafted beer, spirits, food, and non-alcholic beverages. If it’s time to celebrate a big milestone, or just get outside to enjoy Downtown Reno, Brew Bike is the best choice for a fun way to bring your group together! With a sober driver, party lights, and sound system included, it’s easy to get your pedal party started and keep it rolling through town! Whether you’re new to Reno Brew Bike or a returning customer, take your social event to the next level with a 15-passenger pedal trolley experience. You’re sure to make happy and lasting memories! Individual Seats Smaller groups and those who prefer to pay separately can reserve by Individual Seats. Bar stops and music are selected by your driver, but these bar crawls are just as much fun! No pressure of fronting money for friends or difficult decision-making. Duration : 2 Hours From USD $32.00 BOOK NOW Private Bike Make it your own personal party and reserve the whole bike (all 15 seats)! Play your own music, get wild with decorations, and you get to choose the stops. Save Money: It’s already discounted! A Private Bike costs $100 less than 15 Individual Seats. Duration : 2 Hours From USD $385.00 BOOK NOW Birthday Parties Groups of all sizes have a blast celebrating birthdays on the Brew Bike! Eliminates much of the hassle of hosting one too 😉 Bachelorette Parties Treat the bride to a party bike experience sure to get the night started in style! Choose from add-ons to make the celebration extra special. Team Building Recognize the achievements of your employees with a fun group activity! Have a drink, socialize, and pedal to bring your team together. Other Reno Tours Bar crawling isn’t our only specialty. Choose to experience Reno’s: Art, Food, History, or Mixed Age food & drink. Brew Bike will get your experience rolling! Brew Bike is the most fun way to do Reno! Are you new to Brew Bike? It’s best to think of your reservation as a social vehicle rental that comes with a sober driver. We most often do a 2-hour bar crawl during which we visit two bars, but Private Bike reservations can also visit other fantastic small businesses in the Downtown and Midtown areas of Reno. Whichever outing they choose, our passengers always have a great time! Alcohol is not currently allowed on the Brew Bike due to Reno’s open container law, and the cost of your drinks is not included in your reservation. Before reserving, we encourage you to check out our FAQ , or contact us , and we will do our best to help you out. Remember to get to our tour start location 30 minutes ahead of your scheduled start. Your driver will check you in inside Black Rabbit Meads, at 401 E 4th Street, Reno 89512 . We've got everything you need at Our California Ski Run Boulevard location. Rip N' Willies is South Lake Tahoe's top-notch, one-stop ski and snowboard shop! We specialize in rentals, carrying a wide variety to suit any renter's needs: snowboards, demo skis, performance packages, children's, cross country, sleds, and clothing - conveniently located on the way to Heavenly Mountain Resort. FIND US Our Friendly & Knowledgeable Staff Will Get you the Proper Fit . Our service is what we take pride in and trying to remain your local ski shop is what drives us. Located on Ski Run Boulevard, minutes away from the California Base Lodge, at Heavenly, the location gives you the ease of getting set up quickly and being on the mountain in just minutes. And if you are one to visit us throughout the year on a regular basis, we can set your name up in our database and all you have to do is call and we will have your rental equipment ready for you to pick up, at your convenience, all at a discounted rate. BOOK NOW Testimonials Great service! As soon as you walk in the door someone is ready to help. Easy reservation system online. I also got a nice iron wax that looks really good on ny board. Overall, I will recommend this shop for rentals. Convenient location. Affordable. Naydine C. My family and I had such a great experience at Rip N Willies. Their rates are very affordable, and the "4th day free" deal is amazing especially when you are a family of 4! I've been able to get some fun demos while my kids are fit with everything they need head to toe. The condition of their equipment is the best I've seen from any rental shop. Best Part is that they are so close to Heavenly Mountain making it so convenient. My husband likes to get a good wax on the way up! Cesar is the best at making sure you're ripping on the mountain. I'm so happy we found them and will be back. Kimberly B. Love Rip N Willies! We've been coming here for years. Staff is super friendly and helpful!! Mindy K. Great friendly service, and super reasonable prices on rentals. Overall great experiencing renting from this business. Will come back! Kristen B. So You Want to Snowshoe or Go Cross Country Skiing and Don't Know Where to Go? Don't worry about that. Depending on your ability and snow conditions, we will send you on your way with your rental equipment in hand, and a map showing you a few different places to go. Cross country skiing and snow shoeing is a beautiful way to enjoy the peace and quiet that happens during the winter. It's a great way to get away and see what Tahoe is really all about. Tahoe's pristine beauty comes alive when you are out there in her elements: the snow, the pine trees, the big boulders, her creeks and rivers sparkling through the snow showing off their icy brown grass, and snow covered banks. We suggest taking your lunch, a bottle of wine or hot chocolate, and a blanket, and find one of those large boulders so you can sit down and enjoy yourselves. Stop throwing money in the casino and go do something you’ll never forget! Sand Harbor State Park has Limited Docks About Sand Harbor The largest alpine lake in North America, Lake Tahoe is a cobalt blue lake atop the Sierra Nevada mountain range. On its eastern shores, gently sloping beaches, crystal-clear water and interesting rock formations allow for wonderfully sublime swimming, kayaking and scuba diving at Sand Harbor. Boaters, water-skiers and fisherman can easily launch from one of the park’s two ramps. Visitors who would like a peaceful retreat from surf and sun can picnic in the shade of cedars and Jeffrey pines in one of many picnic sites equipped with barbecues and tables. The park also hosts the Lake Tahoe Shakespeare Festival every summer. Park Detail Hours 8 a.m. to 1 hour after sunset. Boat Ramp: 6AM - 4PM (Boat Docks Unavailable). Office Hours: 8am - 4pm, Tues-Fri Entrance Fees (see all park fees) $10.00 ($15.00 for Non-NV Vehicles) Contact Us 775-831-0494 shsp@parks.nv.gov Address 2005 Highway 28 Incline Village, NV 89450 Amenities Connect with Sand Harbor Make a Reservation View on Parks App Get Directions Current Weather Road Conditions FACILITIES & AMENITIES Please Note: Camping is not permitted at Sand Harbor Day-Use Reservations are required for vehicle entry daily May 15 through September 30. Learn More Frequently Asked Questions : View a list of FAQs for Sand Harbor Transportation: From Memorial to Labor Day Sand Harbor is very popular and experiences high visitation. Those planning to visit Sand Harbor should be prepared for park closures and have an alternate destination in mind. Parking and dropping off on Hwy 28 at any location other than designated parking (Memorial Point) is prohibited and you will not be permitted entry to the Park. Tahoe Transportation District (TTD) is pleased to announce the return of the East Shore Express Service beginning June 28, 2024. This season, hourly paid parking will be available at the Tunnel Creek parking lot, located at 1102 Tahoe Blvd. at the Tahoe East Shore Trailhead. Learn more here . Group Area/Ramada : A group use area set next to the lake that can accommodate groups of up to 120 people. Larger groups may be accommodated by making arrangements with the Park prior to booking and may require a special use (SCUP) permit (applications only accepted October 1 - April 15 each year). The covered facility comes equipped with a large gas grill which the Park will provide propane for (use of the grill is prohibited during red flag days), electricity via two 110V outlets (No amplified sound, including music, speakers, and PA systems) potable water (pending weather conditions and winter shutoff), and twelve cafeteria-style tables which can comfortably seat 10 people each. Use is by reservation only which can be made via Nevada State Parks' online reservation system, ReserveNevada.com . Information, rules, regulations, and the group area reservation agreement are available on the reservation site. Camping Reservations Visitors may make reservations from 3 days to 11 months in advance on reservenevada.com. Inventory opens up at 8 a.m. Pacific Standard Time and is on a rolling 11 month booking window. All reservable campsites not reserved may be paid for on a first come, first served basis for 1 night at a time. First come, first served visitors may extend their stay by reaching out to park staff. Campground and cabin check in is at 2:00 pm and check out is at 11:00 am. Group Use Areas vary by check in and check out times but are listed on their Unit Details. There is no minimum stay requirement, but each park varies for their maximum stay from 7 to 14 days. This information can be found on each park's webpage. Payment is due at the time of booking your reservation. To ensure fair access to cabin reservations, modifications and cancellations will be restricted for a period of one week. This policy is designed to prevent last-minute adjustments by those booking on the edge of the reservation window, to allow others the opportunity to reserve available dates before an existing reservation is extended or adjusted. -Reservation Fees Visitors pay a non-refundable $5.00 transaction fee per reservation. -Modifications Modifications can be made up to 3 days before the day of arrival. Visitors will be charged $5.00 for making a change further than one month out from their upcoming stay. Visitors will be charged $10.00 for making a change less than one month out from their upcoming stay. -Cancellations Visitors can cancel their reservation up to 3 days before the day of arrival. Cancellations occurring more than a month out from the arrival date will not be charged for canceling their reservation, with the exception of the $5.00 nonrefundable transaction fee. Cancellations occurring less than a month out, but more than 3 days before the day of arrival, will have a $10.00 fee assessed. Cancellations that occur within 3 days of the reservation arrival date will have a $10.00 fee assessed plus the cost of a one-night stay. - Refunds will not be given for: Events, circumstances, or decisions that are beyond the control of the Agencies. Including bad weather and other weather conditions (smoke), early departure not due to an emergency, drought, bugs, fire restrictions or bans, water conditions, trail closures, algae, traffic/city noise, equipment failure, customer error and Wi-Fi/cellular service availability. Early departures or cancellations after arrival date. -No Shows Park staff will hold reserved campsites or cabins until the applicable check-in time, one day after the scheduled arrival date. If contact is made with the park, the reservation will be honored. If the visitor does not make an effort to contact the park then the reservation will be cancelled and nonrefundable. Day-Use Reservations Parks that require day use reservations: Big Bend of the Colorado State Recreation Area (May 15 through September 15) Sand Harbor State Park (May 15 through September 30) All other parks are open for day use without a reservation -Day Use Reservation Rules Visitors must enter the park by 11:30 a.m. at Big Bend and 10:30 a.m. at Sand Harbor, thereafter the park will open to first come, first served visitors. The Nevada Division of State Parks has fully implemented required day-use reservations at Sand Harbor State Park. This system aims to reduce traffic congestion on Highway 28, improve trip planning, and alleviate overcrowding. Frequently Asked Questions Where do I make a reservation? www.reservenevada.com When are day-use reservations required? Daily May 1 through September 30 from 8:00am - 10:30am. Why did the park add reservations? The reservations help alleviate traffic congestion on HWY 28, assist with trip planning, and prevent overcrowding on the beach. Visitors no longer need to be at the park in early morning hours in hopes of getting a parking spot. Reservations are a guarenteed parking spot until 10:30am. Is the Boat Launch reservation only? No, the boat launch remains first come, first served. Do I need a reservation to get in? Day-use reservations are required for vehicle entry from park opening to 10:30am daily from May 15 to Septmeber 30. After 10:30am, the park opens to first come, first served as long as the park has not yet reached capacity. Entering the park via the East Shore Trail will not require reservations. Does a reservation guarantee a parking spot? Yes, up until 10:30am. If a reservation holder does not enter the park before 10:30am, they forfeit their reservation and their spot will become available to first come, first served. Do I need to get a day use reservation to use my Ramada/Group Use Area reservation? No, your group use area reservation comes with 25 parking spots exclusively for the Ramada/group use area. All vehicles coming into the park to utilize the Ramada/Group Use Area reservation will still need to pay vehicle entry fees. Will I need a reservation if I have tickets to the Shakespeare Festival? If Shakespeare Festival ticket holders want to arrive before 10:30am, they will need a reservation. Since the shows don't begin until later in the day, the reservations should not impact the ability for ticket holders to gain entry to the park in late afternoon. Will I need a reservation to enter the park through the East Shore Trail? No, reservations are not required for pedestrian access into the park via the East Shore Trail. Pedestrian access is strictly prohibited at all times on HWY 28. Do locals get special access? No, the Nevada Division of State Parks remains committed to providing equal access to everyone at all State Parks. The park entrance fee remains the same at $10 for NV vehicles and $15 for out of state vehicles. Can I drop my family off without a reservation? No. Drop offs are strictly prohibited at all times. Can I use a ride share app to get dropped off if I have reservation? Yes, a valid reservation will get you access into the park until 10:30am; however, Ridesharing into Sand Harbor is highly discouraged due to the limited availability of rideshares in the evening. Being picked up or dropped off on HWY 28 is strictly prohibited. Is the non-refundable $5.00 fee charged in addition to the entry fee? Yes, the $5.00 fee is a processing fee that is charged on all reservations. Visitors who make a same-day reservation will not be charged the reservation fee. Do I get charged the $5.00 fee even if I have an annual permit? Yes, the $5.00 fee is a processing fee that is charged on all reservations. You can make a reservation online through Epic Mountain Rentals or directly through participating resort rental pages. You can book your reservation at any time before your arrival, but we recommend reserving at least a few days in advance to ensure the best selection and availability. If you make a reservation less than 2 calendar days in advance of your arrival, gear will only be available for pick up at a store location and delivery will not be available. Gear selection is subject to gear availability at time of booking. We recommend booking gear for a minimum of 48 hours in advance to ensure the best overall experience and selection. What if I need to cancel or change my reservation? Reservations may be canceled up to 24 hours before 8:00 am local time on the first day of your reservation for a full refund, and can be done online. For cancellations inside of 24 hours that have not yet been fulfilled, refunds are available minus a restocking fee. Restocking fees are applicable to each package on the reservation. No shows are non-refundable. Please call 970-754-0033 (or toll free at 1-800-200-9990) so we can assist you. We cannot cancel reservations by email or in person. Rescheduled reservations will be subject to inventory available of their new date, which may be different from your original reservation. How do I determine my skier type? Your skier type reflects your ability level and is typically classified as Type I (Beginner), Type II (Intermediate), or Type III (Advanced). Bike Rentals FAQ What is your refund policy? You can cancel up to 24 hours before your reservation for a full refund. Call us to make a change at 970-754-0033 for U.S. reservations or 800-766-0449 for Canadian reservations. If you can, have your confirmation number handy. Can I change my rental dates after I book? Yes. We understand plans change. We're happy to modify your reservation up to 24 hours in advance. Call us to make a change at 970-754-0033 for U.S. reservations or 800-766-0449 for Canadian reservations. If you can, have your confirmation number handy. Do you rent helmets? Absolutely. For your safety, all rentals include a helmet. We have adult and kids sizes available for every bike rental. What should I wear? We recommend wearing layers you can remove as needed and packing rain gear or wind protection. Consider bringing a backpack to store any extra items and a water bottle if you're cruising around town. Do you rent kids' bikes? Most locations have kids bikes available; sizes may be limited. What time can I pick up my half-day morning rental? Generally, half-day morning rentals are 10 AM 2 PM. This can vary by location, so confirm the exact times with your rental shop. What time can I pick up my half-day afternoon rental? Generally, half-day afternoon rentals are 2 PM 6 PM. This can vary by location, so confirm the exact times with your rental shop. Do you rent protective gear aside from helmets? Yes, for certain bike park and downhill bike rentals. These options include knee and elbow pads and body armor and can be selected in Step 3. Are there mountain bike trails for beginners? Most locations have mountain bike trails for beginners. Ask a team member for their trail recommendations based on your experience and comfort level. What happens if I get a flat tire? Safety first. Dismount and move your bike to a safe place. Then, call the rental shop. We'll help fix your flat and get you back out there. We recommend bringing a cell phone and adding the shop's number before you begin your ride. What times of the year do you rent bikes? Typically, May through August, but this can vary by weather conditions and resort. For your safety, some trails may be closed early in the season. Can we bike on the ski resort property? At most resorts, yes. Check current conditions and for any trail restrictions before your visit. Several resorts also have chairlifts that carry you and your bike up the mountain so you can ride down single-track trails or ski runs. Resorts like Whistler Blackcomb, Keystone, Northstar and more have bike parks. My child is coming with a group, but I will not accompany him or her. Is there a liability waiver I need to sign? We require a parent or legal guardian to sign a release of liability on behalf of an unaccompanied person younger than 18 years old. Download, complete and print this waiver and send it with your child. They will not be able to participate if the release is not signed. No exceptions. Are there weight limits on your bikes? Yes, each manufacturer will set a maximum rider weight to ensure the safety of riders please contact your preferred rental store directly to confirm the maximum rider weight for the bike you're interested in renting. Sierra Adventures takes care of the details, you have fun! LESSONS & CLINICS Kayak Sierra Adventures is proud to offer kayak lessons and clinics for both river and flat water kayaking. Our Intro is only $79 per person, designed to introduce the basics of safety, gear, paddle strokes and boat styles. At Level Two, we split the group for either river or flat water lessons, designed to get you to the next level of your ability. Level Two includes wet exits, bracing, wet entry, boat maneuvering, and advanced paddle strokes. Level Three is final preparation for open water sessions at Reno’s Truckee River Whitewater Park. This level includes Eskimo rolls, assisted rescue, open water safety, and equipment fitting. Level Four is optional for continued roll sessions or open water skills and training. Levels Two-Four are $79 per person for each level, everything included. The entire four level course is $199 per person. Pool classes are every Tuesday evening from 7:30 – 9:30 pm. Meet fifteen minutes before start time at Sierra Adventures in downtown Reno, at the Silver Legacy Adventure Desk. Adventure We provide introduction lessons for all water, land, and snow activities for the whole family. Choose from Kayak 101, Bike Safety & Repair, Boogie Board 101, Nordic & Snowshoe Basics, River Guide Basics. Packages include safety gear, maps, and accessories. We feature shuttles to whisk you up river, to trail heads, and to the mountains. Sierra Adventures has your adventure gear: Clothing, Bikes, Kayaks, Accessories, Tubes, Rafts, Snow Gear, Rentals, Repairs, Lots More. For directions and more information, call Sierra Adventures at 775-323-8928. Make Reservations Prices are per person based on the number of guests. Please call Sierra Adventures at 775-323-8928 for pricing information on different size groups. Advance Reservations Required! Book Adventure Now Important – Read This : Your deposit is only a deposit. You are responsible for the remaining balance, due and payable at least 48 hours before your activity is to begin. One-day adventures require a $50 per person deposit, and two-day adventures require a $100 per person deposit. Fill out the short Deposit Payment form, then click the “Pay Deposit” button. You will then choose your adventure, your preferred date, and go to our secure PayPal system to pay your deposit. You don’t need a PayPal account to use the system. Questions? Call us at 775-323-8928 or e-mail: info@wildsierra.com . Packaging & Pricing Info : All activities offered are designed, supported and packaged by Sierra Adventures. Packages include: An experienced personal guide, top rated rental gear, free transportation, snacks and bottled water, free photos, free outfitting with safety equipment. Pricing is subject to variation due to group size, location, fuel costs & holiday periods. See the Sierra Adventures price list for more information. OUR INSTRUCTORS & POLICIES ACA certified with 25 years experience. Former US Olympic and UC Irvine coach. 100% refund on cancellations 15 days or more before your trip. No refund on cancellations less than 15 days before trip. Date changes $25 per person. Advance Reservations Required! Make A Reservation Now Historical/Leisure and Guided scenic tours abound with choices ranging from Virginia City and Lake Tahoe to a Mark Twain Historic tour. Adventure seekers can even visit the many Ghost Towns located in Northern Nevada. Earth, Wind, and Water tours include horseback expeditions, ATV excursions, rock climbing, hang glide adventures and helitours over Lake Tahoe. The Winter/Spring options feature snow gear and equipment rental and include snowshoes with ski poles, snow tubes and boards. Guided active day trip choices showcase a selection of great ideas to please just about anyone. Chose from dog sledding, sleigh rides, a snow cat powder adventure, or perhaps a snow shoeing tour high above Lake Tahoe will suit your needs. Snowmobiling adventures and intro to ski/snowboard packages are also available. Nevada day trips and activity options are endless in this scenic wonderland. A Balloon Flyaway over Lake Tahoe with views of Yosemite can take anyone’s breath away, or take the family on a Zoo and Wildlife Discovery tour. Brought to you by the knowledgeable (and genuinely nice) staff at Sierra Cyclesmith, this collection is designed to help you spend less time scratching your head over your bike and more time enjoying the ride. Whether you’re a weekend cruiser, a daily commuter, or a backcountry trail chaser, our step-by-step videos break down essential bicycle maintenance, diagnostics, and upgrades into simple, shop-tested techniques. No jargon overload. No snobbery. Just honest tips from the folks who love fixing bikes as much as you love riding them. Tech Tips Video Library Shop Now Firebird Everything You Need to Know The enduro-bred Firebird is danger and daring dialed in. It’s built of carbon and courage, urging you to give in to gravity on the descent and willfully defy it on the climb. With nearly bottomless suspension, it’s so planted it may as well grow roots. Roots that can fly. Look, we don’t get it, either — but you will when you ride it. We’ve dialed up the new Firebird to make it even more aggressive, planted, and efficient. This is no minor tweak to the tuning; we re-engineered the bike from the ground up to improve performance in every dimension. Learn More VLT E-ALL-MOUNTAIN Feel unrestricted full-power performance without the weight The Sight VLT CX is all about balance, boosting riders' confidence to go hard and trust their bike. The high pivot layout combined with 160/150mm travel makes this bike punch above its weight without losing snappy playfulness. Available in three different models, you’ll be able to choose the spec build that best suits your riding style. Continuous development of our VLT lineup means the Sight VLT CX is almost 20% lighter than our previous generation, with a larger battery and improved riding noise, all without compromising on the exceptional torque and power the Bosch CX system is known for. Turbo Kenevo Super Light melds the legendary handling and all-around big trail prowess of the Enduro with our Super Light electric support to deliver indomitable capability, light weight, and power to conquer more and bigger trails. The Turbo Kenevo Super Light puts the "E" in our Enduro, delivering more of what you want from your trail ride, more capability everywhere, more power to climb, more pop when you really need it, more adrenaline. More laps, more jumps, more drops, faster rides with fresher legs. And, it does all this with less. Carrying much less weight than bulkier e-MTBs, the Turbo Kenevo Super Light is hyper-responsive and just as willing and able to redefine big trail performance as our Enduro. Level up your trail game. We spared no expense with the S-Works Turbo Kenevo SL and tricked it out with the absolute best components available including SRAM's premier Eagle AXS XX1 drivetrain; feature-packed FOX Factory suspension; and a super-light, super-tough Roval Traverse SL wheelset. - The Turbo Kenevo Super Light motor/controller system is a full integration of the bike's 250-watt motor and 320Wh battery with a radically advanced and seamlessly integrated controller. The result is massive power delivered, up to 20mph/32kph, to get you to the top of your favorite descent with just half of the effort and much faster, giving even more of the quality ride you yearn for and more of it than ever before possible. - Our next-generation TCU2 is your information hub with customizable display fields, including the exact percentage of battery level, and features our all-new, bar-mounted MicroTune function to adjust power delivery in 10% increments, so you get exactly the support you need to experience precisely the ride you want. - 29-inch wheels front and rear deliver a nimble ride that carves circles around other full-power e-MTBs. A generous cockpit centers you on the bike, optimizing traction and corner control. The low bottom bracket, slack headtube angle and reduced fork offset keep things stable in the rough. - The Turbo Kenevo Super Light geometry can be fine-tuned for wherever and however you ride. Six distinct geometry settings allow easy adjustment to hone performance in any terrain. Head angle can be adjusted between 63 and 65.5 degrees. Bottom bracket height can be fine-tuned up or down by 7mm. We've never made a more adjustable, adaptable trail bike. - The Turbo Kenevo Super Light's 170mm of Enduro-inspired travel is supple on small bumps, devours square-edged hits without a twitch, eats massive G-outs for breakfast, yet still offers amazing pedal response and delivers your power to the ground with total efficiency. - The Turbo Kenevo Super Light's S-Sizing is based on what matters: rider size and style, not inseam. All sizes have similar headtube lengths and standover, allowing you to choose the size that best suits your individual style. Smaller S-Size numbers are going to be nimble and more flickable, while bigger S-Sizes deliver more stability and a roomier ride. Specialized Turbo Vado 3.0 $3,000.00 Vado is the vehicle for everything from daily commutes to fast workouts to longer-than-planned adventures—an electric bike for life. The smoothest-riding e-Bike experience yet, Vado is designed to boldly take on the ever-changing landscape you'll encounter as a daily rider, carry whatever you need it to, and keep you riding more often. Redesigned geometry puts you in the best position for everything from workouts to commutes while comfortably keeping your eyes on busy roads. We took learnings from the speed a road rider seeks and the maneuverability a mountain bike rider needs. The rider's position on the Vado instills confidence and, at the same time, optimizes the rider's ability to efficiently power from A to B. - Turbo Full Power 2.0E motor and 530Wh battery offer an unparalleled riding experience, providing a smooth, seamless, and shockingly quiet amplification of your efforts, up to 28 mph. The integrated controller responds to your pedal inputs resulting in intuitive amplification of your efforts with an incredibly natural feel. - MasterMind and Mission Control - The MasterMind display reveals all relevant info about your ride, allows real-time tuning of support levels, and enables over-the-air updates so that your bike gets better over time. MasterMind seamlessly integrates with the Mission Control app for range optimization tools, advanced tuning, on-ride diagnostics, and more. - Proven Smooth Efficiency - We designed a custom testing mechanism to analyze bumps at even the smallest frequency to increase comfort and vision. That precision, paired with higher volume tires, and an 80 mm suspension fork, will flatten roads before your eyes. - Turbo System Lock - Use the Mission Control app to disable your bike's motor and activate the motion sensor alarm. Once locked, the motor cannot be enabled again except by the owner. - Fully Integrated Removable and Lockable Downtube Battery - Easy to charge, easy to secure. - Equipped with DRYTECH Fenders, LED front and rear lights, and 27kg capacity rear HD Rack. The rear rack is compatible with child bike seats, and the bike is also rated to pull a thru-axle trailer.
