Technical Diving Discover the Thrill and Mystery of Technical Diving with Sierra Diving Center E-Mail DSAT Tec Deep Diver Course Technical diving is NOT for everyone. But for the adventurous few, a whole new world awaits. During the course you'll learn and practice: Gas switch, decompression dives to 165 feet Motor skills required for technical diving Hazard and risk management as well as limits Emergency response skills for tech diving Fundamental skills to further your training in technical diving Cost per Diver : Private Group Tec 40 $1950.00 $1495.00 Tec 45 $1950.00 $1495.00 Tec 50 $1950.00 $1495.00 The course includes all training and certification costs. Required books, required minimum equipment and gas are additional. Rentals available. Prerequisite: PADI Advanced Diver, Rescue Diver, Enriched Air Diver, Deep Diver or equivalent. 100 logged dives. 20 Enriched Air dives. 25 dives deeper than 60 feet. 15 dives deeper than 100 feet. The course is interactive with lots of hands on practice and workshops and 12 dives. At the end of the course You'll be prepared! DSAT Tec Trimix Course The DSAT Trimix Course will provide you the training required to competently and safely utilize breathing gases containing helium for dives that require staged decompression. During the course you will learn about the benefits, hazards, proper procedures and equipment utilized in making oxygen/helium/nitrogen mixture dives. You will make 9 open water dives using trimix and nitrox/oxygen decompression gases. This course can qualify you to a maximum depth of 330 fsw. Cost: Private - $ 3595. 00 Group of 2 or more $2595.00 per diver. Books, Equipment & Gas Additional Prerequisite: DSAT Tec Deep Diver or qualifying, 100 logged open water dives. Course is limited to 3 divers. TDI Advanced Nitrox This course is designed to train you in the benefits, hazards, proper procedures and equipment for utilizing EANx 21 through 100% oxygen. You'll learn and practice using these optimal mixes for making no decompression dives to a maximum depth of 1 3 0 fsw. During the course you'll make 4 dives on one weekend at Lake Tahoe. This course is your first step toward the Decompression Procedures Course and Trimix diving. Cost: - Private $ 1950.00 Group of 2 or more $1495.00 per diver. Books, Equipment & Gas Additional Prerequisite: Enriched Air Diver or Equivalent and 25 logged dives Course is limited to 6 divers. TDI Decompression Procedures This course examines the theory, methods and procedures of planning stage decompression diving. In the program you plan and conduct 4 standard stage decompression dives to a maximum depth of 150 fsw. The class includes information on the most common equipment requirements, gear set-up, decompression techniques, and accelerated decompression mixtures including nitrox and oxygen. Cost: Private - $1950.00 Group of 2 or more $1495.00 per diver. Books, Equipment & Gas Additional Prerequisite: Advanced Nitrox Diver and 25 logged open water dives. Course is limited to 4 divers. TDI Extended Range This course examines the theory, methods and procedures of planning stage decompression diving at the maximum air depth . In the program you plan and conduct 4 standard stage decompression dives to a maximum depth of 1 8 0 fsw. The class includes information on the most common equipment requirements, gear set-up, decompression techniques, and accelerated decompression mixtures including nitrox and oxygen. Cost: Private - $ 1995 .00 Group of 2 or more $1495.00 per diver. Books, Equipment & Gas Additional Prerequisite: Age 18, Decompression Procedures Diver and 100 logged open water dives. 25 dives logged over 100 fsw. Course is limited to 4 divers. TDI Entry Level Trimix The Entry Level Trimix Course will provide you the training required to competently and safely utilize breathing gases containing helium for dives that require staged decompression. During the course you will learn about the benefits, hazards, proper procedures and equipment utilized in making oxygen/helium/nitrogen mixture dives. You will make 4 open water dives using trimix and nitrox/oxygen decompression gases. This course qualifies you to a maximum depth of 200 fsw. Course is limited to 3 divers. TDI Advanced Trimix The Advanced Trimix Course will provide you the training required to competently and safely utilize breathing gases containing helium for dives that require staged decompression. During the course you will learn about the benefits, hazards, proper procedures and equipment utilized in making oxygen/helium/nitrogen mixture dives. You will make 4 open water dives using trimix and nitrox/oxygen decompression gases. This course qualifies you to a maximum depth of 300 fsw. About - Sierra Ski & Cycle Works - Lake Tahoe Ski & Bike Shop Skip to main content Menu Home About Bike Ski Spoke Junkie Contact facebook Close Search About Sierra Ski & Cycle Work Sierra Ski & Cycle Works has been a part of the Lake Tahoe outdoor sports scene, having big fun in the little shop since 1980. Owned by South Lake Tahoe mountain bike pioneer, Gary Bell, this fun & funky shop has been feeding adventure to locals and visitors for generations. “I want to help people understand the roots of Tahoe mountain biking and skiing, and how it has evolved over the past 40 years,” says Bell. A philosophy that landed him a featured article in Bike Magazine. Where It All Began Gary Bell moved to Lake Tahoe for a winter. Forty-six years later, he’s still here. Gary knows a lot about Tahoe bike and ski culture, having owned his shop since 1980 and helping to organize the Tahoe Area Mountain Biking Association in 1988. When asked why he still enjoys turning people on to mountain biking and skiing after 46 years, he just smiles and says, “It’s about time spent in the woods.” It all started more than four decades ago when Gary decided to move to South Lake Tahoe, for just one winter. That one winter turned into 46 years and the beginning of a lifelong love affair with Tahoe. Besides his laid-back style, Gary is serious when it comes to bikes and skis which stems from his years of exploring his backyard. Gary and Chris make it a point to understand the skier or rider, the terrain they prefer, fitness level, and the fun factor expectation. Gary fell in love with the mountains at age four during family ski trips to Alpine Meadows. Seeking more time in the mountains than just weekend ski club trips from the Bay Area, Gary made the move when he turned 20 telling his mom and dad it was just for one ski season. Like any new dedicated ski bum back in 1976 Gary painted houses, shoveled snow off rooftops, towed people off the snow berm, and was a late night cook at the Nugget. Soon he landed a ski teaching gig at Heavenly Valley while at the same time he practiced his aerials off the ski ramp into the lake at Bill O’Leary’s World Freestyle Training Center at Zephyr Cove. During the summer he worked for Frank at Tahoe Bike Shop and at the Clean Machine for Bill Miller. It was then when Gary and long-time friends Geoff Clarke and Gene St. Denis started exploring all the back-country trails on the first Tahoe-made mountain bikes called Clunkers that they built in 1978. Made from beach cruiser frames and big heavy tires, Gary and his buddies would ride their custom-built Clunkers all over, connecting abandoned hiking trails they called the “Cabin Ride” and “Tin Shack Ride.” Following one of their more crazy descents down Saxon Creek, they named the trail Mr. Toad’s Wild Ride – South Shore’s most famous trail to this day. Today, you can still find Gary and Geoff, a certified ski guide, deep in the back-country on their bikes or skis. Gene – still a wild man – continues to turn people onto nature with fishing outings on Lake Tahoe. With old Tahoe memorabilia decorating the walls and busting at the seams, Sierra Ski and Cycle Works is the unofficial official Tahoe bike and ski history museum. You can check out a Tahoe Clunker built by Gary in 1978 and share your own Tahoe trail tails with others at the shop daily. Gary's 1979 Clunker Gear for Kids of All Ages "Big fun in the small shop since 1980" Powder Skis The Evolution of Mountain Sports and the Gear to Get There Sierra Ski and Cycle Works has witnessed first-hand the evolution of the gear for getting into and around the mountains. In some cases, when the innovation didn’t happen fast enough, we did it ourselves. Gary purchased his first cross country skis from Jack Francis of Rock Bottom Sports which is the current location of SSCW. When Jack closed his doors, Gary took over the space in 1980 and created a corporation with two partners that focused on used ski gear. The Ski Trading Company had three locations; one in Kings Beach, Squaw Valley, and its current spot on Hwy 50 in the middle of South Lake Tahoe, next to Safeway. Gary and his friends loved the freedom of back country skiing and soon the shop was retrofitting the soft leather x-c ski boots with downhill boot cuffs to make them stiffer. Always the innovator, Gary created a releasable telemark ski binding in the early 80’s, before Voile. However, he never went anywhere with his original design, except up to Heavenly Valley. Soon he was kicked off the mountain for having an “illegal binding.” After a ski meeting with HV mountain manager, Malcolm Tibbetts, Gary was issued a special pass that gave him permission to ride the lifts and use his newfangled gear. By the mid 90’s, telemark skis and equipment were transformed to handle bigger all-mountain terrain – finally. Like a kid in a candy shop, Gary happily introduced everyone to telemark skiing along with split snowboards to help us get further into the mountains. Today, SSCW remains the quintessential back country ski shop in Lake Tahoe that rents and sells skins, shovels, probes, beacons and avalanche safety & preparedness kits. The Local Shop Is Born In 1983, the corporation changed its name to Sierra Ski and Cycle Works and became a full-service ski and bike shop. SSCW carried SR, Raleigh and Specialized bikes, and became the top Specialized Dealer in Northern California in the mid 80’s. By 1988, mountain biking had taken hold and Gary started TAMBA, the Tahoe Area Mountain Bicycling Association, along with Kathlee and Jesse from North Shore. The three developed a model program driven by volunteers who helped to build trails and educate riders to assist the USFS. Although never called upon, TAMBA even developed a bike search and rescue team, a first in the nation. TAMBA continues strong to this day with a new fresh crew. Gary mastered his technical bike handling skills in the early 1980s when he competed in bike trials next to Hans Rey. Sponsored by Raleigh and Yeti, he placed second in the Worlds and Third in Nationals in the Expert Division. He quit the circuit when it felt like a job. Instead, he prefers to take his friends on epic multi-day bike adventures that, so far, have traversed the Sierra from Tuolumne to Buck’s Lake. Those invited have learned to bring a head lamp, extra clothing, food, positive attitude, Advil and a water pump. Gary can often be spotted riding around town on his vintage penny farthing. This flexibility caters to diverse preferences within the group, accommodating both those seeking a shorter, quick adventure and others opting for a more extended exploration. ​ Scenic Views of Sierra Crest and Palisades Tahoe: Participants can enjoy picturesque views of the Sierra Crest , Palisades Tahoe , and the Tahoe National Forest . The diverse and captivating scenery enhances the overall experience, providing a visually appealing backdrop for the group outing. ​ Equipment Provided for a Hassle-Free Experience: Snowshoes and poles are provided as part of the rental package, eliminating the need for participants to bring their own equipment. This ensures a hassle-free experience for the entire group, especially for those who may not have their own snowshoeing gear . ​ Suitable for Adventurous Beginners: The self-guided tour is labeled as perfect for adventurous beginners, making it an ideal choice for groups with varying levels of experience. This inclusivity allows everyone in the group, regardless of their snowshoeing expertise, to participate and enjoy the winter wonderland. ​ Customizable Adventure with Multiple Loop Options: The Palisades Loops Trail network offers four unique loop options with varying durations, catering to different fitness levels and time constraints. Whether opting for a quick 45-minute loop or a more extensive 3-hour adventure to Palisades Point , participants can customize their experience based on the group's preferences and abilities. ​ What We Provide: Snowshoe and Pole Rentals : Our comprehensive rental package includes top-notch snowshoes and poles , ensuring you have the right gear for your journey. Digital Map with Loop Options: Navigate the snow-covered terrain effortlessly with our digital map of the Palisades Loops, offering four unique loop options suitable for all snowshoeing abilities and time constraints. ​ Choose ho w long an adventure. (45 minute ) The Quick Loop (1 hour) Mini Meadow Loop (2 hour) Frog Meadow Loop (3 hour). Palisades Point Loop If you Choose the longest loop to follow your adventure will take you to Palisades Point, (same as our half day guided tour route ) , reaching the highest and tallest points for panoramic views of Alpine Meadows, and Palisades Tahoe Ski Resorts. Consider Bringing: To make the most of your self-guided snowshoe tour: Appropriate Clothing: Check our packing list located on the bottom of this page for Details on what to bring. Dress in layers, wear waterproof and insulated boots, and bring appropriate jacket for the conditions. Personal Items: Carry a backpack, sunglasses, sunscreen, a hat, water, snacks, and any personal belongings you may need. Camera or Smartphone: Capture the breathtaking winter scenery and memorable moments. Health and Safety Items: Bring any necessary medications. Navigation Tool: Although we provide a digital map, and up-to-date map app on your phone with GPS device, can be useful. Timekeeping Device: Ensure you have a watch or another timekeeping device to track your adventure's duration. Personal Comfort Items: If desired, bring items like hand warmers or a neck gaiter for added comfort. South Lake Tahoe E-Bike Rental FAQ | South Lake E Bikes Home Make A Reservation Our E-Bikes FAQ Repair Contact Home Make A Reservation Our E-Bikes FAQ Repair Contact Explore Lake Tahoe: E-Bike Rental FAQ & Riding Guide South Lake Tahoe E-Bike Rental FAQ Everything you need to know before renting an electric bike at South Lake E Bikes in South Lake Tahoe, CA. Where can I rent e-bikes in South Lake Tahoe? South Lake E-Bikes on 841 Emerald Bay Rd offers premium electric bike rentals near Emerald Bay and the best bike trails in Lake Tahoe. Our bikes are perfect for exploring beaches, scenic viewpoints, and Tahoe bike paths. Head to our Booking Page . Can you ride an e-bike to Emerald Bay? Yes, but with caution. “Our nearby bike trail starts at South Lake E Bikes and ends at Baldwin Beach.” (4.4 miles). It is up to you if you want to continue your path to Emerald Bay on a two lane highway, which is an extra 3.5 mile trek with incline. How much does it cost to rent an e-bike in South Lake Tahoe? South Lake E Bikes offers the best rates in Lake Tahoe. Starting at just $50/day for our most popular bike, we offer the most premium e-bikes! Need a baby carrier or trailer for your kids or dog? We offer it at only $5/day . Can I e-bike around the lake? Literally? Yes. Just need a few extra batteries. As far as around South Lake Tahoe, our e-bikes are one of the best ways to explore South Lake Tahoe because they help riders handle hills, longer distances, and scenic routes with less effort. Do I need experience to ride an e-bike? No experience is needed. Our e-bikes are beginner-friendly and easy to ride. We’ll show you how everything works before your ride starts. What are the best bike trails in Lake Tahoe? Popular bike routes from our shop lead you to Emerald Bay, Pope Beach, Baldwin Beach, Camp Richardson, Fallen Leaf Lake, Angora Lake, and the scenic Tahoe bike path system. All within a radius! For more information on trails, visit TAHOE TRAILS to get more in depth on where you want to ride. How long does an e-bike battery last? All day! Our customers have used our e-bikes from open to close, and come back with some battery left. Battery dead? We will bring you a new battery and/or e-bike. Just call us! Are helmets included with e-bike rentals? Yes! Every South Lake E-Bikes rental includes a helmet for safety and comfort. Can tourists ride e-bikes in South Lake Tahoe? Definitely. E-bikes are perfect for visitors wanting to explore Tahoe without needing intense physical effort. Do you offer family-friendly e-bikes? Yes. We offer comfortable bikes for beginners and availability for kid seat options depending on the season. Billing FAQs Can we book e-bikes online? Yes. RESERVE here to claim your e-bikes. Plan your vacation ahead and reserve today! Do you accept cash or card? Both! All we need is you to sign a waiver, and pay how you like. What happens if we return our e-bikes late? Depends how late you are. We do like to make sure bikes are put away by 6pm, but just call us and we’ll make sure you’re taken care of. Does it cost more for overnight? Yes. For only $25 more, keep it overnight and return in the morning. Cookie Consent We use cookies to improve your experience on our site. By using our site, you consent to cookies. pages.text: South Tahoe Kayak & Paddleboard rentals and tours | Book our [4th of July Fireworks Tour](/tours/4th-july-fireworks-tour/) Now Book our 4th of July Fireworks Tour Now South Tahoe Kayak & Paddleboard rentals and tours south tahoe kayak and paddleboard logo South Tahoe Kayak & Paddleboard Menu Rentals Tours About Us BOOK NOW On Water Rental 1004 Lake View Ave , South Lake Tahoe , CA , 96150 Open Daily: 9 : 30 am - 6 : 00 pm Weather Permitting Parking Lakeview commons beach parking Parking on San Jose Ave Parking near South Lake Tahoe library Parking near Sprouts Cafe Delivery Avaliable from our Tahoe City Location Rental Rates 1 Hour 3 Hours Full Day Single Kayak $32 $64 $96 Double Kayak $48 $96 $110 Paddle board $32 $64 $96 Hobie Eclipse 12.0 $50 $100 $150 South Tahoe Kayak & Paddleboard is the newest venture of Tahoe City Kayak , a paddlesports company that has has assisted in getting thousands of paddlers out on Lake Tahoe since 1997. Even though it’s in the heart of South Lake Tahoe, this new location offers paddlers easy access to a large stretch of pristine, undeveloped beach (known as “Secret Beach”), preserved marshlands filled with wildlife, and the upper Truckee River, which is home to river otters, endangered Lahontan Cutthroat Trout, and many species of birds. This scenic wonder is just a short paddle from our rental beach. All of this is accentuated by the stunning backdrop of Mount Tallac (Tahoe’s highest peak), and the beautiful peaks above Emerald Bay. Cave Rock is also clearly visible from this location. Rentals Our rental tent/kiosk is conveniently located on South Lake Tahoe's Lakeview Commons Beach, and operates 7 days a week (during the summer months) with beach-front rentals and guided tours. rentals BOOK NOW tours BOOK NOW Tours There are lots of reasons to upgrade from a rental to a guided tour or lesson. Some people want to learn about the history and ecology of Lake Tahoe. Others like the safety of knowing that they’ll be paddling with a guide who’s been trained in ACA (American Canoe and Kayak Association) techniques for rescue, water safety, and efficient paddling form. Many of our guests just want to pick up some local knowledge or have our guides entertain the kids with G-rated “Dad Jokes.” Whatever your reason, we feel that upgrading to a guided experience will enhance your Tahoe adventure. Compare Tours Sunset Tour This tour begins 2 hours before sunset. This is a stunning time of day to see Lake Tahoe as the water reflects the vibrant sunset BOOK NOW Get Up Stand Up This one-hour paddle is an affordable way to learn proper technique for stand-up paddle boarding, and a great way to enjoy the lake’s smoothest water BOOK NOW Wild and Scenic Nature tour Enjoy this family-friendly nature paddle while hearing tales of the Wild West from Tahoe’s past. BOOK NOW Emerald Bay Boat Camp Overnight This tour includes a nature paddle in the Upper Truckee River, a hike on Fannette Island, a tour of Vikingsholm, stories and music by the campfire BOOK NOW “ We walked in on a Sunday morning and were able to hop in a kayak immediately. The instructors were helpful, and it was a great experience for the money ” Akshatha Why Paddlers Keep Coming Back What is the best time of day to go paddling? Lake Tahoe is usually fairly windy and wavy from 2:00pm to 6:00pm. Although the West Shore of Lake Tahoe is somewhat sheltered from the wind most days, it’s usually best to paddle in the morning/early afternoon, or at sunset. For a multi-sport day, we recommend planning a morning paddle and hiking or biking for the afternoon. Our “Sunset Kayak Tour” and “Get Up Stand Up” programs are a great way to get on the water outside our normal business hours. Learning Center My Account (530) 582-5781 Ski Tuning and Services Home Ski Tuning and Services Downhill Ski, Nordic Ski & Snowboard Tuning Services Our Service Philosophy At Start Haus, our philosophy is simple: We believe that every skier, regardless of ability, deserves the performance of a World Cup tune. We’ve invested in the world’s most advanced machinery - the Wintersteiger Jupiter, Trim Jet and Wax Future - because we believe in the science of precision. We want your edges to be accurate to the tenth of a degree and your bases to be saturated with infrared technology. As much as we rely on precision and technology we believe in the soul of the craft, because technology is only as good as the technician operating it. That’s why every piece of gear that passes through our machines ends up on our benches for a final hand-check. We aren't just a "factory" shop; we are a local service center where we treat your gear like it’s our own. Our goal is to remove the variables of your equipment so you can focus entirely on the feeling of the perfect turn. Types of Gear We Service We take pride in being the most versatile shop in the Truckee-Tahoe area. Our machinery and our technicians are equipped to handle any gear that slides on the mountain and tune at a World-Cup Race level. Our expertise extends far beyond standard alpine skis; we are proud to service: Snowboards: From park boards and cruisers, to boardercross race boards, powder boards and splitboards. Nordic & Cross-Country Skis: Precision grinds for skate and classic setups. Sit Skis, Ski Bikes, Ski Blades & Monoskis: If it has an edge and a base, we tune and service it! FIS & Junior Race Gear: World Cup-level precision for the next generation of racers. Backcountry & Alpine Touring (AT): Lightweight setups that require specialized care. Alpine Skis : All widths, shapes, sizes and styles. From the beginner one-ski quiver to the World-Cup racer. No matter what you ride, you can trust that it will receive the same elite level of attention and care. The Wintersteiger Jupiter at Start Haus At Start Haus in Truckee, California, we are committed to providing the highest level of service for all your winter gear. That’s why we’ve introduced the Wintersteiger Jupiter, a cutting-edge, fully automated tuning system designed to deliver unmatched precision. This state-of-the-art machine represents a significant leap forward from traditional tuning methods, utilizing a fully digital system to ensure your equipment is optimized for the snow. Digital Edge Angle Adjustments: One of the standout features of the Jupiter is its digital edge control. Unlike older technologies, limited by fixed increments, our new system allows for incredibly precise edge angle adjustments. This level of customization ensures that whether you are a World Cup racer or a weekend enthusiast, your edges are tuned exactly to your specifications. Base Grinding: The Jupiter allows for variable pressure technology during the grinding process. As the stone moves across the base of your skis, the machine can automatically adjust the pressure along a curve, allowing us to pinpoint the exact pressure needed throughout the length of the ski for a consistent and professional finish. The Jupiter also brings incredible efficiency to our shop with its dual-grind feature, which allows us to pre-grind a pair of skis simultaneously, doubling our production speed compared to previous methods. This versatility extends to all types of gear; the machine is fully equipped to handle snowboards and even Nordic skis. For Nordic skiers, the Jupiter can pattern the entire length of a skate ski or intelligently avoid the skin and scale sections on classic skis to preserve their performance. Sidewall Planer: To ensure a professional, factory-level finish, the Jupiter includes a sidewall planer with a trim-cut feature to remove excess material and a ceramic disc polishing unit that deburrs the ski with linear precision. Final Hand Work: While the machine produces a finish that is nearly "ready-to-ride," our expert techs still bring every piece of gear to the bench for final hand-work - checking the equipment, detuning, and deburring-to guarantee it is perfect before it hits the snow. Wintersteiger Infrared Waxing by Wax Future At Start Haus, we know that a great tune is only as good as the wax that makes it glide. To provide the ultimate glide and base protection, we utilize the Wintersteiger Wax Future, a high-end infrared waxing unit that goes far beyond traditional hot wax. This technology is designed for those who want their wax to last longer and perform better, whether you are touring the backcountry or racing a World Cup. The secret to the Wax Future is its infrared heating technology. Unlike traditional waxing irons that apply high heat to the surface of the ski, the infrared lamps penetrate the base material deeply and evenly without physical contact. This non-contact heating allows the pores of the ski base to open up more effectively, drawing the wax deep into the material rather than just letting it sit on the surface. This process results in several key benefits for your equipment.

We got you! Rental Equipment Rental packages include skis/snowboard, boots, poles, and a helmet. A complete line of rental equipment is available at the Main Lodge Rental shop, including basic and performance equipment featuring Atomic + K2 skis and Nitro snowboards. Book online for a fast and efficient rental process. Book Now Tuning Shop Rental Types + Rates Sport Sport skis and snowboards for beginner and intermediate riders provide the perfect balance of value and quality. Ideal for those taking lessons or new to the sport, these options ensure a great start on the mountain. Packages start at $55 Reserve Now Performance Performance skis and snowboards are for advanced riders. Curated by Sugar Bowl staff, high-performance brands and models ensure you’re ready for any condition and terrain. Atomic skis available. Nitro & K2 snowboards available. You can select to upgrade to Performance Rentals, on-site when you check in at the Main Lodge Rental Shop. Packages for $90 Upgrade On-Site Rental Equipment Rates Adult Sport Package (ski or snowboard) ages 13+ $75 Book Now Child Sport Package (ski or snowboard) ages 12 & under $55 Book Now Adult Performance Package (ski or snowboard) ages 13+ $90 Upgrade at Rental Shop Packages include skis, boot & poles or snowboard with bindings and boots. Plus a helmet ($25 value) Main Lodge Rental Shop The Main Lodge Shop offers rentals and repair services for both Sport and Performance Rental Equipment. The shop is conveniently located steps from the slopes, so there is no gear schlepping required. Open daily, Ski + Snowboard Tuning Conveniently located on the snow, just outside Main Lodge. Drop off your equipment for the following services: Edge Sharpening Hot Wax Belt Wax Binding Mount (Alpine) Binding Adjustments (Alpine) Open daily, Additional Information Where is the rental shop located? > The Rental Shop is located on the 2nd level of Main Lodge, right next to the retail shop. What time should I arrive? > Guests getting rentals should arrive at least 30 minutes before you would like to be on the snow. If you are taking a lesson please arrive at least one-hour in advance. The rental shop opens at 8:00am and is generally the busiest from 9:00am - 11:00pm. Where can I store my stuff? > Day use lockers are available, adjacent to the rental shop. Small and large lockers are available and can be paid for with a credit or debit card. Do I have to reserve my rentals online? > To guarantee availability, we recommend reserving your rentals online before you arrive. Day-of rentals will be offered on a first-come, first-served basis and are subject to availability. Do you rent just boots or just skis/snowboard? > Yes. At the Rental Shop, you can rent boots, boards, skis, poles, and helmets individually with an à la carte option. Please note that if you rent boots only, your ski bindings will need to be adjusted to fit the boots and set your DIN, which requires an additional fee. Do you rent other items like clothing and goggles? > No. Sorry, we do not rent clothing or goggles. We have a selection of items available for purchase at the retail shop next door. Sugar Bowl’s 2026/27 Seasonal Programs are your pass to growth, community, and unforgettable days on the mountain. From youth and adult season-long programs to skills-focused clinics and camps, train with the same coaches and groups all season. You’ll build skills and friendships in a fun, no-pressure environment. With options for ages 4 and up, there’s a perfect fit for every member of the family. Description Explore the North Shore at your own pace with kayak rentals in North Lake Tahoe from Tahoe Vista Recreation Area. Our rental program is built for visitors who want a simple, self-guided way to spend time on the water. Launch directly from the beach in Tahoe Vista and paddle along the shoreline while taking in the clear water, mountain views, and scenery that make this stretch of the North Shore worth exploring. Whether you want a quick hour on the lake or a longer outing, you set the pace. Kayak rentals are available daily from Tahoe Vista Recreation Area. Guests can reserve in advance or stop by for select walk-in availability, and all rentals include core safety equipment. Join us and Kayak or Paddle Board the crystal clear waters of Lake Tahoe on your own schedule with a rental or join one of our Lake Tahoe Kayak or SUP tours. Ask about our Kayak and SUP delivery service as well as our Special Multiday and Group Rental Rates! Rentals launch from Tahoe Vista Recreation Area at 7010 North Lake Blvd in Tahoe Vista. What types of kayaks are available? Guests can choose from single kayaks or double kayaks depending on their group size and preference. Can beginners rent a kayak here? Yes. This is a great option for casual paddlers looking for an easy, self-guided outing on the lake. Guests should be comfortable on the water and able to swim. How long can I rent a kayak? Rental options range from 1 hour to 24 hours, depending on availability. Do I need a reservation? Reservations can be made up to 24 hours in advance but aren’t required. One-hour rentals are available for walk-ins only. What’s included with the rental? All kayak rentals include the kayak, paddle, and life jacket. What should I bring? We recommend a reusable water bottle, sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses with a strap, water shoes, swimwear, a towel, and a dry change of clothes. Is parking available? Yes. Street parking and a lot at Tahoe Vista Recreation Area are both available. The lot charges a daily fee. What’s the difference between a kayak rental and a guided tour? Rentals are self-guided — you choose your own route and pace. Guests who want instruction, a planned route, and local insight should consider a guided option like the Clear Kayak Tour. Our paddleboard rentals are based at the Tahoe Vista Recreation Area on the North Shore of Lake Tahoe, offering easy beach access and calm water ideal for paddling. Do I need prior experience to rent a paddleboard? No experience is necessary. Stand up paddleboarding is beginner-friendly, and our staff will provide a brief orientation to help you get comfortable before heading out. What’s included with my rental? Each rental includes a paddleboard, paddle, and a properly fitted personal flotation device (PFD). We’ll also provide basic instruction and safety guidance. How long can I rent a paddleboard? We offer flexible rental durations, typically including hourly rentals and extended time options. Ask us about half-day or full-day availability. 3rd hour is free! What should I wear or bring? Bring a small cooler with lunch and your swim goggles! Is there an age limit? Paddlers of all ages are welcome, but minors must be accompanied by an adult or have a guardian sign a waiver. Youth should be comfortable in the water. Is it safe for beginners? Yes. Tahoe Vista Recreation Area is known for its relatively calm, shallow waters, making it a great spot for first-time paddlers. Our team will review safety tips before you launch. Do I need a reservation? Baldwin Beach 6.9 miles This popular electric bike route takes you to Baldwin Beach, a beautiful sandy beach with stunning views of the Sierra Nevada mountains. Enjoy a rewarding ride and make sure to keep an eye out for wildlife; ospreys, hawks and even eagles. And if you spot a black bear, bring us a photo! San Francisco, CA FAQs About Bike Rentals in South Lake Tahoe Below you'll find some of the most frequently asked questions. Visit our FAQs Page for more answers. What is the best bike rental in South Lake Tahoe? Tahoe Bike Company is a top-rated local favorite, known for its wide selection of e-bikes, family-friendly options, and easy access to scenic trails. How much does it cost to rent an e-bike in Tahoe? E-bike rentals typically start around $29 per hour, with half-day and full-day options available. See detailed pricing on the Rentals Page. What is the best value? Renting DeLuxe e-bikes for half a day (4 hours) is $54, or less than the cost of twice the hourly rate, for a bike that includes manyfeatures, such as basket, phone holder, lights, pedal assist, key lock. How long does it take to ride to Baldwin Beach from your shop and back? It takes 50 to 60 minutes to ride to Balwin Beach on an e-bike, more on a regular bike. If you stop for a sandwich or an ice cream at Camp Richardson, or take your time to enjoy the scenery, the beach, and take photos, it may take 3 hours or so. Are e-bikes worth it in Lake Tahoe? Yes, e-bikes make it easy to ride longer distances and enjoy Tahoe's scenic routes without fatigue. Why is Tahoe Bike Company so well rated? The Company main focus is on fun and safety for couples, friends, and families. Helmets and trailers are available and an expert staff will recommend the type of bike and bike paths to fit everyone's skill level. Our aggregate rating on Google is 4.8 but since the new ownership took over a year ago we have had over 60 reviews all at 5.0. Where can I ride near Tahoe Bike Company? Anywhere! The South Lake Tahoe extensive bike trail network runs right by the shop. From there you can easily ride to multiple beaches like Cove East, Kiva Beach, Baldwin Beach, Camp Richardson, and scenic bike paths through forests and meadows. Do I need to make a reservation in advance? While walk-ins are welcome, we recommend booking in advance, especially during weekends and holidays to guarantee availability, particularly for DeLuxe E-bikes and Fat Tire E-bikes. Reservations must be made at least 24 hours in advance. If you are less than 24 hours, simply come in and we will do our best to accommodate you. What should I bring with me for my ride? We suggest bringing sunscreen, water, comfortable clothing, and a phone or map if you're exploring longer routes. Helmets and locks are included with all rentals but feel free to bring your own. Are helmets required? Helmets are required for riders under 18 and for all throttle equipped e-bikes such as Fat tire e-bikes, Power e-bikes and Cargo e-bikes, but we strongly recommend to use a helmet for all bikes. We provide them free with every rental. Can kids ride their own bikes or ride along with an adult? Yes! We have kid-sized bikes as well as trailers, tag-alongs, and child seats so the whole family can enjoy the ride together. Kids under 14 must be accompanied by an adult. What types of bikes do you offer for rent? We offer a wide range of top brand bikes like Aventon, Fuji, or BESV, including all-trail and comfort e-bikes, power e-bikes, fat tire e-bikes, cargo e-bikes,

Boat Rental Agreement. All the Information you need. Home About us Boats FAQs Contact us Services Book now Skip to content Home About us Boats FAQs Contact us Services Book now FAQs Boat Rental Agreement. According to the boat rental agreement the renter agrees to: Operate the boat in DAYLIGHT hours only. Dock, anchor or secure the boat and equipment to prevent damage to the boat, motor, equipment and/or dock boat and persons as a result of existing or changing weather conditions. Follow any and all Federal, Maritime and Local Laws. Driver must be present and sign responsibility for the watercraft and have a valid driver’s license. The person signing the boat rental agreement must be the only person operating the vessel. Check boats out and in during daylight hours. Strictly enforce boat safety and capacity limits. Boat is only rented after safety protocols have been explained to renter(s) as per watercraft regulations and guidelines. The rental does not include gas or oil consumed unless stated otherwise by the rental agent. Return the boat, motor and equipment in like condition as when boat was taken. Renter is fully responsible for all damages and/or losses to the boat, motor and equipment. To hold owner and rental agent of this boat, motor and equipment harmless and free of liability for any damage occurring to renter, passengers or other persons, or property for any causes arising from the operation and control of the boat, motor and equipment. The boat rental period starts at the scheduled time. Please plan to arrive at least 30 minutes before your start time so that you can get the proper instructions on operating the vessel and sign the boat rental agreement. No excuses for being late or not following the instructions on how to get to the meeting spot will be considered. Thank you for your understanding and we appreciate your business! How far in advance should we make our reservation? About a week is generally enough to reserve a boat . However, our reservations go by quick, so call us as soon as you can to guarantee yours, especially for Holiday and summer vacations! Where do you operate from? We are located in Incline Village, NV but boats are available for use at any point in lake Tahoe with depth enough to accommodate the boat at the Lake. We also offer delivery services to any lake of your choice for an additional fee. How does fuel for the boat work? We include the cost of fuel in the regular rental price. If discount is applied the renter/s will have to pay the amount of gas they spent at the daily rate at any of the Marina’s. Our rental staff will estimate the amount of fuel used. Since this is an estimation you pay the amount, we payed when we brought the boat at the gas station. Do you have life vests for children? We have a variety of life vest from infant size to adult large size, so let us know on the day of your reservation the number and sizes of vests you need. What parts of the lake do you deliver to? We can deliver the boats to any part of lake if safe to do so. Since we value our time and we know you value yours too, make sure you are punctual for your reservation. We do have a fee for delivery which is $99 each way. This is to cover the cost of getting the boat to your Dock, Buoy, or Launch point of your choice. Can I tow the boat myself? Yes, if you feel comfortable towing the boat behind your truck or SUV and are confident with launching and loading the boat. However, keep in mind that you agree to take a full responsibility for the boat, motor, equipment for the rental period and will be charged for damages, if there are any. Can I pick which location and boat I want? Absolutely, reserve early enough and you can pick the boat and location you want to go to. However, we reserve the right to substitute a like kind and size of watercraft in the event of a break down or boat out of service. Do I need to pay for parking at the lake? We are located in Incline Village, NV and there are complementary parking options. Most meeting spots on lake Tahoe do offer free parking as well. Can we bring a dog? We prefer not to because dogs are not welcome at our pickup sites and can be harsh on the interiors. If you have a small dog that you can easily carry to and from the boat, we will allow it for an additional $100 deposit. Can I bring food and drinks on board? Yes, but stay away from messy foods and things that melt. When choosing drinks, resalable options are best. Try to stay away from glass bottles. We will charge you a minimum of $100 for returning an excessively messy boat and remember you can still get a DUI on a boat, so no excessive drinking please! Does the boat have a Bimini? This is the canvas that provides shade over head on the boat. Yes, all boats have some type of Bimini . Does the boat have a stereo? All boats have a stereo, and most have i-pod jacks. We have well maintained boats, but because boat radios are notoriously touchy we do not Guarantee the radio will work. What happens to my deposit if the weather is bad or I can’t make it for the reservation? The minimum deposit is 50%. We take the deposit on the day of the reservation and charge the rest on the day of the rental. We will not allow our boats to go out in unsafe conditions. If you need to cancel you will receive 100% of your deposit if 14 + days out. If between 14-7 days out you will receive a credit of the full deposit amount for the future. 7-4 days before your reservation you will receive your deposit back, minus processing fees, unless we can reschedule. Less than 4 days, we keep the deposit. 24 hours or less you will be charged full amount for your reservation. If Mother Nature makes it unsafe to get on the lake you receive your deposit, minus processing fees, unless we can reschedule. Then your full deposit will be counted towards the rescheduled date. This is the fairest way we’ve come up with to ensure all parties are treated fairly. Commons Beach offers easy access to Lake Tahoe with free parking, and a location that's very close to most of the major hotels in North Lake Tahoe. Additionally, Commons Beach hosts a weekly Farmer's Market and free concerts on Sunday afternoons. Paddle with Confidence While we have a selection of both beginner-oriented and advanced kayaks in our rental fleet, the majority of our watercraft are wide, stable, and confidence-inspiring. Customers with little to no kayak experience, and families with kids, find our kayaks are easy to succeed on. Family-Friendly Fun on the Lake Kids need to be at least 5 years old to paddle in a double kayak with an adult, and 10 years old to paddle their own single kayak or paddle board. All minors need to be under the supervision of an adult while using our equipment. This means that their parent or guardian needs to paddle with them, or keep them close to shore (and within view) of the beach where the parent is hanging out. Our location on Tahoe City's Commons Beach makes it easy for parents to watch their kids as they paddle in the large, shallow bay in front of a sandy beach. Commons Beach, and the adjacent Northwest shore of Lake Tahoe, is one of the most wind-protected areas of the lake, offering fewer waves to navigate than the rest of the lake. Also, Commons Beach has a large, shallow area that extends hundreds of feet out from shore, making it easy to hop back on your kayak or paddleboard in the (extremely unlikely) event that you capsize. We make getting out on Lake Tahoe easy, safe, and hassle-free. Whether you’re looking for a rental, a guided tour, or a personal kayak or paddleboard of your own, our experienced staff is ready to help. We have two beach-front rental locations at the water’s edge, both with free parking and easy access. If you’re staying in North Lake Tahoe or Truckee, please proceed on this website for paddling experiences at Tahoe City’s main town beach, “Commons Beach.” If you’re staying in South Lake Tahoe, visit our southtahoekaykak.com site for paddling experiences at South Lake’s “El Dorado Beach.” Our family friendly location at Commons Beach in Tahoe City is the closest location to most North Tahoe’s major hotels, including the hotels in Palisades Tahoe ski resort. Commons Beach offers a shallow water launch and better natural protection from wind and waves than many other Tahoe beaches, so it’s perfect for kayakers and paddleboarders of any skill level. This beach also offers a playground, BBQ pits, a Thursday Farmers Market, free live music performances on Sundays, and it’s within walking distance of popular restaurants. rentals BOOK NOW tours BOOK NOW Let Us Be Your Guide to Tahoe Adventure There are lots of reasons to upgrade from a rental to a guided tour or lesson. Some people want to learn about the history and ecology of Lake Tahoe. Others like the safety of knowing that they’ll be paddling with a guide who’s been trained in ACA (American Canoe and Kayak Association) techniques for rescue, water safety, and efficient paddling form. Many of our guests just want to pick up some local knowledge or have our guides entertain the kids with G-rated “Dad Jokes.” Whatever your reason, we feel that upgrading to a guided experience will enhance your Tahoe adventure. We carry the best names in kayaks, stand up paddleboards, gear and apparel. Our Store and our retail prices are competitive with big-city retailers! We carry popular kayaks brands such as hobie , eddyline , bote , Kokopelli , Advanced Elements , Mocean , Hurricane and paddleboard brands such as bote , tahe , pau hana , sic , BIC , Aqua Marina . Lynx Relish the power of pedal propulsion, in both forward and reverse. The effortless speed of the MirageDrive 180 with Kick-Up Fins. Breeze Wing features ultra-light, durable and extremely rigid construction for performance typically found only in rigid boards, travel-ready and easy to store “ We just returned back east from a glorious week in Lake Tahoe. The weather was superb with constant blue sky, warm days and cool nights and the prevailing mood was uplifting with the fire contained, the residents cohesive and the Fourth of July fireworks on the lake spectacular. Yet even with the great hiking, fun sailing, terrific dining and frequent drinking, the highlight of our trip was a private kayak tour starting at Sand Harbor with Tim and Molly. The lake was like glass, the sun was warm, the exercise invigorating but the information we learned about Lake Tahoe and the surrounding area and mostly the camaraderie of the instructors was something we will never forget. The memory will bring smiles and laughter to us for a long time. ” Thank You Dr Elissa Savrin and Dr Mack Jacobs Why Paddlers Keep Coming Back What is the best time of day to go paddling? Lake Tahoe is usually fairly windy and wavy from 2:00pm to 6:00pm. Although the West Shore of Lake Tahoe is somewhat sheltered from the wind most days, it’s usually best to paddle in the morning/early afternoon, or at sunset. Rooted in freeride with a side of all-mountain and a dash of art by Chris Benchetler, the celebrated Bent 100 has been reimagined from tip to tail. Incorporating performance feedback from athletes, the Bent 100 features a Light Woodcore and Powder Rocker with 5% more rocker for more tail pop and easier transitioning to switch. Freeride specific HRZN 3D tip delivers improved float in deeper snow and better handling in variable conditions. MAVERICK 96 CTI (129-96-114.5) 18m@179 (TC,TR) Wood/Carbon/Titanal . A ski without boundaries, the powerful Atomic Maverick 96 CTI is a wildly versatile all-mountain ski that can handle every slope and snow condition. Employing All-Mountain Rocker with early rise in the tip for total versatility and a Power Woodcore for added stability and vibration damping at speed, the 96mm waist of the Maverick 96 CTI offers precision performance on hardpack and beyond. BLIZZARD ANOMALY 94 (132.5-94-114.5) 17m@176 (TC) Wood/Metal. Let’s face it: Not every day is a powder day. A wolf in sheep’s clothing, the 94 is narrow enough to rail groomers but still packs enough to get it done anywhere on the hill, with a redesigned wood core and all-new metal layup. An Anomaly by experience – The Anomaly 94 is No Ordinary ride. ANOMALY 88 (127.5-88-109.5) 16.5m@176 (TC,SV) Wood/Metal. Born to defy the ordinary, the Anomaly 88 is the ski you reach for when the day is shaping up to be anything but ordinary. Packing a redesigned wood core and all-new metal layup, the 88 is just as at home devouring groomers as it is smashing bumps or disappearing into the woods. RUSTLER 11 (140-112-130) 19m@180 (TC) Wood/Metal/Carbon. The Rustler 11 is as predictable as it’s balanced. This is an intuitive ski that feels right when connected to the body. The Rustler’s flared tail coupled with its solid construction that fans of Blizzard expect creates a ski that is equal parts playful and dynamic. It changes modes depending on where you’re skiing and how you approach terrain. Stop asking, because the 11 is our answer. RUSTLER 10 (133.5-102-122.5) 16.5m@174 (TC,TR,SV,TRW) Wood/Metal/Carbon. This quiver-killer is back with a vengeance, fueled by an energetic new construction. It’s designed to provide stability and strength underfoot, yet retain all the playfulness you’ve come to love and expect in the tip and tail of a Rustler. From hunting glory pow in the trees to showing off under the lift, now more than ever, the Rustler 10 is built to send. RUSTLER 9 (129-96-118.5) 16m@174 (ALL) Wood/Metal/Carbon. The nimblest of the Rustler series, the Rustler 9, doesn’t necessarily need a powder day to make yours. Whether you’re ripping through the trees or laying trenches back to the lift for another go, these skis are built for fun. DYNASTAR M-FREE 108 (138-108-128) 17m@178 (TC) Hybrid Wood/PU core. Drop in with confidence. The Dynastar M-Free 108 hits the sweet spot for float, agility and control. Playful and responsive Progressive Rocker features a long rise in the tip and tail for a surfy feel in a range of conditions. M-FREE 100 (130–100–122) 17m@178 (TC, TRW) Hybrid Wood/PU/Titanal core. The new M-Free 100 blends playfulness and power in a versatile, everyday ski. This ski delivers a ride that’s lively and energetic while also providing a damp and solid feel when tipped on edge. This results in a large sweet spot that allows the pilot to decide when it’s time to view the mountain as a playground or lay top-to-bottom trenches. M-PRO 94Ti (128-94-118) 17m@178 (TC, SV, TRW) Hybrid Wood/PU/Titanal core. The Dynastar M-Pro 94 Ti skis are your ticket to ride the whole mountain. Frontside carves and backside exploration come naturally for this playful freeride ski. Its blend of full sidewall construction, a progressive rocker profile and an engineered titanal layer pack a lively blend of power and agility for making tracks anywhere on the mountain. M-CROSS 88 (135-88-117) 14m@176 (TC) Hybrid Wood/PU core. The Dynastar M-Cross 88 allows advanced and expert skiers bring their skiing to the next level. At 88mm underfoot, they offer a narrower platform for charging the piste while channeling the all-mountain feel of a freeride ski for occasionally exploring new terrain. Whether you prefer a wider footprint for everyday skiing at the resort or are looking for all-mountain versatility for changing conditions, the Ripstick 96 is recognized for its ability to turn good times on the hill into great memories. The Ripstick 88 is slim enough to slice and dice early morning corduroy and wide enough to negotiate new snow with quickness, rebound, and easily attainable power thanks to its light weight. Piste or powder, good or bad weather, any kind of snow: The Ranger 96 is ready for every sort of all-mountain adventure. Its optimally balanced construction lets it handle any type of terrain. The Karuba-Beech wood core and dual layers of Titanal ensure a strong yet flexible construction that adapts to your skiing style. Whether you’re skiing down a groomed slope or navigating through fresh powder, the KORE 100 Ti delivers fun and playfulness in every condition. Season Passes & Day Tickets Home » Season Passes During the winter months, anyone skiing or snowshoeing on the trail system must have either a day ticket or a season pass, including dogs. We kindly request that skiers and snowshoers keep their trail passes and/or tickets visible and easily accessible while using the trails. Skiers ages (0-12) and (76+) ski for free, but must acquire a complimentary day ticket. Skiers aged (70-75) who do not choose to purchase a season pass or Legacy pass will be required to purchase a day ticket. Season Passes Adult Season Pass (19-69) On Sale! $399 Purchase Details Senior Season Pass (70-75) On Sale! $119 Purchase Details Lifetime Legacy Pass (Adult 70+) $399 A one-time purchase, the Legacy Pass is valid for the user’s lifetime. Restricted to Ages 70+ Purchase Details Kids Season Pass (0-12) Free Details Teen Season Pass (13-18) $99 Purchase Details Super Senior Season Pass (76+) Free Purchase Details Team Athlete Season Pass Free Ages (13-18) Eligibility is limited to active members of a recognized Nordic ski program. Proof of enrollment may be required. Purchase Details Dog Season Pass $139 Purchase Details Dog owners agree to rules and regulations upon purchasing season pass. Glide Pass (19+) On-Site Equipment Rental Pass $225 Purchase Details Glide passes do not include trail access. Pass holders must possess a valid Day Ticket or Season Pass. 2026-2027 Season Pass Newsletter 2026-2027 Season Pass FAQs Day Ticket Packs 5-Day Flex Pack $220 Purchase Details Buy 4, Get 1 Free! Fully Transferrable for the 2026-2027 Season Only 10-Pack Day Tickets $440 Purchase Details Save $110 on a Tahoe XC 10-Pack. Fully transferrable and does not expire! Day Tickets Non-passholders ages 13-75 must purchase a Day Ticket to use the trails in Winter. Complimentary day tickets are available for Kids ages (0-12) and Seniors (76+). Day tickets are good for one day of trail use at Tahoe XC. Day tickets must be purchased in-person, are non-refundable, and non-transferable. We do not sell day tickets online or in advance. Rentals and lessons sold separately. Snowshoe Rentals Day Tickets, Rentals, and Lessons Adult (19-69) season passes include access to Tahoe XC trails as well as: A complimentary cookie/coffee card Two complimentary day tickets to Tahoe XC to share with family and friends Access to Tahoe City Winter Sports Park cross-country trails. 2 Day Tickets* to Tahoe Donner Cross-Country Ski Center *Offer not available Saturdays or Sundays, and not during holiday periods. NEW! Tahoe XC Glide Pass – Limited Quantity Available! *Currently Available for Adults (19+) only* The Tahoe XC Glide Pass is your all-access ticket to our on-site rental fleet —all season long. Whether you’re new to skiing, a frequent traveler, or just looking to explore different ski options before investing in a setup of your own, this pass will be your most valuable asset. With only 40 passes available , Glide Pass holders will enjoy use of snowshoes or cross-country skis, poles, and boots (ski rentals only). Choose from any ski in our rental fleet—classic or skate—ready to perform in the day’s conditions. Perfect for: New skiers exploring the sport Travelers who want to skip the hassle of bringing gear In-market skiers who want to try different ski styles and setups before purchasing Anyone interested in cross-country skiing without the upfront gear investment Our experienced staff will work with you each visit to match you with the ideal ski setup for the terrain and snow conditions—whether you’re just starting out or dialing in your technique. Please note: All gear must stay on-site and cannot be taken home . Other restrictions apply. Tahoe XC reserves the right to limit rentals based on availability and the Glide Pass does not include Demo Ski Rentals or Trail Access. Lifetime Legacy Season Pass For Tahoe XC Community Members Age 70+ The Lifetime Legacy Pass is a one-time purchase for skiers and snowshoers aged 70 and above to make a lasting investment in Tahoe XC. This exclusive pass grants permanent, unlimited access to our trails—for life. More than just a pass, this is a meaningful way to give back. By purchasing a Lifetime Legacy Pass, our most experienced and passionate community members support Tahoe XC’s mission and operations—helping fund trail grooming, equipment rentals, and maintenance. In essence, this pass honors those who have made skiing and snowshoeing a lifelong pursuit, while allowing them to support future generations of outdoor enthusiasts. Important: We will be honoring last year’s Legacy Pass price of $300 for trail users turning 70 during the 2026-2027 winter season ( born between January 1st, 1957 – March 31st, 1957). This offer will expire on March 31st, 2027, and the standard price for the Legacy Pass ($399) will apply for all pass holders ages 70-75. Access to Tahoe XC will remain free for seniors ages 76+ . Skiers aged (70-75) who do not choose to purchase a season pass or Legacy pass will be required to purchase a day ticket. How to Register for Tahoe City Winter Snow Park as a Tahoe XC Pass Holder Purchase your Tahoe XC season pass online or at Tahoe XC. Email Tahoe City PUD Recreation Office at recreation@tcpud.org and include a copy of your Tahoe XC season pass receipt. Or, call the TCPUD at 530-583-3440 (ext. 2) and arrange a time to physically provide proof of purchase. Once you are established in the TCPUD system as a Tahoe XC pass holder, you will be able to use the Tahoe City Winter Sports Park. Review TCPUD Winter Sports Park rules before arriving for hours, reservation guidelines and rules of use. Rad Runner 3+ Electric Trike Rental (Hourly / Half Day / Full Day) Equipment / Pet Trailers, Pet Carriers, Belongings Baskets are available while supplies last. Includes: Phone holder, rear storage bungee and / or straps, water bottle holder, properly sized helmet, combination style bike lock. Staring at $65 half day / $100 full day Weight capacity is 415 pounds. Height range is 4’10”-6’4”. Clear Kayak Tour Daily at Sand Harbor During our tour you will get the chance to encounter Lake Tahoe from a whole new perspective. We will spend 2 hours on the lake exploring the beautiful sandy eastern shoreline and viewing some of the most photographed and iconic granite boulders on the lake. Includes: Clear kayaks, Paddles, Lifejackets, Dry Bags, Shuttle into the Park (even when the park is closed) and Park Entrance Fee. Starting at $150 per Person. Double Kayak 1 Day (up to 24 hr) Includes: kayak, paddle, seat, dry bag, life jackets, straps for transport $75.00/Day Roof padding and straps are included if necessary, and we demonstrate how to do it 😉 Stable and can carry up to 500 pounds (dogs, kids …), can also be paddled as a single. Double Inflatable Kayak 1 Day (up to 24 hr) Includes: kayak, pump, paddle, seats, dry bag, life jackets. $75.00/Day Stable and can carry up to 500 pounds (dogs, kids …), weighs 34 lbs Double Inflatable Kayak 1 Day (up to 24 hr) Includes: kayak, pump, paddle, seats, dry bag, life jackets. $75.00/Day Stable and can carry up to 500 pounds (dogs, kids …), weighs 30 lbs Single Inflatable Kayak 1 Day (up to 24 hr) Includes: kayak, pump, paddle, seats, dry bag, life jackets. $60.00/Day Stable and can carry up to 300 pounds (dogs, kids …), weighs 24 lbs Single Kayak 1 Day (up to 24 hr) Includes: kayak, paddle, seat, dry bag, life jackets, straps and padding for transport $60.00/Day We demonstrate how to do it, carrys up to 350 pounds, can stack two and sometimes three on a roof Stand Up Paddleboard 1 Day (up to 24 hr) Includes: SUP, paddle (for sup and kayak), kayak seat , dry bag, life jackets, pump, backpack $60.00/Day Can carry up to 350 pounds, can easily fit four in a sedan, 6 in an SUV, wieghs 28 pounds Many of our Guests choose Inflatable Kayak/SUP Hybrids enabling them to cherrypick the best beaches all around Tahoe. They come rolled up into a backpack and are ready for short hikes to quiter, more remote destinations. We have complimentary Dog Lifejackets 😉 SAND HARBOR – Sand Harbor can regularly reach 2/3 parking capacity and closes to new parking visitors until later in the afternoon (3-5pm ish). Guests wanting to get to sand harbor can ride the East Shore Express located 100m from our store with Inflatable Models, or Bike into the park from our store even when the park is closed to cars! We allow our guests to pick up rental equipment the evening before their rental so they can get into Sand Harbor early if that is their plan. PARKING along the East Shore of Lake Tahoe – Park Parallel, outside of the No Parking Zones (even if 20 other cars do, there is no safety in numbers, they will all get tickets!), keep your tires off the white (fog) line, mark your parking spot with a pin on your map so you can find it on the way back, take any one of the unmarked trails leading to the lake. East Shore BATHROOMS are located at Chimney Beach Parking lot, Secret Cove parking lot, half way between it secret cove, and just passed creek beach there is a port o pottie. East Shore Beaches – Hidden Beach, Spooners Cove, Memorial Point cove, Sand Harbor (boat Beach, Divers Cove, Main Beach), Bonsai Rock, Lady Bug Beach, Cave Beach, Thunderbird Beach, Pi Rock, Chimney Beach, Secret Cove, Speedboat Beach, Creek Beach, Whale Beach, and Skunk Harbor. LIABILITY FORM Kayak & Paddleboard Shop WELCOME TO TAHOE PADDLE & OAR Your location for superior kayak & standup paddleboard rentals in Lake Tahoe. We provide High Quality Kayak & Paddleboard Rentals, Guided Tours, Sales, and Delivery Services so you can enjoy getting on the water. Lake Tahoe offers the most beautiful crystal clear water in the country, and a paddle adventure is the best way to enjoy it! We offer rentals perfect for individuals or groups, and our rental equipment is ready to go at the water’s edge when you arrive. Our beach crew will assist you with your gear so you don’t have to worry about lifting heavy equipment. Your fun and memorable paddle experience is our top priority and the reason we have been in business in Lake Tahoe for over 35 years. We look forward to getting you out on the water! BOOK YOUR PADDLE ADVENTURE TODAY! Rentals RENTALS Tahoe Paddle and Oar provides Ocean Kayak sit-on top kayaks and Surf Tech and Bic Sport Paddleboards for rentals. All of our rental equipment is very stable, user-friendly and no experience is necessary. More Info Tours TOURS Our friendly and experienced staff will guide you through gigantic boulder mazes and will also provide you with instruction, talk about the history of the lake and the geological history of the area. More Info Sales SALES Our retail store is located at 8245 North Lake Boulevard in Kings Beach – we offer a full line of paddleboards and kayaks including Surftech, Bark, Bic Sport, Ocean Kayak, Old Town and American Traders. More Info Tahoe Paddle & Oar 8245 N Lake Blvd Kings Beach, CA 96143 530.581.3029 Email Us! OPEN DAILY 9:00am-6:00pm Our Mission Tahoe Paddle & Oar is dedicated to creating recreation opportunities for guests to explore Lake Tahoe, create memories, and have fun with friends & family. BOOK ONLINE! Our Philosophy At Tahoe Paddle & Oar, we recognize the environmental, personal health and spiritual benefits of paddling the crystal clear waters of Lake Tahoe. Established in 1986, we strive to provide our Tahoe Basin guests and residents with the best access to paddle sport opportunities while leaving no trace. We invite you to experience the North Shore of Lake Tahoe aboard a kayak or stand up paddleboard – a fun adventure you’ll never forget. TAHOE SLED SCHOOL Lake Tahoe's Premier Snowmobile Rental & Guide Service SERVICES Book Online Now! Guided Backcountry Ride One or Two full days of fun, riding one or two of lake Tahoe's gorgeous sled zones. Work with your instructor ahead of time to select your riding zones, gather your backcountry gear and get ready to see the best scenery you could possibly imagine. Our instructors have been sledding around Lake Tahoe for 12 + years and know all the hidden gems and best lines. Don't have your own snowmobile? No problem! We have a small fleet of top of the line snowmobiles available for rent. See our Snowmobile Rentals Page for further information. You will meet your guide at a pre-determined location each morning depending on which zone you select, gear up, and head out on the road. You will be out on snow for 8-10 hours, so please come prepared with proper waterproof snow gear, layers, boots, gloves, helmet, avalanche pack (including your beacon, shovel, and probe), and a sack lunch. If you do not have an avalanche pack, we have those available for rent so do not fret! For this service, you must be of intermediate or higher skill level on backcountry mountain terrain. If you are a beginner or have never been on a snowmobile, check out our Learn to Ride Clinics and Private Lessons! Backcountry Ski/Board Taxi Want to get ALL the fresh pow lines all day long without the extra effort of skinning? Let one of our amazing snowmobile chauffeurs shuttle you and you crew up to the top endlessly for an epic day of backcountry bliss. ​ Lake Tahoe is arguably one of the most beautiful places to ski and snowboard, and what better way to find all the best spots than to let one of our guides show you the way? ​ For this service, an intermediate ski or snowboard experience level is require, and you will be required to carry an avalanche pack including a beacon, shovel, and probe. If you do not have an avvy pack, don't worry you can't rent one of ours! ​ Available in half and full day options with 1 or 2 drivers. 2-Day Learn To Ride Clinic Never been on a mountain snowmobile? New to riding and want to progress quickly? Feel like your sled is fighting you instead of you controlling it? This riding clinic is for you! Whether you are brand new to the sport or have been riding but are struggling to nail down the basic fundamentals, our amazing instructors will help boost your confidence and ensure you will be on your way to having safe, fun adventures in the backcountry. These clinics will begin with an overview of avalanche safety knowledge and the key features of your sled. You will then progress on to some fundamental skills including how to load and unload your sled from your vehicle or trailer, how to ride and handle your sled on a hard packed road, how to handle riding in powder, making turns, and getting your sled up "on edge". Depending on your skill level and confidence, you will move on to more intermediate skills, such as riding "wrong foot forward", side-hilling, hill climbing, and a few other tips and tricks. These clinics will be offered 6 times over the course of the winter, and you will get to experience some of the world's most beautiful backcountry snowmobile terrain in a safe, fun environment. These clinics are capped at 5 students to ensure ample attention and time with your instructor. No prior riding skill is necessary to join this course, though you will be required to carry an avalanche pack including a beacon, shovel, and probe. If you do not have avalanche safety gear, we do have these available for rent so do not fret. Lastly, you will be out on the snow for 8-9 hours per day, so come prepared with proper waterproof snow gear, boots, layers, gloves, helmet, plenty of water, and lunch/snacks. Don't have your own sled yet? No problem, we have a small fleet of top of the line snowmobiles available for rent for this program. See our Snowmobile Rentals page for further information. Ready, Set, Ride! Snowmobile Rentals Looking to rent a top of line snowmobile for an incredible experience out on the snow of lake Tahoe? We've got you covered. No waiting in tour lines or getting out-dated, non-technical equipment. ​ We have a small fleet of premier snowmobiles to choose from, whether you are looking to buy and want to try a few different models and brands first, or you are visiting for the week and couldn't bring your sled so you need something awesome to rip on, we've go you! ​ We have brand new 2022 and 2023 Polaris and Ski-Doo mountain sleds, see our rentals page for more details on each sled we have to offer. ​ We also rent out avalanche safety gear, which is required for all of our services. Whether you're here for a day or a season, Tahoe Waterman is your lakeside destination for fun, fitness, and fresh food—right on the North Shore of Lake Tahoe. Open to the public, dog-friendly, and welcoming all ages, our year-round beach club offers paddle sports, youth programs, and lakeside community in one beautiful, family-friendly space. Come explore, train, relax, and belong—where the lake meets legacy. Learn What We’re All About RESERVE TODAY Paddle Experience Lake Tahoe from the water. Our paddle center at Waterman’s Landing in Carnelian Bay on Lake Tahoe’s north shore offers hourly kayak and stand-up paddleboard rentals, guided tours, and outrigger canoe adventures for all skill levels. Glide across Lake Tahoe’s crystal-clear waters and enjoy panoramic Sierra Nevada views as you paddle. MENU Eat Refuel and relax at our lakefront café. We serve organic coffee alongside a wholesome menu of breakfast, lunch, and pastries to fuel your day of adventure. Enjoy your meal on our beachside patio with panoramic Lake Tahoe views. BOOK A CLASS Fitness Take your workout outdoors on Lake Tahoe’s shore. Our fitness offerings include paddleboard workouts, beach bootcamps, and yoga sessions that let you soak in Tahoe’s natural beauty while you train. From building core strength to finding your zen with lakefront yoga, we have classes for all fitness levels. REGISTER TODAY Kids Camp Give your kids an unforgettable summer at Lake Tahoe. Our Kids Camp gets children out on the water to learn paddleboarding and kayaking in a safe, encouraging environment. Led by experienced instructors, campers build confidence, make friends, and create lifelong memories splashing in Tahoe’s clear blue waters. While single-day rentals can be fun, they often feel rushed and restrictive. Multi-day rentals, on the other hand, transform boating from a scheduled activity into a seamless part of your Tahoe lifestyle. A tour we think you'll love Mastercraft X24 Luxury Wakesurf Multi-Day From $2,100 View tour Here’s why renting a boat for multiple days is the smartest, most enjoyable way to explore the lake. Freedom to Boat When Conditions Are Perfect Lake Tahoe’s conditions can change throughout the day. Winds typically pick up in the afternoons, while mornings and evenings often offer glassy water and calmer cruising. With a multi-day rental, you’re not locked into a single time slot—you simply head out when the lake looks inviting. No racing the clock. No stressing over return times. Just pure flexibility. No Rush, No Pressure—Just Relax Single-day rentals can feel like an appointment: arrive on time, get out fast, enjoy yourself, then hurry back before the clock runs out. Multi-day rentals remove that pressure entirely. Want to head out for a sunrise cruise, come back for lunch, then surf again in the evening? Go for it. Prefer shorter, spontaneous outings spread across several days? That works too. The boat is there when you want it. More Time = Better Experiences With multiple days on the water, your Tahoe experience naturally becomes richer: Multiple surf, swim, and cruise sessions Time to explore different parts of the lake Sunset cruises without watching the clock Relaxed days that feel effortless instead of packed Rather than trying to “do it all” in one day, you can enjoy Tahoe at its natural pace. Better Value Per Day Multi-day rentals often provide a lower per-day cost compared to single-day bookings. More importantly, you’re getting significantly more usable lake time. When you factor in flexibility, convenience, and the ability to go out whenever conditions are best, the value becomes undeniable. A Boat That Feels Like an Amenity, Not an Errand One of the biggest differences with a multi-day rental is how it feels . Instead of planning your vacation around a boat rental, the boat becomes part of your stay—like having a private dock, a hot tub, or a great view. It’s there when friends stop by. It’s ready when the kids want to surf again. It turns an ordinary Tahoe trip into something truly special. Ideal for Waterfront Stays and Group Trips If you’re staying in a lakefront home or traveling with family and friends, multi-day rentals shine. Everyone can enjoy the boat on their own schedule, without trying to coordinate a single, tightly packed outing. It’s perfect for longer stays, special occasions, and anyone who wants a premium, stress-free Tahoe experience. The Bottom Line Lake Tahoe isn’t meant to be rushed—and neither is boating on it. A multi-day boat rental gives you the freedom, flexibility, and comfort to experience the lake the way it was meant to be enjoyed. More time. Less stress. Better memories. If you’re planning a Tahoe trip and want the most out of your time on the water, multi-day is the way to go. Does your peer-to-peer rental have a patented rear swim deck that meets the water with no propellers , allowing you to maneuver safely to the rescue? Or do you have to leave the helm, shut off the motor while your boat gets blown into the rocks, and help three adults try to hoist her over the propeller zone? Parker, Co-Founder & Chief Safety Officer, Tahoe Jet Boats Lake Tahoe is a place that captivates the senses. Glass-clear water that seems to glow. Snow-dusted peaks that look like a postcard. It’s easy to fall in love—and just as easy to forget how quickly conditions can turn deadly. Every summer, dozens of boat operators launch undertrained crews and propeller boats with little more than a booking calendar and a credit card transaction to guide them. It’s a business model built on volume—and it comes at a steep cost. 🔴 Tahoe Jet Boats was founded to be something different. A safety-first, detail-obsessed alternative for people who value their families more than a discounted hourly rate. 💬 An Interview with James W. Parker, Chief Safety Officer “When we started Tahoe Jet Boats, our question was simple: Why would anyone put a child behind a propeller-driven speedboat when there is a no-propeller option? It’s not like you can’t wakefoil, surf, wakeboard, waterski, or tube behind our surf-ready jet boats—and their deep-V hull design is exactly what the U.S. Coast Guard uses.” “Does the company you’re considering even mention safety—or is their website just another megacorp tourism directory, a bland booking calendar and an automatic confirmation email, devoid of anything but price comparisons? Do they offer or recommend cancellation and rescue insurance as a reasonable, prudent safeguard—or is that conversation simply ignored? Do they explain which parts of the lake are best to avoid daily rough water, wind exposure, and the congestion created by first-time peer-to-peer jet ski and boat renters bent on going full throttle past your 10-year-old who’s 50 yards behind your boat trying to learn how to waterski? These are serious issues. Road ragers abound in South Lake Tahoe. They don’t care on the interstate, and they care even less on the lake—because law enforcement can’t be everywhere at once. Imagine it: it’s your first day driving a peer-to-peer rental boat with a horn that doesn’t work, and your child is about to get run over by someone going 40 mph while fumbling with Spotify to pull up Yacht Rock. Or picture this: you’re floating off Monkey Rock when a storm slams into the 100-foot cliff and sends four-foot waves over the gunwales, knocking your 72-year-old grandmother—who has a bad knee and no upper body strength—into the water. Does your peer-to-peer rental have a patented rear swim deck that meets the water with no propellers , allowing you to maneuver safely to the rescue? Or do you have to leave the helm, shut off the motor while your boat gets blown into the rocks, and help three adults try to hoist her over the propeller zone? Worse yet, you panic and keep the motors running—but in the chaos, you forget to shift into neutral, leaving the propeller spinning in a do-or-die Russian Roulette. What will you do—20 seconds to impact? Are you experienced enough to handle that? Do you know how long it takes for that thunderstorm to reach you from Placerville? Are you even looking up at the weather approaching?” “Before you book, ask yourself: Did this company operate during the Red Flag warnings leading up to the 2025 fatalities? Because we didn’t—and we never will.” “Hundreds of propeller-strike injuries happen every year in this country. Several every summer on Lake Tahoe. Understand Your Options When you’re envisioning a day on the sapphire expanse of Lake Tahoe, you’ll quickly encounter two options: a Lake Tahoe boat rental or a Lake Tahoe boat charter . While the terms are often used interchangeably by first-time visitors, they represent vastly different experiences—and, more importantly, drastically different levels of safety, professionalism, and peace of mind . What Is a Lake Tahoe Boat Rental? A Lake Tahoe boat rental is typically a “drive it yourself” affair. You sign a waiver, get a quick orientation on operating the vessel, and then you and your guests are left to navigate the vast, unpredictable mountain lake on your own. Rental companies may tout this as “freedom,” but in reality, you are assuming all responsibility for: The safety of your passengers The handling of a powerful machine in one of the most variable alpine environments in North America It’s also important to understand that Tahoe boat rentals often don’t undergo the same rigorous scrutiny and compliance standards as properly credentialed charters. If you’ve ever wondered how so many vessels ended up caught in the recent fatal storm, the answer is heartbreakingly simple: Inexperienced operators and companies willing to prioritize volume over prudence. What Makes a Lake Tahoe Boat Charter Different? A Lake Tahoe boat charter provides not just a vessel, but a highly trained, credentialed United States Coast Guard licensed captain . At Tahoe Jet Boats, your captain isn’t a seasonal hire or a part-time employee trying to build hours. Our captains have decades of full-time, year-round Lake Tahoe experience —and that depth of knowledge can be the difference between an idyllic day and a catastrophic outcome .
