(opens in new window) Marine Specialties Service Department Marine Specialties Boat Service & Repair – Northern Nevada’s Trusted Marine Experts Welcome to the Marine Specialties Service Department, where keeping your boat in peak condition is our top priority. We know that owning a boat is all about fun on the water, but it also comes with the responsibility of regular maintenance. That’s why we proudly offer expert boat repairs and service for Nautique, Sanger, Barletta Pontoons, and many other boat brands up to 20 years old. Expert Boat Maintenance & Repairs Our factory-trained technicians specialize in preventative maintenance, diagnostics, and repairs, helping you avoid costly breakdowns and unexpected downtime. Whether you need a 25-hour service, annual service, impeller replacement, full engine diagnostics, or even a new engine installation, we complete repairs efficiently and effectively so you can spend less time in the shop and more time on the water. As an authorized dealer for Nautique, Sanger, and Barletta, we perform warranty repairs on the boats we sell. If you purchased a Nautique, Sanger, or Barletta from us and need warranty service, we will handle the repair process for you. We Service a Wide Range of Marine Engines & Boat Brands We proudly service inboard and sterndrive boats within the last 20 model years, including those powered by: ✔ PCM Marine Engines ✔ Indmar Marine Engines ✔ Volvo Penta Marine Engines ✔ MerCruiser Engines If you’re unsure whether we service your boat, please have your boat’s make, model, and engine information ready when you call or text us, and we’ll be happy to assist you! Preventative Maintenance – Protect Your Investment Preventative maintenance is the key to avoiding costly repairs, maximizing your boat’s performance, and extending its lifespan. Our service team focuses on routine inspections, fluid changes, and system checks to catch potential issues before they turn into major problems. ✔ Oil & Filter Changes – Extend engine life & improve efficiency ✔ Annual Service – Includes engine oil & filter change, fuel filter replacement (if equipped), multi-point inspection, and trailer service ✔ Impeller & Cooling System Checks – Prevent overheating and engine damage ✔ Battery & Electrical System Testing – Avoid unexpected power failures ✔ Fuel System Maintenance – Ensure peak engine performance ✔ Trailer Inspections & Service – Keep your boat trailer safe & road-ready ✔ Maintenance Inspection – Performed on all Summer Preps to check critical systems and catch problems before you’re on the water By staying on top of these essential maintenance steps, you can ensure smooth operation, improved fuel efficiency, and fewer unexpected breakdowns. Seasonal Services – Summer Prep & Winterization ✔ Summer Prep & Maintenance Inspections – Ensure your boat is ready for the season with a full system check and tune-up. ✔ Winterization Services – Properly protect your engine and systems during the off-season to prevent costly freeze damage. Check out the sections below for Preventative Maintenance Estimates, our Maintenance Inspection Sheet, and why Winterization is a must for boaters in Northern Nevada & California. NOTICE FOR OUTBOARD ENGINE CUSTOMERS At this time, Marine Specialties does not provide service or repairs for outboard engines (with the exception of Yamaha outboards on Barletta Pontoons purchased from Marine Specialties). However, we’re happy to assist you in finding a qualified outboard service provider in your area. If you’re performing your own outboard repairs, our Parts Department may have what you need. We stock select older outboard engine parts, and if we don’t have it in stock, we can help you locate the right parts for your specific model. Submit a request through our Parts Request Page, and we’ll do our best to assist you. Service Information SERVICE MENU MAINTENANCE INSPECTION Click any of the pictures for more information Service Menu 1 Maintenance Inspection Service Menu 2 Schedule Your Boat Service – Plan Ahead to Secure Your Spot! At Marine Specialties, we’re here to help you keep your Inboard, V-Drive, or Sterndrive (Inboard/Outboard) boat in top condition with expert maintenance and repairs. Whether you need routine service, diagnostics, or seasonal prep, our factory-trained technicians are ready to assist. Book Early – Peak Season Fills Up Fast! Our service department gets very busy during peak maintenance times, especially in the spring and fall. To ensure you get the dates you need, we highly recommend scheduling your appointment well in advance. pages.text: HOME | Sierra Wake Surf | Wake Surf and Wakeboard Charters and Lessons top of page HOME ABOUT SERVICES CONTACT US FAQ'S LUXURY WAKESURF CHARTERS Built for those who expect more We offer luxury wakesurf and wakeboard charters in the Truckee Tahoe area, led by a local, licensed captain with over 25 years of experience on the water. Our charters are designed for people who want an easy, well-run day without having to think about the details. Some guests come to strictly play or learn, others simply want to cruise and enjoy the lake and most do a little of both. We look forward to welcoming you aboard and taking care of every detail along the way. MEET THE CREW Three Stunning Lakes Nestled in these stunning mountains, we have many pristine lakes, each with its own character. We are proud to offer charters on three of them. BOCA RESERVOIR Boca Reservoir, located in Truckee, California, sits on the Little Truckee River within the Tahoe National Forest. This man-made lake rests at an elevation of about 5,500ft and offers beautiful mountain views. STAMPEDE RESERVOIR Just past Boca, sits Stampede Reservoir, at 5,900ft. Tucked further into the forest, it offers a peaceful, scenic setting and is great for sight seeing. It feeds water into Boca Reservoir throughout the year. LAKE TAHOE Lake Tahoe is a natural lake that straddles the California Nevada border, and is famous for its crystal clear, deep, blue waters. Beyond its scenic beauty, Tahoe offers a variety of waterfront dining and bars. SERVICES Gallery "Cole and Brian were hands down the best instructors I have ever had with this sport. They made me feel comfortable with my limited knowledge and experience of surfing and really made me feel like I knew what I was doing.10/10 would recommend for anybody looking to have a great time with their family and friends, thank you Sierra Wake Surf for introducing me to a lovely sport with amazing people and an even better experience! Parker S. Phone 775-303-8885 Email Sierrawakesurf@gmail.com Connect 2026 Sierra Wake Surf Powered and secured by Wix bottom of page

SERVICES | Sierra Wake Surf top of page HOME ABOUT SERVICES CONTACT US FAQ'S We offer luxury wake surf and wakeboard charters. We have 4-hour and 8-hour charters, along with an hourly option. We require a 2-hour minimum for our hourly option. Some guests come to strictly play or learn, others simply want to cruise and enjoy the lake and most do a little of both. We look forward to welcoming you aboard and taking care of every detail along the way. Locations BOCA RESERVOIR Boca is conveniently located, is the smaller lake of the three, and is also the warmest. It has beautiful sunsets and mountain views. It almost always is glass. Located about 27 miles from Reno and roughly 10 miles from Central Truckee. Exit Interstate 80 at Hirschdale Road in Truckee, California ​ LAKE TAHOE North Lake Tahoe is about 12 miles from Truckee and about 37 miles from Reno. It is the largest of the three and is world-known from its crystal clear, blue water and its stunning coastline. There are waterfront restaurants on the lake as well. ​ North Lake is normally where we launch, but our charter can go to other areas of the lake, weather permitting of course. STAMPEDE RESERVOIR Stampede Reservoir is located about 7 miles past Boca and offers a more secluded setting. Larger and set deeper in the forest, it's typically quieter. It has a beautiful dam that feeds water into Boca throughout the year. Exit Interstate 80 at Hirschdale Road in Truckee, California. Truckee + North Lake Tahoe's First Mobile Axe Throwing Experience About Alpenthrow Thanks for checking out Alpenthrow! North Lake Tahoe's first mobile axe throwing trailer. Whether you're a pro-beard, flannel wearing axe-throwing professional or a first timer, our goal is the same for you and your crew to have an unforgettable time. ​ Whether you're celebrating a special event or just want to have some fun, we'll make any event a fun and unique experience. ​ If you've never thrown before, our coaches will walk you through the how-to's on throwing an axe safely, and in a matter of minutes you will experience the primal thrill of hitting the target. We start with a safety tutorial, followed by throwing with our coaching staff providing detailed instruction to each member of the group. All groups are different, but the learning process generally takes between 10-15 minutes depending on the size of the group. We can provide your group with different games to get competitive with one other. How it Works When you are ready to book, please contact us. Here is what we are going to want to know about your event: ​ ● Date, time, and full address of your event, we request 7-days advance notice to your event. ​ ● Distances of further than 20 miles from Truckee will require additional mileage charges. ​ ● We require a 25ft long x 10ft wide x 12ft. tall space on level ground where we can park our trailer that is easily accessible from the road. ​ ● Our package minimum is 2 hours but can customize pricing specific to your event needs. ​ ● 50% deposit required at time of booking; payment is non-refundable. We have ample space for boats up to 22’ and limited space for larger boats. We always give priority storage to wooden boat owners. Before boats are put in to winter storage, they are fully prepared for layup. We usually start with an oil change followed by the addition of fuel stabilizer and the fogging of the engine. Fogging or pickling, puts a coating of oil over all of the combustion components which includes cylinders and valves. This ensures that during long term storage, surface rust does not erode engine components. The engine is then drained of all cooling water and is fully inventoried for contents stored in the boat. Once racked, the boat is then double checked to make sure it was properly drained. Finally we cover the boats and map their location. When the boat comes out of storage, we activate the engine and go through a check list to make sure critical components are functional such as bilge pumps and lights. We then give the boat a water test to make sure it is performing properly before we release it to the customer. If any problems are encountered, the customer is notified so repairs can be made. This process ensures that our clients receive a trouble free boat upon pickup. How to Read Water Conditions to Improve Your Catch Rate - Fishingintahoe Skip to content info@fishingintahoe.com 530-318-1981 REVIEWS BLOGS CONTACT US HOME About Us Charters Our Guides Our Fleet Book Online Menu HOME About Us Charters Our Guides Our Fleet Book Online BOOK ONLINE How to Read Water Conditions to Improve Your Catch Rate By samsearchberg / September 13, 2024 Understanding water conditions is crucial for enhancing your fishing success. Whether you’re heading out for fishing in Lake Tahoe or any other location, reading water conditions accurately can significantly impact your catch rate. Here’s how to interpret these conditions to make the most of your fishing trips. Observe Water Clarity Water clarity is one of the most important factors in charter fishing . Clearwater generally means fish are warier and may be harder to catch. On the other hand, murky water can make fish less cautious, but it also requires different techniques. In Lake Tahoe, where water clarity can exceed 70 feet, you may need to use more subtle baits and lures. Check water clarity regularly and adjust your fishing methods accordingly. Monitor Water Temperature Fish are highly sensitive to water temperature, and it affects their feeding behavior. For a successful fishing charter, always check the water temperature before you begin. In Lake Tahoe, the water temperature can vary greatly depending on depth and season. Generally, fish are more active in cooler water and might prefer deeper areas during warmer months. Using a temperature gauge can help you find the ideal fishing spots based on current conditions. Watch for Surface Activity Surface activity is a good indicator of fish behavior . Look for signs such as fish jumping, birds diving, or ripples caused by feeding fish. These indicators can help you locate where the fish are active and improve your chances of a successful catch. During your fishing boat trips, use these observations to adjust your location and bait. Paying attention to surface activity can guide you to the most productive fishing areas. Pay Attention to Weather Patterns Weather conditions play a significant role in fishing success. Changes in weather can affect fish behavior and water conditions. For example, overcast skies often lead to more active feeding, while bright sunny days might make fish more elusive. Wind can also influence where fish are located, as it can push baitfish and create feeding opportunities. Before heading out, review the weather forecast and plan your fishing trips around expected conditions. Understand Current and Tide Effects For those engaging in fishing tours in areas with significant currents or tides, understanding their effects is crucial. Tides can influence fish movement, and strong currents can impact where fish are located. In Lake Tahoe, while tides are less of a concern, water flow and current patterns still affect fish behavior. Use this knowledge to choose the best times and locations for fishing boat trips, and consider adjusting your techniques based on current conditions. Ready to Improve Your Catch Rate? If you’re ready to put these tips into practice and experience the best fishing in Lake Tahoe , we at Nor-Cal Charters are here to help. We offer expertly guided fishing trips and private fishing charters that will put you in the prime spots for a successful fishing charter. Our experienced fishing guides know how to read water conditions and will ensure that your fishing tours are both enjoyable and productive. Contact us today to book your next adventure and maximize your catch rate! More NcStar Optics & Accessory Performance Gear CCW CCW News Contact Us Firearms News NSSF Celebrates 20th Anniversary of the Protection of Lawful Commerce in Arms Act WASHINGTON, D.C. — NSSF® – The Firearm Industry Trade Association – celebrates the 20-year anniversary of the enactment of the Protection of Lawful Commerce in Arms Act (PLCAA). The PLCAA is the bipartisan law passed by Congress and signed into law on October 26, 2005, by former President George W. Bush that protects the firearm industry from frivolous lawsuits attempting to hold highly-regulated and lawful firearm businesses liable for the criminal misuse of lawfully sold firearms by remote third parties. The PLCAA, at its core, ensures that the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms can be exercised by law-abiding Americans. “Americans cannot exercise their God-given right to purchase, possess and use firearms without a strong and present industry that provides the means to acquire those firearms. The firearm industry is comprised of more than 400,000 hardworking men and women who take immense pride in providing safe and reliable products for Americans to purchase if and when they choose to do so,” said Lawrence G. Keane, NSSF Senior Vice President and General Counsel. “The Protection of Lawful Commerce in Arms Act has ensured that this Constitutional right has not been bankrupted out of existence by gun control activists and those bent on eliminating the right of law-abiding Americans to keep and bear arms.” The PLCAA codifies traditional American jurisprudence and common-sense principles to prevent baseless litigation from bankrupting an entire industry critical to the safety and security of our nation. The PLCAA codified a bedrock legal principle: that firearm industry manufacturers and retailers are not responsible for the subsequent criminal misuse or illegal possession of their lawfully sold, non-defective products by remote third parties – criminals – over whom they have no control. Firearm industry members are no more legally responsible for illegal shootings than a cookware manufacturer is responsible if a criminal misuses a sharp kitchen knife to stab someone, or than Ford is for a fatal crash caused by a drunk driver operating a Ford vehicle. Congress recognized the threat these frivolous lawsuits represented and passed the bipartisan PLCAA in 2005, explaining it was because antigun politicians were using the courts to “attempt to circumvent the Legislative branch of government” and “expand civil liability in a manner never contemplated by the framers of the Constitution.” The PLCAA is still proving necessary, as the industry is still being targeted by gun control groups and politicians, including those who continue to falsely claim the firearm industry is “the only industry immune from liability.” While the PLCAA has been incredibly successful in protecting the firearm industry from frivolous lawsuits, the PLCAA is constantly under attack. In recent years, several states have attempted to defy the will of Congress by codifying the same strained tort theories in statutes providing that industry members are subjected to ill-defined “reasonable controls” standards for public nuisance. For example, displeased with Congress’ judgment, New York passed a law in 2021 to, in then-Governor Andrew Cuomo’s own words, “reinstate the public nuisance liability for gun manufacturers” that states tried to impose two decades ago, in an avowed effort to “right the wrong done 16 years [earlier]” when Congress enacted the PLCAA. While we celebrate the anniversary of this landmark legislation, we remain vigilant in defending the PLCAA from ongoing threats. -30- About NSSF NSSF is the trade association for the firearm industry. Its mission is to promote, protect and preserve hunting and the shooting sports. Formed in 1961, NSSF has a membership of thousands of manufacturers, distributors, firearms retailers, shooting ranges, sportsmen’s organizations and publishers nationwide. For more information, visit nssf.org. ________________________ Media contact: Mark Oliva 202-220-1340 Big Banks are Blinking on Discrimination Against the Firearms Industry By Larry Keane Big banks are blinking in the stare down over discrimination against the firearm industry. So much so, that even The Wall Street Journal is taking notice. The issue of financial discrimination has been a top priority for NSSF in what can only be described as a David versus Goliath battle of wills. The firearm industry is a $93 billion-a-year industry that faced off against the combined economic strength of the banking industry, which tops $23.6 trillion in assets and a net income of $260 billion in FY 2022. That’s like slinging a pebble against a giant. But persistence pays off and now the giant is thinking the fight isn’t worth the cost. The Wall Street Journal reported, “Big banks are trying to get out of the crosshairs of Republican states that are cracking down on companies for ‘woke’ policies that conservative policymakers say are illegal and discriminatory.” Those meetings were between JP Morgan Chase, Citigroup and Wells Fargo, as well as other big bank representatives, and officials in Texas and Oklahoma. Interestingly, those are the same banking institutions that had, and some continue to have, policies to refuse banking services to firearm-related businesses. Citigroup recently recanted its antigun positions and publicly stated it would conduct business based on financial risk, instead of the ill-defined “reputational risk” that banks used to justify freezing out gun and ammunition businesses. NSSF is cautiously optimistic that Citigroup’s reversal is genuine, but we’re watching and waiting for evidence that firearm businesses are again banking with the corporate financial provider. “Trust but verify,” as President Ronald Reagan used to say. Book Now About Current Fly Fishing A Safe, Fun, and Educational Experience on the Water We offer catch-and-release guided fly fishing trips in Reno, Nevada and Truckee, California. Taking anglers of all ability levels — from first-time fly fishers to experienced anglers looking to improve their skills. Being licensed to guide in both California and Nevada allows us access to some of the best rivers in the Eastern Sierra. If you're looking for a quality fly fishing guide service that offers top-notch instruction for all skill levels, Current Fly Fishing is ready to make your next adventure a great one. Guide Trips & Rates Lessons Fly Fishing Locations Truckee River | East Walker River California & Nevada With Reno, Nevada as our home base, we are able to access many great fly fishing locations within an hour drive, along with other productive waters throughout the Eastern Sierra. The Truckee River is our home water, and we also guide trips on the East Walker River. These are two of the Eastern Sierra’s best rivers for large, hard-fighting brown and rainbow trout. Float trips on the Truckee River offer a completely different perspective on this beautiful fishery and allow access to water that is difficult to reach on foot. Fishing Locations Guided Fly Fishing Trips Truckee River Guided Fly Fishing Trips From half-day guide trips to full-day float trips, Current Fly Fishing offers guided fly fishing trips for anglers of all experience levels in Reno, Nevada and Truckee, California. From $425 Half-Day Guide Trip A great option for anglers looking for focused instruction, an immersive experience and a shorter day on the Truckee River. More Details From $550 Full-Day Guide Trip Spend a full day learning, fishing and covering productive water with a guided fly fishing trip tailored to your goals. More Details From $600 Full-Day Guided Float Float trips offer a unique way to fish the Truckee River, cover more water and experience the river from a different perspective. More Details Large Groups & More Book Your Trip Today Ask about large groups, custom trips, gift certificates and the best option for your next day on the water. More Details Plan Your Trip The Best Time to Fish the Truckee River A day on the water always beats a day in the office, but going when conditions are right makes it even better. Our favorite times of year to fish are spring and fall, especially May through June and September through October. July and August can still be great months to fish, but we usually start early in the morning to beat the heat of the day. The Truckee River sits on the eastern side of the Sierra Nevada and can experience a wide range of weather and water conditions. Use the links below to check river flows, weather and access before your trip. Here are a few common questions about our guided fly fishing trips, locations, rates, timing, dogs, licensing and cancellation policy. See All Information What services do you offer? We are a catch-and-release fly fishing guide service. We teach all levels of anglers, so if it is your first time, we make sure to take the time to teach you the skills and techniques you will need for a day on the water. What locations do your trips take place in? We are based in Reno, Nevada and offer guide trips on the Truckee River. We have the ability to guide in California and Nevada, allowing us to access much of the Truckee River. What are the rates of your services? We offer a range of trip options, and rates differ based on how many people are in the group and the trip type. To see all services offered, visit our Guide Trips and Rates page . What is the best time of year to fly fish? Anytime you can make it out is a good time to go fishing, as many of the places we fish are open year-round. However, depending on water conditions, we especially enjoy fishing in early spring and fall. Can we bring our dog? The short answer is that it depends. We understand every dog is different, and we like to chat about it before booking. If it seems like a good fit, we are happy to have your furry friend along. However, dogs are not allowed on Truckee River float trips because the rafts are relatively small and inflatable. Are you licensed and insured? Yes. We are licensed by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife and the Nevada Department of Wildlife. We are also insured and bonded. What is your cancellation policy? Deposits become non-refundable 14 days prior to the trip date. Our guide trips go out rain or shine, and cancellations based on environmental factors are solely at Current Fly Fishing’s discretion. Whether you’re new to fly fishing or looking to improve your skills, Current Fly Fishing offers guided trips built around safety, instruction and a great day on the water. Read FAQs What’s Included Clean, well-fitted waders & boots Premium flies, leaders, tippet & terminal tackle Rods & reels (or bring your favorite setup) Full-day and Float trips include lunch . Bottled spring water and Gatorade Photos What to Bring Sun protection (hat, sunglasses, sunscreen) Water & snacks (we carry extras) Fishing license — NV or CA (we’ll confirm locations the day before) Layered clothing for mountain weather Need help with a license? We’ll advise which state based on the day’s plan. See our Pre-Trip Checklist for links to each states licensing website, a full list of what too bring and how to prepare for the day. Trip Options & Rates Half-Day · Walk & Wade ~5 hours · 1–2 anglers $425 Custom meet location (Reno · Verdi · Truckee) All gear included; waders & boots provided Book Half-Day Full-Day · Walk & Wade 6–8 hours · 1–2 anglers $550 Lunch included Fish more than one location. Mix and Match any of our location offerings to make for an unforgettable day. All gear included; waders & boots provided Book Full-Day Full-Day · Float Trip 7–8 hours · 1–2 anglers $600 A great way to see the river and if mobility is a concern it's the best option. Lunch included All gear included; waders & boots provided Float Trip availability is subject to water level conditions. Book Float Rates shown are for 1–2 anglers,add $150 for each additional angler up to 3 people. Group larger than 3 will require additional guides. We also offer lessons, See other offerings . We can accommodate large groups with advance notice. Large groups will require additional guides. (Unless a guide is specifically requested, trips maybe assigned to any of our professional guide staff) Seasons & Conditions on the Truckee The Truckee River fishes year-round with changing techniques through the seasons. We choose our fly fishing locations based on flows, clarity, and hatches. Spring: As the snow melt run off subsides and temps warm up we see the most diversity in our insect hatches; BWOs, March Browns,PMDs, Yellow Sally Stoneflys and Caddis. There is a fair chance to see a few fish rising too. A great time of year to Float, higher water levels allow float access to many sections. Summer: As temps rise and water levels begin to lower we see Caddis, Mayfly, Golden Stoneflys and Midge hatches. Floating remains an option in certain areas however, depending on flows we may be limited.Many areas open up for Walk and Wade Fishing. Fall: Consistent flows and cooler weather; Mayfly/Baetis and October Caddis. Once temps drop we start floating east of Reno. This section of river can offer opportunities for dry fly fishing and stunning desert views. Winter: Fish move into slower pools and begin to feed during the warmest parts of the day. Midges and BWOs are the main hatch. Surprisingly, this is the most productive time of year for dry fly fishing. Floating east of Reno is a great option as well as Walk and Wade. Meeting Areas Common meet points include Reno/Verdi (NV) and Truckee (CA) . Exact locations are confirmed the day prior via text or email. We are flexable an can pick you up if needed, just let us know. Easy highway access Parking at or near the water Options for mobility and comfort Float Trips: We'll meet at the Put-In and Shuttle a vehicle down to the Take-Out. At the end of the day we'll return to your vehicle at the Put-In. Why Current Fly Fishing? Local Expertise & Quality Instruction Reno–Tahoe based; daily reads on flows & clarity. Over a decade of teaching the art of fly fishing to all ages and abilities. All Gear Included &amp Lunches Waders, boots, premium flies, rods & reels. Our lunches are made to order right there on the river, just the way you like it. Client Centered &amp Friendly Vibe Beginner-friendly to advanced technical sessions. Above all we're on the river to have a fun and safe experiance. FAQs Do I need a Nevada or California license? The Truckee crosses both states. We’ll confirm the day before so you can purchase the correct license. Are waders and boots included? Yes — clean, properly sized waders & boots are included on all guide trips. What’s the best time of year? We guide year-round. Spring and fall are the most consistent; summer offers fun pocket-water; winter is technical but rewarding. Where do we meet? Typically near Reno, Verdi, or Truckee. We’ll text you the exact pin the day before based on flows and clarity. What’s your cancellation policy? Life happens — see our cancellations below for details and weather considerations. Other Offerings Looking for dedicated instruction on casting, knot tying, or rigging? Explore our Fly Casting & Intro Lessons We also offer Gift Certificates , give us a call or email and we'll help make that next special event even better. Parking reservations will be required for all lots on weekends and peak periods (excluding February 20th). See the FAQs below for more information and visit ParkKirkwood.com to book your reservations. We remain committed to addressing challenges with traffic, road congestion, and parking. This winter, we will continue to require reservations on weekends (Saturday Sunday) and peak periods until 12pm in all lots at Kirkwood, with a mix of free, paid, and free carpool (4+) options. If parking in any lot at Kirkwood on a weekend or peak period before 12pm, guests must secure a reservation in advance via our website (regardless of how many people are in the vehicle). Free reserved lots during weekends and peak periods include: Lower 7, Kirkwood Meadows Drive (north of Loop Rd. 88), and Kirkwood Inn. Paid and carpool reserved lots during weekends and peak periods include: VIP, Chair 5/6, Volcano, Upper Red Cliffs, Lower Red Cliffs, Upper 7, Middle 7, Tennis Courts, Shop Lot, Shanty Town, Powerhouse Rd., Loop Rd., and Chair 9 (drop off only). These lots are $20 for vehicles with 3 or fewer occupants. Vehicles with 4+ occupants park free but still require a reservation. Parking at Kirkwood on non-peak weekdays, and after 12pm on weekends and peak periods, will not require reservations and will remain free in all lots. Please see our FAQ below for more information. Carnegie SVRA Known for its challenging hill climbs and single track trails, the SVRA offers a variety of recreation opportunities for OHV enthusiasts. Clay Pit SVRA Located two miles west of Oroville, this 220-acre SVRA provides recreation opportunities for motorcycle, ATV and 4x4 recreationists. Heber Dunes SVRA The sand dunes and dense groves of tamarisk trees that prevail throughout the SVRA offer a unique desert recreation experience. Hollister Hills SVRA Divided into two unique recreation areas-the Upper Ranch and the Lower Ranch-the park provides a wide-variety of OHV recreation opportunities for all skill levels Hungry Valley SVRA OHV recreation opportunities include open areas, identified trails, tracks, play areas, special use areas, and a 4x4 obstacle course. Oceano Dunes SVRA The SVRA provides a unique opportunity for visitors to participate in OHV recreation on several miles of beach and coastal sand dunes. Ocotillo Wells SVRA More than 85,000 acres of Southern California desert provide a wide variety of opportunities for OHV recreation and exploration. Prairie City SVRA This urban OHV Park provides recreational opportunities for motorcycles, ATVs, 4x4s, ROVs, Karts, and Quarter Midgets. Our Mission The Mission of the Off-Highway Motor Vehicle Recreation (OHMVR) Division is to provide leadership statewide in the area of off-highway vehicle (OHV) recreation; to acquire, develop, and operate state-owned vehicular recreation areas; and to otherwise provide for a statewide system of managed OHV recreational opportunities through funding to other public agencies. The OHMVR Division works to ensure quality recreational opportunities remain available for future generations by providing for education, conservation, and enforcement efforts that balance OHV recreation impacts with programs that conserve and protect cultural and natural resources. State Parks Commissions Historic Preservation Boating & Waterways Visit one of our SVRAs Ride your dirt bike, ATV, side-by-side (ROV/UTV), 4x4, or dune buggy on a wide variety of designated terrain and trails available at nine state vehicular recreation areas (SVRAs). Some SVRAs feature camping, interpretive programs, and other recreational opportunities. Learn about our Grants Program Our OHMVR Division's Grants and Cooperative Agreements Program in an annual program providing financial assistance to eligible applicants for well-managed off-highway vehicle recreation. OHMVR Commission The Off-Highway Motor Vehicle Recreation Commission meets quarterly to review plans for new and expanded recreation areas and welcomes public comment on the OHMVR Division's program s . OHV Safety Week Join the OHMVR Division and its partners for this year's OHV Safety Week, held from November 15th to 23th, 2025. OHMVR Division encourages everyone to prioritize OHV safety and respect for one another. Off-Highway Vehicle Access Project The Off-Highway Vehicle (OHV) Access Project is a state initiative lead by the California Department of Parks and Recreation (State Parks) Strategic Planning and Recreation Services Division, Off-Highway Motor Vehicle Recreation (OHMVR) Division, and OHMVR Commission to identify new opportunities for additional OHV facilities in California as mandated by Senate Bill 155 (SB 155). LEARN MORE Support the protection of our resources The OHMVR Division plays an important role in protecting diverse natural and cultural resources throughout California. Click here to learn about the division’s numerous resource management projects. Know before you go Prior to leaving for your outdoor destination, learn how to recreate safely and responsibly. Read up on the rules of the riding, take a training course and find out about the proper equipment. OHV Announcements Legislation Updates Off-Highway Vehicle Adventure Guide The OHV Adventure Guide has been updated. Click here to view the list of OHV opportunities. We are testing out an online version of the OHV Adventure Map . Try it out and let us know what you think. Send comments and suggestions about the map to ohvaccessproject@parks.ca.gov . Captain Brad has been guiding fishing charters on Lake Tahoe since 2011 and offers private, family-friendly trips for all experience levels. Guided Lake Tahoe fishing trips are available daily on the North Shore and last up to four hours. From spring through summer, a second trip is often available starting between 9 and 10 am, and during the summer months, feel free to swim as well during your trip! All trips are private charters, meaning it will only be your group on the boat. pages.text: Fishing Guide ─ Captain Chris' Fishing Charters Skip to content Fishing North Lake Tahoe Since 1980. Guiding Tahoe Since 1999. +1 (530) 583-4857 Captain Chris is a friendly, knowledgeable North Lake Tahoe fishing guide who loves to catch fish All charters are private all of the time—up to 5 people. You & your group will be the only ones on board. Come fish on my boat, a 25-foot Skip jack, with a comfortable cabin and restroom. Captain Chris does it all, from taking your call to filleting your fish. Mackinaw trout are the primary target in Lake Tahoe; however, from July through September, I also fish for rainbow trout after catching Mackinaw first. April through September, trips depart early morning. Winter trips are wind and weather permitting. Charter length is approximately 4 hours. Call for start times. All Charters are Private All of the Time. All Tackle Provided (I Use Light Tackle). U.S. Coast Guard & California Fish and Game Licensed. Charter Rates Rates change from season to season; please call for a price quote. Passes Golf Events & Programs Local Clubs Parks & Fields The parks and fields in Incline Village are great places to hold sporting events and picnics. Many of the facilities/venues listed here are available for group rentals. View more information on the Rental Facilities page . Ridgeline Park Ball Fields 939 Southwood Blvd., Incline Village, NV 89451 Ridgeline Park consists of three well-maintained softball/baseball fields, located right below the Incline Skate Park on Southwood, next to the middle school. Ball Field #3 underwent extensive renovations in 2021, made possible through a public-private partnership with Ridgeline Apps , the Incline-Tahoe Foundation , and the Incline Village General Improvement District. Read more about the renovation on the Ridgeline Park & Ball Field page . Ridgeline Park Ball Fields are available for group rentals for Incline Village and Crystal Bay residents and the general public. Preston Field & Playground 700 Tahoe Blvd., Incline Village, NV 89451 This field is located right along Hwy 28 by the Hwy 431 turnoff and it’s easily spotted by its radiant green grass and perfectly groomed field. Preston Field is perfect for playing softball and baseball. Preston Field is available for group rentals for Incline Village and Crystal Bay residents and the general public. Adjacent to the field is a playground with two play structures and a swing set surrounded by a grassy area and picnic tables. Picnic areas are available for group rentals for birthday parties, small outdoor gatherings, etc. Village Green 960 Lakeshore Blvd., Incline Village, NV 89451 Village Green is a wide open space next to the Hyatt Regency Lake Tahoe. There is a multi-use field for playing soccer, Frisbee, or a friendly game of football. A trail and a creek run around the edges of it and it’s nestled among the Aspen trees. Park at the Aspen Grove parking lot. Village Green is available for group rentals for Incline Village and Crystal Bay residents and the general public. The schedule for Village Green is posted here during the spring, summer, and fall months as the fields are occasionally rented for sports leagues and special events. Passes Golf Events & Programs Local Clubs Rental Facilities Incline Village has several venues available for your next party, family reunion, wedding, sporting event, or meeting in North Lake Tahoe. Recreation Center, Beach Picnic Areas, Parks and Fields The Recreation Center offers year-round facilities for birthday parties, group fitness room, indoor gymnasium, and indoor pool. Adjacent to the Recreation Center, the new Bocce Park is a great outdoor space that is available for parties and rentals. On the west end of town, Preston Park is another great location for a family gathering, work outing or your child’s birthday party. In addition, Village Green, Preston Field and Ridgeline Park offer wide open spaces for activities and have multi-use fields for your softball and baseball needs for tournaments, family reunions, or corporate events. For IVGID Picture Pass Holders (with beach access), Incline and Burnt Cedar beaches have picnic areas to reserve for your spring or summer event. No longer do you need to arrive hours before your event to secure a spot for your group. The designated beach sites include picnic tables offering you and your friends an area to picnic or grill and enjoy the beach. The volleyball courts and bocce area is also now available for group rentals. Each guest is still responsible for beach access fees. Reservations at all sites are taken on a first-come, first-served basis at the Parks & Recreation Counter. Please call (775) 832-1310 or stop by and see us for rates or more information. Payment is required with your application. Group Picnic Area Rental Application (Picnic areas at Preston & Incline Park, Village Green, Rec Center Bocce Park, and IVGID Beaches) Field Rental Application (Preston & Ridgeline Park Fields, Village Green, and Skate Park) Recreation Center Rental Application (The Zone, Gymnasium, Pool, Group Fitness Room, and Lobby/Deck areas) – visit the Recreation Center for application Tennis & Pickleball Center Sitting along a year-round creek, the Incline Village Tennis & Pickleball Center is a beautiful location for your private tennis or pickleball event, clinic, or tournament. Rent individual courts or rent the entire Pickleball Center (15 upper courts). The newly renovated deck can also be rented for events. Tennis & Pickleball Center Facility Rental Application (tennis courts, pickleball courts, and Tennis & Pickleball Center deck) Incline Village Golf Courses, Tournaments & Groups ​The Incline Village Golf Courses offers special rates for groups of 16 or more. The unique Robert Trent Jones, Jr. designed Mountain Course and the renowned Robert Trent Jones, Sr. designed Championship Course provide fun and challenging options for all levels of golfers. Fill out the Tournament Inquiry form and our staff with contact you with options. The Chateau at Incline Village® Radiating with Tahoe charm, The Chateau at Incline Village® is located at the Championship Golf Course at 955 Fairway Blvd. Vaulted ceilings, stacked rock fireplaces, and expansive decks all enhance the beauty of the natural surroundings. Our 37,000 square foot, first-class complex boasts a wide variety of activities for all ages and interests. The Recreation Center offers a vast selection of memberships and equipment for you and your family to enjoy. With a myriad of activities and fitness classes available, we have a place for your workout! Recreation Center Daily & Membership Rates (PDF) Cancel a Membership To cancel a membership you must come into the Recreation Center and fill out a cancelation form by the 21st day of the month prior to the month you wish to cancel. Forms will not be mailed or faxed. Call the Front Desk at (775) 832-1310 for more information. New Member Orientation If you are a new member to the Incline Village Recreation Center, you may sign up for a complimentary “get acquainted” orientation. New members will receive a facility tour, an overview of the fitness/weight room, and some helpful program and class information. Call (775) 832-1310 to make an appointment. Passes Golf Events & Programs Local Clubs Transfer of Service In order to transfer service to a new owner we will need to receive notification at least two business days prior to close of escrow. Water and sewer services are not interrupted upon change of ownership. Service is not transferred until a Grant Deed has been received from the title company. The details below also provide other helpful information to ensure accuracy upon close of escrow. Buyers can contact our office to provide their contact information, but water and sewer utilities follow the property. Once we receive a copy of the Grant Deed after close of escrow we can transfer service. Processing change of ownership upon sale For single, multi-family and commercial properties (excluding HOA accounts or vacant land) For all changes of ownership due to sale we will require a minimum of 2 working days notice, prior to the close of escrow, to schedule a final read on the water meter. Please call our office to notify us of the estimated close of escrow date and a request for final meter read. By the morning of the close of escrow date we will provide you with the current balance on the account and the consumption charges due from the final meter read. IVGID does not prorate balances on accounts so the final read breakdown will include the base rate charges for the account (which are billed in advance). If a final meter read is not requested the new owner will be liable for the past consumption charges on the account. Other helpful information to ensure accuracy upon close of escrow If the leak notification is set at the time of collecting a final meter read IVGID will advise escrow so all parties can be informed. This is a courtesy notification and IVGID will not require a leak be fixed. When a demand is submitted for completion, we will complete the information requested or indicate if the property is located within an HOA which pays the water/sewer charges or is vacant land. We will also send the demand to the IVGID Recreation department for them to indicate if there are passes which need to be returned upon sale. Our billing cycle is the 19th to the 18th of each month. Our base rates are billed on the 19th of the month in advance for this time period. Consumption charges are billed in arrears based on water and sewer use at the property. IVGID does not prorate charges and water and sewer services and charges are continuous through change of ownership. If the customer has Auto Payment set for their account, we will cancel auto payment once a final read is completed. If duplicate payment is made after the close of escrow date, we will deposit the title company check and issue a refund check to the seller. Upon close of escrow we need to receive a copy of the Deed (excluding properties in an HOA), even if there is not a check being submitted, as well as a contact phone number(s) for the customer. A separate demand for refuse charges must be sent to Waste Management by email: dpayoffs@wm.com. Refuse rates are billed quarterly in advance on October 1, January 1, April 1, and July 1. pages.text: ODM Defense Home Calendar Holsters Instructors Services Deposits Contact Media Home Calendar Holsters Instructors Services Deposits Contact Media Guns - gear - custom holsters - training ODM DEFENSE Providing Safe and Practical Personal Defense Training, Firearms, and Gear for Northern Nevada & Surrounding Areas Founded in Minden, NV with the core value of providing safe, practical, professional, and relaxing firearms training to individuals and groups, ODM Defense is a positive training environment to improve and perfect you knowledge and skills as a responsible gun owner. ODM Defense uses practical methods during our training evolutions to make the student really think about and analyze what it is they are doing, why they are doing it, and what the intended outcome is. Whether it is a CCW class, a first-time shooters class, Hunters Ed, or advanced pistol, the staff at ODM Defense place a heavy emphasis on the “why”. Why do we do things a certain way, why we approach certain methods a certain way… Its the why that helps the student recognize, acknowledge, and accept the information being presented. Get in touch with us to reserve a class seat, or use the contact form at the bottom of this page to enquire whether our services are right for you. Learn More Contact ➤ LOCATION 2559 Precision Dr, Ste 1 Minden, NV 89423 ☎ CONTACT info@odmdefense.com (775) 468-6874 Some of What We Offer Concealed Carry Learn the ins and outs of carrying a concealed firearm. Safety, Mindset, Nomenclature, Local, State, and Federal Laws, Basic Fundamentals & Shooting Skills, Marksmanship, Written Exam & Range Qualification. This class covers the state minimum requirement & much, MUCH more. Ladies Only Orientation We pride ourselves on providing a safe, comfortable, and relaxing training environment where new shooters can feel free to ask whatever questions come to mind, and get hands-on training on all levels of firearm handling and safe use. This is a 2 part class, consisting of classroom and live-fire range time. ODM takes care of all the heavy lifting! FACTORY-CERTIFIED CERAKOTE SERVICES We have a Cerakote factory-certified cerakote applicator on the team to handle all of your custom coating needs! Whether you want a simple single color change-up, or an elaborate camouflage pattern, we can take care of it! Our applicator is well regarded in the industry and has been applying product for nearly a decade. All of our cerakote is done in-house, there is no sub-contracting or outsourcing. We strive to have a fast turn around, approximately 2 weeks or less! Cerkote service pricing is dependent on the size of the job. Feel free to contact us for pricing and timeline. Pistol training Whether you’re a first time shooter or a higher level competitor, ODM has something for you. Firearm safety and manipulation, mechanics, recognizing and clearing various malfunctions quickly and efficiently, or just making a few tweaks here and there, we can get you dialed. unarmed combatives training Our unique Combative Self Defense Program draws from the most effective combative fighting systems available, including systems such as Filipino Martial Arts, Krav Maga, Brazilian Jiu Jitsu, C.O.B.R.A, Marine Corps Martial Arts Program, and more. There is literally nothing else like this available anywhere. FFL TRANSFERS Having trouble finding a reasonable place to have your firearms transferred to? Look no further! ODM Defense is happy to conduct your FFL transfers! We charge $20.00 for the initial firearm, and $10.00 for any additional firearms on the same transfer. For current and former LE/Mil, 1st Responders, It’s $10.00 for per firearm. Contact us directly with any questions you may have pertaining to our transfer services! Rifle training Want to learn to build your very own custom AR-15? We can do that. Want to learn to run that gun? We can do that, too. We offer build classes and multiple levels of rifle training from static range to dynamic movement and working in pairs and teams. private instruction Often times, some individuals may not feel safe or comfortable receiving training in a large group of strangers. Not a problem? We are happy to offer one-on-one training and private group instruction at a reasonable hourly rate. If its a standard class we offer, you will not be charged extra for a private group class. NEVADA STATE PRIVATE INVESTIGATORS LICENSING BOARD ARMED GUARD CERTIFICATION ODM Defense is state certified and approved to teach both the initial two-day armed guard certification, and the 6-month renewal course. If you are employed by a third-party security contracting company and require either your initial or renewal, contact us for scheduling and we can get you certified! “ Awareness is good. But without skills and ability tied to that awareness,all you have is anxiety. ” Tony Blauer Let's Chat. Questions, comments, or concerns for us? Please feel free to correspond with us below. We will address any of your questions or concerns as soon as possible! Looking for a new firearm but not sure what works for you? Looking for a recommendation on defensive ammo? Can’t recall something that was covered in class and need a quick reminder? We’re happy to help! #jeffsays home | about | services | contact (775) 468-6874 | info@odmdefense.com 2559 Precision Dr, Ste 1 Minden, NV 89423 Echo 6 Industries, LLC is a retail, training and manufacturing business and intellectual property that provides safe, practical defensive training to civilians of all skill levels and disciplines, as well as quality thermoplastic retention systems, and retail service. Services ODM Defense Home Calendar Holsters Instructors Services Deposits Contact Media Home Calendar Holsters Instructors Services Deposits Contact Media Services Safe and practical self-defense, firearms, & emergency medical training for an unsafe world. Training Courses & Services State of Nevada cONCEALED CARRY CLASS ($120) - Renewals ($60) We offer one of the most in-depth and comprehensive concealed carry classes in Northern Nevada. The state mandates an 8hr minimum block of instruction, but we push a little beyond that to make sure you are getting the information and training you need to apply for your Nevada state carry permit. We cover basic safety, handling, nomenclature, basic shooting skills, force continuum, laws and regulations, all with a heavy emphasis on mindset. The course time covers the instruction portion, range qualification, and written exam. Completion certificates are handed out at the successful completion of the course. Lady’s only safety and pistol orientation ($100) The shooting world can be intimidating and overpowering to new shooters. There a lot of “Type-A” personalities out there, a lot of self-proclaimed “subject matter experts” that claim to be the end-all-be-all of range ninjas. This can make trying to get involved in shooting very daunting for some. We believe truly that comfort equals confidence. Our Lady’s Only classes provide a safe, low pressure environment where women can feel comfortable learning and asking questions. The class is geared more towards novice or first-time shooters that may want to learn more about firearms and safety in general. You do not need to own a gun to attend this class. The class consists of a 2 hr evening classroom session with no live firearms. It is strictly safety, proper handling and manipulation, and basic shooting fundamentals. We then meet up at the range for a 2 hr demonstration. All handguns and ammunition are provided, though you are welcome to bring your own firearm if you choose to! indoor shooting simulator Our shooting simulator provides users an opportunity to hone their shooting skills without the requirement of live ammunition. Through a combination of private instruction and the use of green-gas operated laser training pistols, the user gets positive feedback from the firearm cycling, while being coached on proper technique. This is a great way to greatly improve accuracy while solidifying basic fundamentals and techniques. It’s also a fun way to blow off some steam! The simulator can be booked as instructor led training, or for basic individual and groups by the hour. Tactical Advantage ($250) We are living in some extremely strange times! We are seeing more more acts of violence across the country with random targeting and zero provocation. Sadly, in these violent situations, when seconds count, help is MINUTES away! No one is coming. It is up to you. YOU are your own first responder. Our EDC Skills class is designed to give the shooter the skills, abilities, and confidence needed to carry a concealed firearm for personal defense, and the ability to deploy that defensive tool in a time of need. In our EDC Skills course, we discuss the mindset necessary in self defense situations. We will discuss equipment selection and options available to best suit the needs of the student. A heavy emphasis is placed on mechanics, fundamentals, and technique needed to get the gun into the fight quickly and accurately. The student can expect repetitions on draw technique, combat marksmanship, multiple target engagement, movement shooting, cover and concealment, reloading technique, malfunction and clearance manipulation, shooting from retention, stress inoculation, and some scenario based shooting focusing on rapid decision making. Requirements for this course: a valid CCW Permit demonstrating a basic knowledge of firearms handling and proficiency, carry pistol, holster, at least one (2) magazines minimum, magazine carrier, cover garment, and 250 rounds of ammunition (minimum). More ammo means more live fire drill repetitions. Pistol development (level I, II, III) ($125-$250) Let’s face it, we can’t all be John Wick. But what we can do, is train as hard and as disciplined as we can to become better, more proficient shooters than we were yesterday! And who knows, with enough time on the range, maybe someday you could find yourself in the lobby of the Continental. Until then, we train. Our pistol curriculum is designed to improve the abilities and confidence of all levels of shooters. From our introduction Level I class, up through our advanced Level III class, and everything in between. Safety, proficiency, gun handling skills, platform familiarity, mechanics, induced stress, and mindset are just a few of the things you will learn to overcome and master during our instruction. Requirements: Proof of successful completion of preceding course Quality belt, pistol, holster, 3 magazines (minimum), magazine carrier (2 singles or one double recommended), eye protection, hearing protection, 250 rds (minimum) Tactical Advantage ($250) This course is essentially a truncated version of our Handgunner II and our Rifleman II class rolled into one day. This course is intended for the intermediate shooter who already has a solid grasp on basic fundamentals and is ready to move to a higher level. The student must provide documentation showing training previously completed that covers introductory level skills. This is a fast paced course that covers a lot of information quickly. The first third of the day will encompass pistol work, the middle of the day will encompass rifle work, and the trail third of the day will involve use of both platforms in both drills and scenario based training. At the end of this class, students will have a solid working knowledge of pistol and rifle manipulation, reloading and malfunction resolution, proper implementation, and decision making skills that will make the student a better, more proficient defensive shooter. Requirements: Proof of successful completion of prior training Quality Belt, Pistol, Holster, 3 pistol magazines (minimum), magazine carrier (2 singles or one double recommended), Rifle, sling, 2 rifle magazines (minimum), rifle magazine carrier, eye protection, hearing protection, 200 rds pistol ammo, 200 rds rifle ammo TAC-Med (CPR/AED, First-Aid, Stop the bleed) Being able to make holes is important when it comes to defending yourself, but when seconds count, help is minutes away. This also holds true for medical response. You may be put in a position where medical aid is essential and there’s no one there to provide it. This class encompasses several aspects of emergency first aid: Stop the Bleed, First Aid, and CPR. Our TacMed class is AHA certified! once you complete this training you will receive your CPR Certification. This is a very thorough course, covering knife and gunshot wounds, wound packing, tourniquet use, chest seals, bandage application, and CPR implementation. This class is open to all age groups! rifle build class *Kit Dependent ($500-$1500+) Ever wanted to have that custom AR-15 to play with but didn’t know how to make it happen? In this class, builders will select their wants formalist of components. Once those components are ordered and delivered, builders than come in and build their very own rifle, to their specifications, with their own hands under the tutelage of our armorers. You leave the class with your very own, one of a kind, custom hand-built rifle! And normally for less cost then if you were to buy one off the shelf! RIFLE development (Level I, II, III) ($125-$250) Whether it be the first time shooter or the top level 3-gun competitor, we all want to become more proficient with our long guns. Our Carbine courses are designed for the shooter to become more comfortable and seamless in their rifle controls manipulation. Our carbine courses focus on clean manipulation and mechanics to establish proper “muscle memory”

We are seeing more more acts of violence across the country with random targeting and zero provocation. Sadly, in these violent situations, when seconds count, help is MINUTES away! No one is coming. It is up to you. YOU are your own first responder. Our EDC Skills class is designed to give the shooter the skills, abilities, and confidence needed to carry a concealed firearm for personal defense, and the ability to deploy that defensive tool in a time of need. In our EDC Skills course, we discuss the mindset necessary in self defense situations. We will discuss equipment selection and options available to best suit the needs of the student. A heavy emphasis is placed on mechanics, fundamentals, and technique needed to get the gun into the fight quickly and accurately. The student can expect repetitions on draw technique, combat marksmanship, multiple target engagement, movement shooting, cover and concealment, reloading technique, malfunction and clearance manipulation, shooting from retention, stress inoculation, and some scenario based shooting focusing on rapid decision making. Requirements for this course: a valid CCW Permit demonstrating a basic knowledge of firearms handling and proficiency, carry pistol, holster, at least one (2) magazines minimum, magazine carrier, cover garment, and 250 rounds of ammunition (minimum). More ammo means more live fire drill repetitions. Pistol development (level I, II, III) ($125-$250) Let’s face it, we can’t all be John Wick. But what we can do, is train as hard and as disciplined as we can to become better, more proficient shooters than we were yesterday! And who knows, with enough time on the range, maybe someday you could find yourself in the lobby of the Continental. Until then, we train. Our pistol curriculum is designed to improve the abilities and confidence of all levels of shooters. From our introduction Level I class, up through our advanced Level III class, and everything in between. Safety, proficiency, gun handling skills, platform familiarity, mechanics, induced stress, and mindset are just a few of the things you will learn to overcome and master during our instruction. Requirements: Proof of successful completion of preceding course Quality belt, pistol, holster, 3 magazines (minimum), magazine carrier (2 singles or one double recommended), eye protection, hearing protection, 250 rds (minimum) Tactical Advantage ($250) This course is essentially a truncated version of our Handgunner II and our Rifleman II class rolled into one day. This course is intended for the intermediate shooter who already has a solid grasp on basic fundamentals and is ready to move to a higher level. The student must provide documentation showing training previously completed that covers introductory level skills. This is a fast paced course that covers a lot of information quickly. The first third of the day will encompass pistol work, the middle of the day will encompass rifle work, and the trail third of the day will involve use of both platforms in both drills and scenario based training. At the end of this class, students will have a solid working knowledge of pistol and rifle manipulation, reloading and malfunction resolution, proper implementation, and decision making skills that will make the student a better, more proficient defensive shooter. Requirements: Proof of successful completion of prior training Quality Belt, Pistol, Holster, 3 pistol magazines (minimum), magazine carrier (2 singles or one double recommended), Rifle, sling, 2 rifle magazines (minimum), rifle magazine carrier, eye protection, hearing protection, 200 rds pistol ammo, 200 rds rifle ammo TAC-Med (CPR/AED, First-Aid, Stop the bleed) Being able to make holes is important when it comes to defending yourself, but when seconds count, help is minutes away. This also holds true for medical response. You may be put in a position where medical aid is essential and there’s no one there to provide it. This class encompasses several aspects of emergency first aid: Stop the Bleed, First Aid, and CPR. Our TacMed class is AHA certified! once you complete this training you will receive your CPR Certification. This is a very thorough course, covering knife and gunshot wounds, wound packing, tourniquet use, chest seals, bandage application, and CPR implementation. This class is open to all age groups! rifle build class *Kit Dependent ($500-$1500+) Ever wanted to have that custom AR-15 to play with but didn’t know how to make it happen? In this class, builders will select their wants formalist of components. Once those components are ordered and delivered, builders than come in and build their very own rifle, to their specifications, with their own hands under the tutelage of our armorers. You leave the class with your very own, one of a kind, custom hand-built rifle! And normally for less cost then if you were to buy one off the shelf! RIFLE development (Level I, II, III) ($125-$250) Whether it be the first time shooter or the top level 3-gun competitor, we all want to become more proficient with our long guns. Our Carbine courses are designed for the shooter to become more comfortable and seamless in their rifle controls manipulation. Our carbine courses focus on clean manipulation and mechanics to establish proper “muscle memory”

Incline Bike Park Project is dedicated to building a full spectrum riding experience that will unite the world-class recreational riding experiences around Lake Tahoe. Bike parks, or pump tracks are becoming increasingly popular. It is a park with a continuous loop of dirt berms and “rollers” (smooth dirt mounds) that you ride without pedaling. The origins are rooted from the hardpack BMX trails of the 1970/1980s. In the early 2000s, a group of Australian downhill racers designed and developed the first pump track. Please do not throw from out of bounds areas including any tennis courts, pickleball courts, ball fields or roadways. No Smoking or open fires of any kind! It’s the forest and fire danger is high. Enjoy the course. Course Rules, Map & Scorecard – Download 2-page PDF Map & Scorecard (PDF) Disc Golf Course Project History & Future Construction of a disc or frisbee golf course began late summer of 2011 after approval by the IVGID Board of Trustees. The Disc Golf Course construction was funded through private donations from community clubs, businesses and individuals. In July 2011, The North Lake Tahoe Lions Club donated $10,000 to partially fund the course. Remaining funding was raised through Incline-Tahoe Foundation , by individual business and family hole sponsorships. The Incline Tahoe Foundation is currently collecting funds to help with future improvements and upkeep of this facility. Visit the Disc Golf Course project page at InclineTahoe.org for more information or to make a donation. Recreation Center, Beach Picnic Areas, Parks and Fields The Recreation Center offers year-round facilities for birthday parties, group fitness room, indoor gymnasium, and indoor pool. Adjacent to the Recreation Center, the new Bocce Park is a great outdoor space that is available for parties and rentals. On the west end of town, Preston Park is another great location for a family gathering, work outing or your child’s birthday party. In addition, Village Green, Preston Field and Ridgeline Park offer wide open spaces for activities and have multi-use fields for your softball and baseball needs for tournaments, family reunions, or corporate events. For IVGID Picture Pass Holders (with beach access), Incline and Burnt Cedar beaches have picnic areas to reserve for your spring or summer event. No longer do you need to arrive hours before your event to secure a spot for your group. The designated beach sites include picnic tables offering you and your friends an area to picnic or grill and enjoy the beach. The volleyball courts and bocce area is also now available for group rentals. Each guest is still responsible for beach access fees. Reservations at all sites are taken on a first-come, first-served basis at the Parks & Recreation Counter. Please call (775) 832-1310 or stop by and see us for rates or more information. Payment is required with your application. (IVGID Picture Card holders are exempt from pre-booking fees.) Cancellation policy: Fill out the Golf Contact Form and select “Tee Time Cancellation” to cancel tee time reservations. Cancel at least 72 hours prior to your tee time to avoid cancelation fees. 50% of green fees will be charged for cancellations made between 72 – 48 hours of tee time. Within 48 hours of tee time, full green fees will be charged for all golfers in your party. Pre-booking fees, if applicable, are non-refundable for all cancelations. Single Players: Single players may only join an existing group. Please call the Golf Shop and we will do our best to pair you with other golfers. Check-In Procedures: Golf cart keys will be in the Golf Shop for all carts. Public Check-In Procedure: Each golfer responsible for their tee time or their group’s tee time will be required to check in with the Golf Shop and pick up a receipt for the Starter. A golfer who is not responsible for payment, or someone in their group, will only be able to check themselves in for golf. IVGID Check-In Procedure: All IVGID Picture Pass Holders within a group must check themselves in individually and show their IVGID Pass. You may not check in other IVGID Pass Holders. Verification of a valid IVGID Picture Pass will be the only way to receive the IVGID Pass rates. Rider / Non-Player Fee: Non-player riders are welcome, but they must pay a rider fee of $35 per person at the Championship Course, or $20 per person (18 holes) / $15 per person (9 holes) at the Mountain Course. The single cart fee is $35 (Championship Course) or $25 (Mountain Course) for golfers who want to ride solo (subject to availability). Passes Golf Events & Programs Local Clubs Transfer of Service In order to transfer service to a new owner we will need to receive notification at least two business days prior to close of escrow. Water and sewer services are not interrupted upon change of ownership. Service is not transferred until a Grant Deed has been received from the title company. The details below also provide other helpful information to ensure accuracy upon close of escrow. Buyers can contact our office to provide their contact information, but water and sewer utilities follow the property. Once we receive a copy of the Grant Deed after close of escrow we can transfer service. Processing change of ownership upon sale For single, multi-family and commercial properties (excluding HOA accounts or vacant land) For all changes of ownership due to sale we will require a minimum of 2 working days notice, prior to the close of escrow, to schedule a final read on the water meter. Please call our office to notify us of the estimated close of escrow date and a request for final meter read. By the morning of the close of escrow date we will provide you with the current balance on the account and the consumption charges due from the final meter read. IVGID does not prorate balances on accounts so the final read breakdown will include the base rate charges for the account (which are billed in advance). If a final meter read is not requested the new owner will be liable for the past consumption charges on the account. Other helpful information to ensure accuracy upon close of escrow If the leak notification is set at the time of collecting a final meter read IVGID will advise escrow so all parties can be informed. This is a courtesy notification and IVGID will not require a leak be fixed. When a demand is submitted for completion, we will complete the information requested or indicate if the property is located within an HOA which pays the water/sewer charges or is vacant land. We will also send the demand to the IVGID Recreation department for them to indicate if there are passes which need to be returned upon sale. Our billing cycle is the 19th to the 18th of each month. Our base rates are billed on the 19th of the month in advance for this time period. Consumption charges are billed in arrears based on water and sewer use at the property. IVGID does not prorate charges and water and sewer services and charges are continuous through change of ownership. If the customer has Auto Payment set for their account, we will cancel auto payment once a final read is completed. If duplicate payment is made after the close of escrow date, we will deposit the title company check and issue a refund check to the seller. Upon close of escrow we need to receive a copy of the Deed (excluding properties in an HOA), even if there is not a check being submitted, as well as a contact phone number(s) for the customer. A separate demand for refuse charges must be sent to Waste Management by email: dpayoffs@wm.com. Refuse rates are billed quarterly in advance on October 1, January 1, April 1, and July 1. Caution needed with the presence of many users: pedestrians, baby strollers, joggers, pets on leashes, river rafters, and fisherman. Trailhead: Starting your ride at the parking area, next to the Transit Center, cross the bike/ped bridge to connect to the bike path and turn left. GPS: 39.164629, -120.147293 (Tahoe City Transit Center) GPS: 39.204733, -120.199446 (Squaw Valley entrance) The Bike Ride: Historic Truckee River Bike Path: This is a great ride for the entire family – its level, relaxing and beautiful. You cruise alongside the Truckee River to the entrance of Squaw Valley. Along the way are several places to turn out to absorb the natural beauty of the river’s eco-system. During the summer months, the river is most popular for rafting and you can literally see hundreds of people enjoying a fun-filled flow down to River Ranch Resort – where they exit and is a great local spot for food, refreshments, and entertainment Preview Ride: Historical: You are riding along the original Tahoe-Truckee Toll Road built in 1860 to enable horse-drawn freight and passenger wagons to travel between the Lake and Truckee. The river was used to float logs downstream to the mills in Truckee, and during the winter months the frozen river became a natural supplier of much needed ice for the mining operations in Virginia City. Later in the 1880’s, this route became the corridor for a narrow gauge railroad hauling logs to the Truckee mills, and then in the early 1900’s automobiles traveled on what was then called the Truckee Turnpike. This was an important transportation route for commerce, freight, and tourists traveling from Tahoe to Truckee and beyond to Sacramento, San Francisco, and Reno. pages.text: Sailing Lessons, Racing, Private Group Charters and Bareboat Rentals on North Lake Tahoe | 1 Bristlecone st. Tahoe City CA 96145 top of page Lake Tahoe Sailing Home Charters Courses Laser Clinics Racing Book Online Regattas Privacy Policy Employment Contact Us Lake Conditions Blog More Use tab to navigate through the menu items. Log In Lake Tahoe Sailing Sailing is for everyone! We offer a variety of experiences from a mellow afternoon or evening charter to full on, adrenaline charged racing. We have experiences that are tailored to you. Anyone from age 5 and up can learn to sail in a safe controlled environment. WE MAKE SAILORS! Learn More Home: Welcome Home: Courses Sailing Charters on Lake Tahoe Hands on learn to sail or sit back and relax! If you want a fun sailing experience with your friends and family on Lake Tahoe you can charter our 33 foot monohull the "Aero" and create a memory you'll never forget. Take the helm and learn to sail or sit back and relax and take in the splendor of Lake Tahoe under sail. Our experienced skippers are in control. We offer 3 hour sailing experiences accommodating up to 6 with a minimum age of 5. Cost is $600 for a three hour experience. Sailing times are 2-5PM and 5:30 to 8:30PM daily. We provide the lifejackets you provide the smiles! Sailing is For Everyone We have a variety of Experiences from Mellow to Wet and Wild For new sailors and families sailing for the first time we recommend our most mellow experience which is a private group charter on our Hobie 33 pictured above top. If you want to solidify the basics and become proficient, sign up for our week long family or adult course on our Melges 24 Raceboat where we'll take you racing on Wednesday night! Once you have the basics you are ready to try Laser Sailing/Racing for Youth and Adults. The Laser is physical, very fast and tippy! This is where saling gets really exciting! Bring your wetsuit because you'll be swimming! ​ Call us at 530-412-1101 or email at william.n.pullen@gmail.com We Make Sailors! Lake Tahoe Sailing News Stay in the Loop Instructor Spotlight - Nick Pullen Introduced to sailing by his Grandfather at the age of 5, Nick went on to become a member of Canada's National Sailing Team in the Laser Class. For decades he's travelled world wide racing Lasers and Melges 24s. He's a former Canadian National Champion, competed in 12 world championships, and has logged over 4 thousand miles of blue water ocean sailing. Nick has coached with International Sailing Academy in Puerta Vallarta drawing from their methodologies. He's also a Licensed Coast Guard Captain and US Sailing Level 1 Instructor. Contact Instructor Spotlight - Tasha Hacker Tasha Hacker is a USCG certified Captain and US Sailing certified basic keelboat instructor. Before moving to Lake Tahoe, she spent 5 years sailing around the world on her own boat. She also competed on the winning boat, Henri Lloyd, in the 2013-14 Clipper Round the World Yacht Race. Prior to the pandemic, Tasha was teaching women to sail a 41-foot racing yacht in the Bahamas and the Caribbean on week-long journeys. Tasha now enjoys teaching day sailors of all levels on beautiful Lake Tahoe. Contact Join our Laser Race Team! We're looking for both boys and girls age 12-21 who LOVE sailing and sailboat racing. This is a high performance race team training 4 weeks in the summer with Nick Pullen and traveling to regattas and training events throughout the year on the west coast. ​ Joining the team is a big commitment and is for kids who really love the sport and want to become champions. The good news is that the boats are provided and there is funding for travel and coaching. ​ The investment required to participate is similar to downhill ski racing. Athletes are required to obtain sailing specific clothing for protection from the elements and pay for 4 weeks of coaching. ​ ​ Learn More Home: About Home: News & Updates Get in Touch 2500 Lake Forest Blvd, Tahoe City CA 96145 william.n.pullen@gmail.com (530) 412-1101 Home: Contact Mindset of a Champion Join our High Performance Race Team The Best Way to Introduce Sailing for Kids Home: Blog Feed Book Now Questions? Most own a hardshell freestanding spa from many brands such as HotSprings, Cal Spa, SunDance, Bullfrog and more. Our 3-step process allows you to detox (flush out) the old chemicals and build up (bio-film) using your existing water. See our start up page for full instructions.
