Most soft tub customers use spa perfect once a month which helps the body oils break down that tend to collect on the liner. ahhNatural will not hurt the fabric and works great in the medium and large sizes. The smaller one will require support products. Smaller soft tubs are harder to maintain because the volume of water to body contaminates is super high. If you own the small size, please be aware that ahh will work but maintenace will be more than the medium and large size. PRO TIP: It's imperative that you keep your filters clean and use your jets often to aid in filtering out the body organics. Get in the habit of letting the jets run when you exit the tub and wiping the sides free of body oils regularly. Use Spa Perfect two times a month to help. The nature of the fabric collects oils and organics the slippery feel is part of owning a soft tub. Avoid lotions, potions and detergents from entering the tub. PRO TIP: If your tub is new, wait to install ahhNatural until the tannins have settled down. The tubs are dried but sit in dark hot warehouses and transport trucks that create an opportunity for pesky things to bloom. Meet Debbie Owner of CHAOS Estate Boutique Out of life's chaos come the stories, memories, and treasures that make a house feel like home. For more than thirteen years, I've had the privilege of helping families throughout Reno and Northern Nevada navigate life's transitions. Through my estate sale and organizing work, I've met incredible people and discovered thousands of fascinating items each with its own history and story. ​ Along the way, I kept thinking about how wonderful it would be to create a space where those treasures could live on and be appreciated by someone new. That idea eventually became CHAOS Estate Boutique. Today, our store offers nearly 5,000 square feet of carefully selected items a blend of vintage pieces, antiques, home d cor, collectibles, artwork, furniture, jewelry, books, rugs, and so much more. You'll also find hobby items, trains, sporting goods, electronics, kitchen pieces, costumes, and everyday items that still have plenty of life left in them. Some pieces arrive through estate sales we manage across Reno and Northern Nevada, while others come from trusted consignors who want their special items to find the right home. We also occasionally bring in new items and unique overstock finds to keep the store fresh and exciting. What makes CHAOS special is that nothing stays the same for long. Every week, new treasures arrive, displays change, and customers discover something unexpected. It's the kind of place where you can wander through the store and suddenly find the perfect gift, a beautiful piece of vintage d cor, or something you didn't even know you were looking for. My hope is that CHAOS Estate Boutique becomes a place people love to visit whether they're hunting for antiques, searching for collectibles, decorating their home, or simply enjoying the thrill of discovering something unique. If you enjoy the charm of vintage finds, estate treasures, and one-of-a-kind pieces, I invite you to come explore with us. pages.text: Ski-in Ski-out Tahoe Condo Search this site Embedded Files Skip to main content Skip to navigation Ski-in Ski-out Tahoe Condo All You Need To Know About Tahoe Ski Lease Finding The Right Toaster For Your Lake Tahoe Home Best Lake Tahoe Beaches Contact Us Ski-In Ski-Out Condo @Heavenly Tahoe Lake Tahoe Photography Things To Do In South Lake Tahoe Ski-in Ski-out Tahoe Condo Tahoe Ski Lease Ski Lease in South Lake Tahoe Skiing is a beloved winter activity for many people, and South Lake Tahoe is one of the best places in the world to hit the slopes. With its stunning natural beauty, numerous ski resorts, and world-class amenities, South Lake Tahoe has become a favorite destination for skiers and snowboarders from around the world. For those who love to ski but don't want to deal with the hassle and expense of owning a ski property, a ski lease in South Lake Tahoe may be the perfect solution. What is a Ski Lease? A ski lease is a rental agreement for a ski property that typically lasts for the duration of the ski season, which is usually from November through April. Unlike a traditional rental agreement, a ski lease is specifically designed for skiers and snowboarders who want to have a place to stay near the ski resorts during the winter months. Ski leases can range from a small studio apartment to a large, luxurious cabin, depending on your needs and budget. Benefits of a Ski Lease in South Lake Tahoe There are many benefits to leasing a ski property in South Lake Tahoe, including: Convenient access to the ski resorts: By leasing a property near the ski resorts, you'll be able to easily access the slopes without having to deal with the hassle of driving or parking. Many ski leases offer shuttle service to the resorts, so you can focus on enjoying your time on the mountain. Cost-effective: Skiing can be an expensive hobby, especially if you own a ski property. By leasing a property, you can save money on the upfront costs of buying a property, as well as the ongoing expenses of maintenance, property taxes, and utilities. Flexible: A ski lease allows you to enjoy the ski season without the commitment of owning a property year-round. You can choose the length of your lease, and if you decide you want to ski somewhere else next season, you're not tied to a specific property. Comfortable and convenient: Ski leases are often fully furnished and equipped with all the amenities you need to enjoy your time in South Lake Tahoe. Many leases include things like hot tubs, fireplaces, and fully equipped kitchens, so you can relax and enjoy your time off the slopes. Community: Ski leases often come with a built-in community of like-minded skiers and snowboarders. This can be a great way to meet new people and enjoy the social aspect of skiing. Choosing a Ski Lease in South Lake Tahoe When choosing a ski lease in South Lake Tahoe, there are a few things to keep in mind: Location: The location of your ski lease is important. You want to be close enough to the ski resorts to make it convenient, but not so close that you're dealing with crowds and noise. Look for a property that is in a quiet, peaceful location, but still within easy reach of the slopes. Amenities: Look for a ski lease that offers the amenities you need to enjoy your time off the slopes. This could include things like a hot tub, fireplace, fully equipped kitchen, and laundry facilities. Size: Consider the size of the property and the number of people in your group. You want to make sure that everyone has enough space to be comfortable. Price: Ski leases can vary widely in price, so it's important to find a property that fits your budget. Keep in mind that you'll also need to budget for things like lift tickets, equipment rentals, and food and drink. Availability: Ski leases can fill up quickly, so it's important to start your search early and be flexible with your dates. If you have specific dates in mind, be sure to book early to ensure availability. South Lake Tahoe is home to some of the best ski resorts in the world, including Heavenly Ski Resort, Kirkwood Mountain Resort, and Sierra-at-Tahoe Resort. Each resort offers a unique skiing experience, with a variety of terrain for all skill levels. Heavenly Ski Resort is the largest resort in South Lake Tahoe, with over 4,800 skiable acres and 97 runs. The resort boasts stunning views of Lake Tahoe and the surrounding mountains, and offers a variety of terrain for skiers and snowboarders of all levels. The resort also offers a variety of other activities, including zip lining, ice skating, and snowshoeing. Kirkwood Mountain Resort is known for its challenging terrain, with over 2,300 skiable acres and 86 runs. The resort is located at a higher elevation than the other resorts in South Lake Tahoe, which means it often has more snow and better conditions. Kirkwood also offers backcountry skiing and snowboarding, making it a popular destination for experienced skiers. Sierra-at-Tahoe Resort is a smaller resort with over 2,000 skiable acres and 46 runs. The resort is known for its family-friendly atmosphere and excellent beginner and intermediate terrain. Sierra-at-Tahoe also offers terrain parks and a halfpipe for freestyle skiers and snowboarders. No matter which resort you choose, a ski lease in South Lake Tahoe is the perfect way to enjoy all the skiing and snowboarding the area has to offer. With its stunning natural beauty, world-class amenities, and excellent skiing, South Lake Tahoe is a must-visit destination for any winter sports enthusiast. Conclusion A ski lease in South Lake Tahoe is a convenient, cost-effective, and comfortable way to enjoy all the skiing and snowboarding the area has to offer. With its stunning natural beauty, world-class amenities, and excellent skiing, South Lake Tahoe is the perfect destination for winter sports enthusiasts. Whether you're looking for a challenging ski experience or a family-friendly atmosphere, there's a ski resort in South Lake Tahoe that's perfect for you. So why wait? pages.text: Home - surfnfoiltahoe Home About Boat Experience Book What’s New Waiver Exclusive Wake Surf Charters & Expert Coaching with Olympian Andy Finch Begin Booking Meet Your Captain, Andy Finch Hi, I’m Andy Finch, and I’m stoked inviting you to wake surf Tahoe with me. As a former Olympian and professional athlete, I’ve spent a lifetime on the water, and nothing makes me happier than seeing how much joy wake surfing can bring. Whether you’re just starting out or you’re a seasoned rider, I love helping people push their limits and find their confidence on the water. Watching those smiles stretch as you ride the wave—that’s what it’s all about. Private Coaching and World-Class Wake Surf Boat My boat is equipped with an adjustable wave system that’s perfect for wake surfing or foiling on Tahoe. We can tailor the waves to fit your skill level. Whether you’re a total beginner or a pro looking to take your skills to the next level, my goal is to make sure you’re comfortable, confident, and—most importantly—having fun, no matter your age or experience. (530) 532-2435 It's about more than wake surf or foil You’ll be wake surfing while surrounded by the stunning beauty of Tahoe National Forest. There’s something truly special about this place. As you ride the wave, you can soak in the fresh mountain air, enjoy the serene views, and really connect with nature. It’s so epic. Bring The Family So, whether you’re young or old, a beginner or an expert, come out with me on the water and let’s make some unforgettable memories. I’m here to guide you, challenge you, and make sure you leave with a huge smile on your face. I can’t wait to share the joy of wake surfing with you! BOOK NOW TAP TO BEGIN BOOKING About Your Wake Surf N Foil Experience Join me, Captain Andy Finch, I’ll personally guide you through an unforgettable day of wake surfing or foiling in Tahoe. No need to worry about gear—I’ve got everything ready for you. Whether you’re a total beginner or a seasoned pro, I’ll tailor the experience to your skill level and make sure you feel comfortable. The best part? It’s completely family-friendly, so bring the whole crew! With the stunning Tahoe National Forest as your backdrop and a boat equipped with adjustable waves, you’re in for a thrilling and safe adventure. All you need to bring is your enthusiasm—I’ll take care of the rest! LEARN MORE Private Wake Surf N Foil Charters and Coaching BOOK NOW People Are Talking About Wake Surf N Foil Tahoe Surf coaching lessons from a pro like Andy is a game changer! I thought I knew how to wake surf, but then I got coaching and I went from liking it, to LOVING surfing! Our family has received several coaching sessions from Andy / Surf n’ Foil Tahoe, and every time our expectations are exceeded! Coaching for wake surfing and foiling is top-notch, catering to all ages and skill levels. Andy is extremely knowledgeable, patient and encouraging, building my kids’ confidence in surfing and helping me get up on the foil-board for the first time despite many falls! Their state-of-the-art equipment is perfect for both beginners and advanced riders. The surf wave on the new Montana boat is phenomenal! Awesome boat! If you want to learn or improve your wake surfing or foiling skills, Surf n’ Foil Tahoe is the place to go. I can’t recommend them enough! Five stars all the way! 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 We will definitely be back for more surfing experiences with Andy and crew. Shara Mock Local Guide Wow!! Such a fun time!! Captain Andy and his crew were the best! Kept us warm with plenty of extra dry life vests and wetsuits and showed us some great spots to avoid the wind that picked up mid day. His new surf boat is beautiful, very spacious & comfortable and creates amazing wakes to surf! His instruction for surfing is the best, even has waterproof hats with microphones to hear his tips and pointers as your on the wave, it was awesome and simply the best. Money well spent! We’ll book Surf n’ Foil again without question. Chad & Liza Hughes As an adaptive wheelchair athlete, it is a challenge to find coaches who know how to adapt with me. Andy has coached me in surfing in ways that have influenced my other sports performance. He teaches athletic principals that can be applied to numerous areas of life, not even just sports. He is an incredible athlete himself, as well as an unparalleled coach and I am so thankful I’ve gotten to receive surf training from this empowering, kind-hearted dude! His family is adorable too. Taylor F Adaptive Athlete MEET THE MONTARA SURF BOSS 2.0 Voted Boat of the Year! —the official boat of the Surf n’ Foil Tahoe experience! Unpredictable mountain weather patterns can change rapidly, turning a calm outing on the lake into a rough day on the sea. High winds and eight-foot waves are not uncommon on Lake Tahoe. “I don’t think people realize how dangerous this lake can get in a few minutes,” says Petty Officer 2nd Class Kauakea Colon. It’s dangerous. You just don’t know what lies beneath the surface. Depending on the weather, it can kill you.” Stretching 22 miles long and 12 miles wide, the crew has a lot of water to cover. The station responds to about 150 search and rescue cases each summer. “We’re non-stop when the busy season gets here. Memorial Day through Labor Day, you don’t sit down at all,” says Petty Officer 2nd Class Megan Archer. “We’re up from sunrise until midnight, then we go to bed to get our eight hours of rest and we’re up the next day doing the same exact thing again.” Don’t risk having your rental cut short and a US Coast Guard fine for overcrowding, swamping/sinking/drowning. (7+) US Coast Guard Regulation (US federal law ) : “GREAT DAY ON THE LAKE! Awesome day on the lake! Captain Scott was great. Everyone had a great time. We had a large group of 17 people and everyone felt that they go their turn (six participants at a time). I would highly recommend this – it’s like having a friend with a boat and toys. We didn’t need to worry about anything other than having fun .” – Vicki G US Coast Guard Lake Tahoe: The crystal blue waters can lure water-goers into a false sense of security. Unpredictable mountain weather patterns can change rapidly, turning a calm outing on the lake into a rough day on the sea. High winds and eight-foot waves are not uncommon on Lake Tahoe. “I don’t think people realize how dangerous this lake can get in a few minutes,” says Petty Officer 2nd Class Kauakea Colon. It’s dangerous. You just don’t know what lies beneath the surface. Depending on the weather, it can kill you.” Stretching 22 miles long and 12 miles wide, the crew has a lot of water to cover. The station responds to about 150 search and rescue cases each summer. “We’re non-stop when the busy season gets here. Memorial Day through Labor Day, you don’t sit down at all,” says Petty Officer 2nd Class Megan Archer. “We’re up from sunrise until midnight, then we go to bed to get our eight hours of rest and we’re up the next day doing the same exact thing again.” Don’t risk having your rental cut short and a US Coast Guard fine for overcrowding, swamping/sinking/drowning. Keep Tahoe Safe, choose a responsible boat company who obeys the law. Babes on a Boat keeps you safer . All boat rental companies on Lake Tahoe must operate in compliance with US Coast Guard regulations (US federal law) On Lake Tahoe and other Federal Waterways the US Coast Guard regulation requires commercial vessels less than 100 gross tons limit capacity to 6 passengers not including captain/crew: link Lake Tahoe boating conditions are similar to the ocean: deep, rough and windy; not like your typical low altitude lake back home and can get dangerous, very quickly. Pontoon boats are a less than optimal rental in these conditions, choose wisely. That’s why the US Coast Guard is stationed on Lake Tahoe! LEARN MORE: 8SEP19 OVERCROWDED RENTAL BOATER DEATH (NOT Babes on a Boat) Most of our Clients have more than 6 participants in their Group: “We booked Captain Scott for a full day and it was an absolute blast! Our group went wakeboarding, tubing & skiing in the morning followed by hitting some party spots in the afternoon. Captain Scott was super knowledgeable about the lake and any questions we had. Having an “all inclusive” experience with a driver, gas & watersports included was absolutely the way to go!! We had such a blast that we ended up booking a half day with him the next day! You will love TahoeJetBoats and Captain Scott!” – Jordan S We’ll operate legally from a pristine, sheltered, warm water beach rotating 6 participants at a time Our No Propeller 24 foot Yamaha Boats require just 18 inches enabling us to pick up and drop off on the beach faster than at a dock or pier! Big Groups love enjoying our Paddleboards and Lily Pad Floating Island at one of Tahoe’s most beautiful warm water beaches , it’s amazing! Opt for our Big Cooler, Paddleboards and Lily Pad Floating Island our Tahoe beach is world class! TIP : If your group is larger than 10 participants plan for a full day rental so everyone get’s plenty of time for watersports FYI: Drive it yourself boat rentals on Tahoe are base model old motorboats most often seen being towed back to shore. They’re also more expensive than the top of the line Babes on a Boat fleet . ✔ Your safety is our priority: Crowding a boat to the manufacturer’s passenger capacity to “fit my entire group,” is not safe or legal The Tahoe wind arrives almost every day around 2pm creating waves which can swamp, disable and sink over-crowded boats Please read our Lake Tahoe Boaters Weather Safety Briefing Please read our Best Location for a Lake Tahoe Boat Rental How Babes on a Boat Keeps You Safer All water sports participants must pass a deep water swim test. Non swimmers will not be permitted to participate in boat watersports, paddleboarding or aqua-lily floating island. They are welcome on the boat but must wear a PFD the entire time. Intentionally jumping off the waketube while being towed on Lake Tahoe may result in the jumper getting a $5000 fine from the USCG Sector San Francisco (Lake Tahoe) for ‘interfering with the safe operation of a vessel.’ Learn more: 1 , 2 , 3 Never jump off the waketube while underway . Overcrowding: Reduces the vessel’s handling and safety characteristics in Lake Tahoe’s big wind and large waves Reduces the vessel’s performance Reduces comfort for passengers Lake Tahoe Presents Ocean Like Conditions at 6253 Feet Above Sea Level: Less than optimal for inexperienced drive your own boat renters Wind and waves build extremely fast at our elevation presenting overcrowded boats with extreme challenges If you don’t have rough water high wind boating experience, leave the driving to Tahoe Jet Boats Tahoe Wave Conditions typically build from the SW - NE. Monoski – DynAccess Ltd. Skip to content Products Monoski Custom Projects Parts and Options Bindings and Binding Blocking Sets Shock Absorber Seat System Other Options Support Quote and Order Demo and Tuning Services Resources Manual How-to Videos Funding FAQs Contact Products Monoski Custom Projects Parts and Options Bindings and Binding Blocking Sets Shock Absorber Seat System Other Options Support Quote and Order Demo and Tuning Services Resources Manual How-to Videos Funding FAQs Contact Contact Products Our Monoskis Hydra The Hydra is our most popular model — a high-performance monoski with unique suspension kinematics that performs exceptionally well for racers and intermediate to advanced recreational skiers. The Hydra automatically moves the body of the monoskier as able-bodied skiers do in a turn: it applies pressure near the ski tip during turn initiation to begin bending the ski, then moves the skier backward on the ski to center the pressure at the apex of the turn, and finally shifts slightly to the back to straighten the ski and accelerate out of the turn. This movement helps users – especially those with limited upper body mobility – shift weight and turn more easily. To our knowledge, the Hydra is the only monoski on the market with this kind of suspension system, and better pressure distribution also leads to better control. The Hydra retains the competitive advantages of all DynAccess monoskis: extremely responsive and strong, with an exceptionally stiff frame, made from high-grade materials yet relatively lightweight. This is achieved through a unique structural geometry, custom-developed high-quality bearings and hardware, and a Penske Racing shock absorber specifically designed for DynAccess. The Hydra sits stably on lift chairs — it sits further back on the seat and tilts the rider slightly backward. Standard finish: clear hard anodized; custom colors available upon request. Request A Quote Parts & Options Hydra Light The Hydra Light is a lighter version of the Hydra monoski, specially developed for lighter skiers. It is a completely redesigned monoski, and almost every part is lighter than on the regular Hydra. The complete frame with shock, etc. (without a seat or a footrest) weighs 15.4 lbs. (7.0 kg) and 18.2 lbs. (8.2 kg) with a footrest. This is 6.5 lbs. (3 kg) lighter than the regular Hydra. A new lightweight shock with a single spring was developed for the Hydra Light, based on a mountain bike shock but modified for DynAccess monoskis. It features a custom-made ice scraper, cold temperature oil, and modified damping by Penske Racing Shocks, with both high & low speed rebound and compression damping adjusters. If desired, a full-size Hydra shock can be installed in the Hydra Light frame. The Hydra Light works best for skiers under 135 lbs, and the frames are anodized in Red or Light Blue as standard. Request A Quote Parts & Options Tensor The Tensor is a high-performance and highly versatile monoski. It accepts different types of shocks — including air shocks, coil-over shocks, and light-duty shocks — allowing you to customize your ride and ride height. Standard setup includes the Penske Racing Shocks Pro-Air: dual-chamber air spring (Chambers 1 & 2), hydraulic damping, and easy adjustability of spring rate, ride height, rebound, and compression damping (no tools needed). Weight (w/o seat): 23.25 lbs. Benefits: high stiffness for excellent control, stable lift-chair positioning by sitting further back and tilting the rider slightly backward, and suitability for racing, recreation, and adaptive programs alike. Request A Quote Parts & Options Legacy Models Legacy Model Torque 2 Our strongest model to date. The Torque 2 uses thin-walled, closed-section chromoly members for its frame, suspension link, and “boot” tower — making it extremely stiff and durable. This stiffness translates to superior rider control and a crisper feel on the slopes. Parts & Options Legacy Model Torque 1 The Torque 1 is the original DynAccess monoski. It’s compact and lightweight, weighing: 23 lbs without a seat 20.5 lbs without a footrest The Torque 1 features a steep thigh angle (40°), which reduces the moment of inertia and helps the skier initiate quick, responsive turns. Multi-Day, All-Inclusive Trips on the Wild & Scenic Rogue River Nestled in the picturesque landscape of Southern Oregon, the Rogue River is one of the most popular destinations for drift boat fishing. Drift boats provide anglers with the perfect way to access remote and offers an unparalleled fly fishing experience for enthusiasts seeking the thrill of catching adult and Half Pounder Steelhead. These steelhead, known for their feisty nature and acrobatic displays, provide an exciting challenge for anglers of all levels. We offer 4 day, 3 night all-inclusive fishing and rafting trips down the wild and scenic section of the Rogue River. Learn More Take a Trip With Us It’s hard to cram 4 days and 3 nights of adventure into one video — but we managed to condense it to about 17 minutes of footage to give you an idea! Give it a listen if when you have the time. 4-Day, 3-Night Drift Boat Adventure Prepare for a one-of-a-kind fishing experience on the majestic Rogue River. Our trips are all-inclusive of lodging and meals and our expert guides will ensure a thrilling and memorable trip. Overnight Lodging at Historic Wilderness Lodges Evenings and nights are spent in historic Rogue River wilderness lodges. These lodges are all boat-in only and feature all the comforts of home with showers and a place to gather around in the main lodge. Riverside & Lodge Meals Each morning, and every night breakfast and dinner are hosted at the wilderness lodges. Riverside lunches on the Rogue are a memorable experience, featuring fresh steelhead and a deli spread. What’s Included in Your Trip Fly Fishing: A Nature Lover's Dream Adventure! Imagine casting your line into the pristine waters of the Rogue River, surrounded by breathtaking scenery that changes with every bend. Towering Douglas firs and rugged cliffs create a stunning backdrop as you wait for that telltale tug on your rod. The air is filled with the sounds of nature: the gentle rush of the river, the melody of birdsong, and perhaps the distant call of a deer hidden in the thickets. Go with the Flow “ One of the best trips we have been on! Scenic ride down the river with plenty of wildlife to see. We had excellent meals every day and the guides were helpful, fun & informative. We had a blast! ” Dan & Jill Ripple, Reno NV Read More reviews from our clients Location Rogue River, Oregon Hours Always Open - Book Now! Fishing | Experience Rogue River Fishing Drift 0 Skip to Content Home Fishing Rafting Lodges Dates & Cost About Contact News from the River Book a Trip Open Menu Close Menu Home Fishing Rafting Lodges Dates & Cost About Contact News from the River Book a Trip Open Menu Close Menu Home Fishing Rafting Lodges Dates & Cost About Contact News from the River Book a Trip The mighty Rogue River flows 215 miles from its headwaters in Crater Lake National Park to the Pacific Ocean in Gold Beach. In 1968, an 84-mile stretch of the Rogue River was designated as a National Wild & Scenic River by the US Congress, which means that it is protected from development and other forms of disturbance that could degrade its natural and scenic qualities. This designation recognizes the river's exceptional values, including its outstanding scenery, wildlife habitat, and recreational opportunities. Our trips take you through 43 miles of the Wild & Scenic section of the river, stopping at 3 comfortable riverside wilderness lodges along the way. All trips include 3 hearty meals and all of the gear and instruction you need to catch those pesky half pounders! Where We Drift BOOK NOW From Our Clients "What a blast on the Rogue!" My family had an incredibly memorable week with Captain Tim and his awesome team of guides through the Rogue for four days. Tim went above and beyond to ensure we were safe, ensure we had fun fishing, jumping off rocks, ate well, always had beverages within arms length, and ensured we made memories that will last forever. Couldn’t recommend Drift any more! —Jack B., Carmel Valley, CA "Put This One on Your Bucket List!" I applaud the owner, Tim Conway, and his very experienced fishing and white water guides. The fabulous scenery of the Rogue River combined with the home cooked meals, real beds, hot showers every night and let’s not forget the fabulous fishing is something everyone should experience at least once. Let’s check that box on your bucket list!! —Al B., Reno, NV "Fantastic Trip Down the Wild & Scenic Rogue River!" Our trip with Drift Adventures down the Rogue River was absolutely fantastic from start to finish. The whole experience captured everything you hope for in an Oregon fishing adventure — stunning scenery, great fishing, and a top-notch outfitter and guides who made each day unforgettable. Can’t wait to go again! —Chris C., Creswell OR "I've never been so close to bears and bald eagles." Nothing beats a back to nature trip! Also, throw in some fantastic fishing with a great crew. The lodges that we stayed in were historic and very comfortable. The food was excellent. I especially enjoyed the lunches with fresh caught steelhead. This trip will rejuvenate your body and soul. Tim is an excellent guide and leader. —Ron R., Reno NV Your Adventure Awaits Big Fish Stories Embark on a thrilling journey as you take in the scenery, the wildlife, and the adrenaline of the experience. Make sure to save your “Big Fish” pictures and stories for the dinner table each night. Unforgettable Memories Create lasting memories and stories to share. Immerse yourself in the thrill of the Oregon wilderness. Along the way, you might spot a black bear, bald eagle, river otter or salmon and steelhead trout who make their home along this incredible river. BOOK NOW Expert Guides Benefit from the knowledge and expertise of our professional guides. Our guides are all trained to navigate the waters of the Rogue to make your trip enjoyable and safe. “ I fished with the Drift crew on the Rogue in September ‘24 and it was the trip of a lifetime. I’ve fished all over the world and none of those trips rivaled my Rogue experience. Tim and his crew were fantastic, getting us into great fishing, amazing scenery, wonderful food and a lot of fun. Trip Dates & Costs | Explore Rogue River Now Drift 0 Skip to Content Home Fishing Rafting Lodges Dates & Cost About Contact News from the River Book a Trip Open Menu Close Menu Home Fishing Rafting Lodges Dates & Cost About Contact News from the River Book a Trip Open Menu Close Menu Home Fishing Rafting Lodges Dates & Cost About Contact News from the River Book a Trip All-Inclusive Trips; 4 Days, 3 Nights Drift maintains a special use permit issued by the Bureau of Land Management. Trip start and end dates are the same every year. Trip Dates September 1-4, 6-9, 11-14, 16-19, 21-24, 26-29 October 1-4, 6-9, 11-14, 16-19, 21-24, 26-29 November Oct. 31- Nov. 3, 5-7, 10-12 Trip Costs $2650/person, 4 days $2375/person, 3 days late season Includes, all lodging, all meals, river fees, guides and equipment. Gratuities are not included but are appreciated for a job well done. Payments 50% of total trip cost is due at time of booking. Remaining 50% is due 60 days prior to trip start date. See below for cancellation policy. BOOK NOW FAQs Transportation If you’re flying in: The closest airport to our launch is Medford. You can also fly to Eugene (about 2.5 hour drive) or Portland (about a 4 hour drive). Driving to the river: If you have rented a car or have driven your own, we will give you directions to the launch and we will arrange for your car to be shuttled to the take out. Charges range from $135 for individual cars to $900 for a group of 12 to be driven in a shuttle van. If you have flown in as a group it is best to rent a van service to pick you up at the airport and be taken to your motel and then on to the river the following morning. They will then pick you up after the trip ends and transport you back to the airport. We can arrange this service for you. Where does the trip start and end? You will meet your guides at Graves Creek the morning of the first day of the trip. Directions to the launch will be given to you once the trip is booked. The launch is located about 20 miles off I-5. We generally reach our final destination on the fourth day about 11 am at the community of Agnes. If you are on a 3 day trip, we reach Foster Bar about 4pm. You are about 27 miles from Gold Beach, if you’re heading for the coast. If you’re traveling back to Interstate 5, you are about 2 hours to Grants Pass. Where should I stay the night before we launch? The trip wiIl begin at Graves Creek at 9 am, so it’s best to spend the night preceding your trip in Grants Pass. Here are some options for lodges near our launch: — Riverside Inn 1-800-334-4567 — Galice Resort 541-476-3818 — Morrison’s Rogue River Lodge 1-800-826-1963. What kind of gear do I need to bring? High quality rain gear including rain hat and warm coat A couple changes of clothes (casual or sport clothes are customary) Sneakers and waterproof boots in the event of rain (late fall) Small flashlight Sunscreen Sunglasses Camera & binoculars if you wish Shorts and Swimsuit (early fall) Hat for shade Long underwear, gloves and rubber pac boots (for late October-November) Day pack for items you want to keep close while on the river Beverage and mix if you wish Book to read at leisure Water Bottle Cell phones & internet Phones don’t work on this stretch of the river! We carry a satellite phone for emergencies. What is the cancellation policy? Due to the nature of our business with limited launch dates, trip size and commitments to lodges and guides - deposits are non-refundable. However, if we can refill your cancelled seats at full price, we will refund all fees received. If you must cancel, your deposit will be refunded only if the vacancies can be filled by you or us. If you cancel within 60 days of your start date, you will owe the entire balance. If we have to cancel, you will receive a full refund. Come rain, snow, or high water, we almost always run our trips. But if there are insufficient reservations, we reserve the right to alter the departure date or place, or to cancel a trip. There will be a full refund for any trip canceled by Drift Adventures, LLC. Our financial liability is limited to the amount paid to Drift and shall not cover any other costs incurred by trip members. We strongly urge that you buy trip insurance in the event you become ill or are hurt prior to your trip or in the event you must depart a trip in progress. Our guests in the past have used Travelex, Travel Guard and others. “Our October fly fishing trip down the Wild and Scenic Rogue was spectacular. The scenery was mind blowing; the wildlife did not disappoint; and the guides were professional and highly skilled in maneuvering the river (and they knew the best fishing spots!). If you are looking for an outfitter who offers a customized experience with attention to the details, Drift Adventures brings it all.” -Shannon Christopher, Brookings, Oregon Book A Trip Location Rogue River, Oregon Hours Always Open - Book Now! They are known for their beauty along with the gorgeous trout that come with them. Although appealing to the eye, many find these fisheries as being some of the most difficult to figure out. This is your opportunity to venture with a highly experienced guide that will make your trip to these rivers an all around success. Service Blake Hunter has the skills and techniques to trick finicky trout in all situations and gives clientele of every skill level the opportunity of catching the fish of a lifetime. Hunter will be there every step of the way; perfecting your cast, matching the hatch, and locating the fish for you. You will be using new age rigging techniques along with intricate home tied flies known to produce positive results. Don't find yourself flustered and alone on the river when you have a definite answer to your fly fishing needs with Blake Hunter's guide service. Private Water: Guided Fly Fishing Adventures to East Peak Lake Stay close to Stateline and get all the adventure! An epic trip for families and small groups on East Peak Lake at Heavenly Mountain Resort. Take the Scenic Gondola and an off-road trail ride in a UTV with your group up to private East Peak Lake . This 3-hour excursion includes an introduction to casting and guided fly fishing, the gondola ride, and an off-road trail ride. Learn More Off-Road Adventure Guided Fly Fishing Packages Jump in one of our 4-Seater UTV Off-Road side-by-sides and buckle up for a fly fishing experience like no other. We’ll take you to remote sections of water with fewer footprints and fish that don’t get to see a lot of flies. Our remote locations offer unparalleled beauty with outstanding fishing. Tahoe Fly Fishing Outfitters offers exclusive access to the picturesque Sawmill Lake located in North Lake Tahoe on the Northstar Resort. The 10-acre lake offers anglers of all abilities the shot at trophy rainbow or brown trout on the fly. Sight cast dry flies at cruising fish or strip streamers deep and enjoy the view! Learn More Guided Fly Fishing The Tahoe area offers an abundance of opportunity to chase trout and other species on the fly. Book your fly fishing adventure today! Rivers: Truckee River, Little Truckee, East Carson, West Carson, East Walker, West Walker, and more. Lakes: Sawmill Lake, Caples Lake, Red Lake, Blue Lakes, Silver Lake, Boca Reservoir, Stampede, and more. Premium products from Simms Fishing, Howler Brothers, Scott Fly Rods, Ross, Galvan, Fishpond, and more. Just getting started, or building an arsenal, our staff is here to help. We also offer a full complement of fly tying materials to customize your ‘secret weapon’ and add your own style to your bugs. Check out our online store for TFFO swag and gear! Shop Gear Classes and Clinics We offer courses for all anglers at every skill level designed to be engaging and make you a better angler. Group clinics bring people together around the love of fly fishing. TFFO creates a social atmosphere by partnering with local vendors and accommodations to deliver a fun and educational experience in small group settings. Upcoming Clinics A better fly fishing adventure with Tahoe Fly Fishing Outfitters Book a Trip Lake Tahoe’s #1 Guide Outfitter. Learn from the best. Alyssa Evart, GUIDE No river too far and with a quiver of tricks she has made a name for herself with a fly rod. Whether chasing backcountry goldens or Steelhead on the coast she is happy in the water. Taylor Norton, GUIDE Taylor grew up fishing Long Island Sound, He moved west and honed his skills on western trout running pack trips in the Rockies. His passion for teaching makes for a a memorable trip for his clients. Jason Shaw, GUIDE A true outdoorsman who spends a lot of time on the water and sure to create a memorable day for his guests on his home waters Chad Fuller, GUIDE Chad has carried a fly rod all over the western seaboard from baja to Alaska and hunts the flats for saltwater big game every chance he gets. Drew Johnston, GUIDE & GEAR GURU “Yo!” Drew is a good time on the water with strong knowledge of Tahoe’s surrounding steams and stillwaters. pages.text: Five Dot Fly Fishing Club | Round Valley Reservoir | Susanville, California top of page Five Dot Pheasant Club (530) 254-6987 HOME RATES GROUP RATES ACCOMMODATIONS MEMBERSHIP ABOUT CONTACT ACCESS LICENSE PHOTOS More Use tab to navigate through the menu items. 400-Acre Private Catch & Release Trout Fishery Located 17 Miles North of Susanville, CA Five Dot Fly Fishing Club | Premier Private Trout Fishery Five Dot Fly Fishing Club is situated on one of California's largest private stillwater fisheries; Round Valley Reservoir. This 400-acre reservoir is located in the upper elevations of Susanville California and is in an ultra secluded basin. Triploid Rainbow Trout are growing fast and strong in this fertile environment and can be commonly caught in the 2 to 5 pound range along with some larger fish. The reservoir is fed by natural springs, seasonal run-off and also from smaller lakes located in remote areas of the Five Dot Ranch. The Ranch is located only a few miles from Eagle Lake and is close enough to Susanville for anglers to have plenty of options for lodging and camping while fishing this remarkable fishery. A limited number of aluminum boats without motors are available. Fisherman are allowed to bring their own electric trolling motors and/or float tubes or personal pontoon boats. ​ The reservoir can accommodate groups of 2-15 people. Smaller groups may be combined with other groups of similar size. There are also some basic guidelines that need to be followed to exclude the rest of the public for your event or activity: All applications require a $5 administrative processing fee. Once an application is approved, the deposit must be paid within 10 working days to hold your date, and all fees must be paid 10 working days prior to your reservation. Comprehensive General Liability insurance naming Douglas County as additional insured will be required for any event when: The event is open to the public A fee is charged for the event The very nature of the event and/or the number of applicants require its application, and/or As determined by the Director of Community Services or his/her authorized designee. The minimum limits for the insurance shall be as follows: $1,000,000 for each occurrence $1,000,000 annual aggregate Insurance coverage must include premises and operations, and products and completed operations as a minimum. Further, if alcohol is to be sold, the insurance policy shall include Liquor Liability naming Douglas County as additional insured, with the same aforementioned requirements and minimum limits Depend

Home » Recreation & Parks » Facilities » Outdoor Rental Spaces » Tahoe Vista Scenic Overlook Tahoe Vista Scenic Overlook Alpen Lily 2026-06-15T10:22:54-07:00 Offering two-hour rental blocks with some of the best views anywhere on Lake Tahoe. ADA accessible, access limited to 40 people. TVRA Scenic Overlook Information Rental Fees User Type 2-Hour Rental Resident $600 Non-Resident/Non-Profit $1,200 Commercial $2,400 Resident : Property owner or tenant within North Tahoe PUD boundaries Non-Resident/Non-Profit : Person or non-profit business that resides outside of North Tahoe PUD Boundaries Commercial : Any business that cannot prove residency and has a business, be it a LLC, Sole Proprietorship, Cooperation, Small Business or Partnership. Facility Information Scenic Overlook is ADA accessible Rental is limited to 40 people Rental includes 40 chairs Time reserved is inclusive of setup and cleanup Scenic Overlook will be sectioned off for private use Rentals available Monday-Friday only in July and August Rentals available 7-days a week in May, June, September and October Rental Instructions Step 1: Login to MyRecAccount Step 2: Log in (upper left corner) or Create Account for first time users Step 3: Click on Facility Rental Tab Step 4: Click on Tahoe Vista Recreation Area and select Scenic Overlook Step 5: Select date under Make a Reservation If area is blocked out, rental is not available Step 6: Complete prompts Sign waiver Continue to payment FAQs Can I bring in additional rental items? Chairs are provided for you to setup with a Scenic Overlook rental. The only additional item that is allowed at a Scenic Overlook rental is an arch. No tables are allowed. Where can I have my reception? A nice idea is to also reserve the TVRA Plaza, which is suitable for a large event and additional rental items. Ceremony can occur at the Overlook, with the reception on the Plaza. Can I throw biodegradable items, such as rose petals or confetti, at the event? No. In protection of the wildlife and environment, there is no throwing or releasing of anything at events or weddings. What time can I arrive? The 2-hour Scenic Overlook rental is inclusive of your setup and cleanup time. That means that you should not plan to arrive several hours early to setup. You can arrive 30-45 minutes early to ensure chairs, arch and flowers are in proper location. Will I have exclusive access to the Overlook? The Scenic Overlook will be marked and sectioned off for private use during your 2-hour rental period. The remainder of Tahoe Vista Recreation Area will remain open and accessible to the public. NTPUD cannot guarantee exclusive use of space during rental. What months are rentals available? May-October Why can’t I book on Saturday or Sunday in July and August? We want all of our users to have an enjoyable experience. Due the popularity of TVRA during summer months and high volume of public use, we need to take each weekend request on a case-by-case basis. Please reach out to parks@ntpud.org for assistance. Can I reserve parking spaces? The Tahoe Vista Recreation Area has a dedicated parking lot and street parking is also available in specific areas. NTPUD will not reserve spaces for events, the lot is available on a first come, first serve basis. Wildlife? Lake Tahoe is black bear and raccoon habitat, please use caution. Make sure to clean up after yourself and your guests and deposit all trash into a bear-proof trash receptacle. Do not leave food unattended at any time. Do not approach wildlife. Can I grill or use charcoal? Charcoal grilling and grills are restricted within North Lake Tahoe and NTPUD parks (with the exception of the built-in grill at the Ramada), per North Tahoe Fire Protection District seasonal burn ban. The use of propane outdoor barbecues are also restricted on certain days, according to the fire restrictions at the time. Visit www.ntfire.net for up-to-date information and regulations related to regional and local burn bans. What about trash? NTPUD staff will collect trash, but renter is responsible for bagging trash and putting inside or next to trash receptacles. Do not overfill trash receptacles. Renter is responsible for bagging their own trash and replacing with bags if full. Renter may choose to bring additional trash cans for placement around rental space. How close to rental can I reserve? A 5 day minimum is required for rentals. What are insurance requirements? NTPUD requires general liability insurance with additional liquor liability coverage any time that alcohol is served. For outdoor events, general liability insurance is required for events over 100 people, any athletic event, and events deemed “high risk” per NTPUD. NTPUD will not reserve spaces for events, the lot is available on a first come, first serve basis. Wildlife? Lake Tahoe is black bear and raccoon habitat, please use caution. Make sure to clean up after yourself and your guests and deposit all trash into a bear-proof trash receptacle. Do not leave food unattended at any time. Do not approach wildlife. Can I grill or use charcoal? NTPUD staff will collect trash, but renter is responsible for bagging trash and putting inside or next to trash receptacles. Do not overfill trash receptacles. Renter is responsible for bagging their own trash and replacing with bags if full. There are several trash cans at the Ramada however renter may choose to bring in additional cans if they desire. How close to rental can I reserve? A 5 day minimum is required for rentals. What are insurance requirements? NTPUD requires general liability insurance with additional liquor liability coverage any time that alcohol is served. For outdoor events, general liability insurance is required for events over 100 people, any athletic event, and events deemed “high risk” per NTPUD. Unless a District-approved exemption applies, applicants shall provide and maintain general liability insurance with limits of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence, two million dollars ($2,000,000) general aggregate
